﴿فَأَنَّى﴾ the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (the fāʾ implying an unstated condition), and an interrogative noun in the position of the accusative (manṣūb) as ḥāl; ﴿يُؤْفَكُونَ﴾ a passive imperfect verb, and the wāw is nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent), and the clause is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of an implied condition, with no grammatical position; ﴿وَقِيلِهِ﴾ the wāw is a preposition and a particle of oath, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted verb of oath; ﴿يا رَبِّ﴾ يا is a vocative particle, and the one addressed (munādā), annexed to the dropped first-person yāʾ; ﴿إِنَّ هؤُلاءِ قَوْمٌ﴾ inna, its noun and its khabar, and the vocative clause is the object of the saying; ﴿لا﴾ negative; ﴿يُؤْمِنُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb in the nominative, and the wāw is its fāʿil, and the clause is an adjective (ṣifa) of قوم; ﴿عَنْهُمْ﴾ both attached to the verb «[Translator's note: the source passes over the word فَاصْفَحْ that precedes عنهم in the verse; it is evidently the verb meant here, and the next item refers to it as اصفح.]»; ﴿وَقُلْ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and an imperative verb whose fāʿil is latent; ﴿سَلامٌ﴾ the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, and the nominal clause is the object of the saying, and the verbal clause is conjoined to اصفح; ﴿فَسَوْفَ﴾ the fāʾ is a conjunction, and سوف is a particle of deferral (taswīf) and of the future; ﴿يَعْلَمُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb in the nominative, and the wāw is its fāʿil, and the clause is conjoined to what precedes it.

farraa:5-5.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿أَفَنَضْرِبُ عَنكُمُ ٱلذِّكْرَ صَفْحاً أَن كُنتُمْ﴾.
Al-Aʿmash read: "إن كنتم" with kasra, and ʿĀṣim and al-Ḥasan read: "أنْ كنتم" with fatḥa on (أنْ), as though they meant something past. In ordinary speech you say: "Shall I revile you أن you deprived me?", meaning "since (إذ) you deprived me"; and you use kasra when you mean: "Shall I revile you if (إن) you deprive me?" Like it is: ﴿ولاَ يَجْرِمَنّكُمْ شَنآنُ قَوْمٍ أَنْ صَدُّوكم﴾: you may read (إن) with kasra or with fatḥa.
And like it: ﴿فلعلَّك باخعٌ نفسك على آثارِهم﴾ "إن لم يؤمنوا" and "أن لم يؤمنوا". The Arabs recite the saying of al-Farazdaq:
أتجزع إن أذنا قتيبة حزتا * جهاراً، ولم تجزع لقتل ابن خازم؟
(Do you grieve if [or: that] the two ears of Qutayba were cut off openly, yet you did not grieve at the killing of Ibn Khāzim?)
And they recited to me:
أتجزع أن بان الخليط المودّع * وجبل الصفا من عزة المتقطع؟
(Do you grieve that the departing companions have parted, and the bond of affection with ʿAzza that is cut?)
And in each of the two verses there is what is in its companion: kasra and fatḥa. And the Arabs say: "I have turned away (أضربت) from you" and "I turned (ضربت) from you", when they mean by it: I left you and I turned aside from you.

farraa:13-13.t:
His saying: ﴿لِتَسْتَوُواْ عَلَىٰ ظُهُورِهِ﴾.
Someone may say: how did He say "على ظهوره" (on its backs), attaching "backs" to a singular? It is said to him: that singular is in the meaning of a plural, in the same way as "the troops", "the army" and "the whole body". If he says: then why did you not say "لتستووا على ظهره" (on its back), making "back" singular when you attach it to a singular? I say: the singular contains the meaning of the plural, so I returned "backs" to the meaning and did not say "its back", lest it be like the singular whose meaning and wording are both singular. Likewise you say: "The women of the troops (الجند) have become many", and you say: "The troops raised their eyes (أعينه)", and do not say "its eye (عينه)". And likewise everything you attach to such of the concrete nouns, you bring out in the plural; but when you attach to it a noun in the meaning of an action (fiʿl), both its plural and its singular are allowed, as in your saying: "The troops raised their voice (صوته)" and "their voices (أصواته)", which is better. This is allowed because the action has no form in the dual other than its form in the singular.
His saying: ﴿وَمَا كُنَّا لَهُ مُقْرِنِينَ﴾.
Capable of it (muṭīqīn). You say to a man: "You have become مُقرن for this", i.e. you are capable of it and have become a match (qirn) for it.

farraa:17-17.t:
His saying: ﴿ظَلَّ وَجْهُهُ مُسْوَدّاً﴾.
The verb belongs to the face, so for that reason you put the predicate (fiʿl) in the accusative; and had you made "ظلّ" belong to the man, you would put "the face" and "blackened" in the nominative, saying: ظل وجهه مسودٌّ وهو كظيم.

farraa:18-18.t:
His saying: ﴿أَوَمَن يُنَشَّأُ فِي ٱلْحِلْيَةِ﴾.
He means the females. He says: you have assigned daughters to the All-Merciful, while you are such that when a daughter is born to one of you, what He described befalls him. As for His saying ﴿أومَنْ﴾, it is as though He said: "and one who is not brought up except in ornaments, and who in dispute is not clear", i.e. does not attain in argument what a man attains. In the reading of ʿAbd Allāh: "أَوَمَنْ لا يُنَشَّأُ إلاّ فى الْحِلْيَةِ". If you wish [169/b], you put "مَن" in the position of the nominative by resumption (istiʾnāf); and if you wish, you put it in the accusative by an implied verb, "they make (يجعلون)" or the like; and if you refer it back to the beginning of the speech, to His saying: "وإِذَ بُشِّرَ أَحَدُهُمْ بِما ضَرَبَ", you put it in the genitive [and if you wish, in the accusative]. Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb, the companions of ʿAbd Allāh and al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī read: "يُنَشَّأُ", and ʿĀṣim and the people of the Ḥijāz read: ينْشَأُ فى الحلية.

farraa:19-19.t:
His saying: ﴿عِبَادُ ٱلرَّحْمَـٰنِ﴾.
ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd, ʿAlqama and the companions of ʿAbd Allāh read it: "عباد الرحمن"; and it is reported [of] ʿUmar (may Allah have mercy on him) that he read it: "عند الرحمن", and likewise ʿĀṣim and the people of the Ḥijāz, as though they took that from His saying: ﴿إنَّ الذين عِنْد رَبِّك لا يَسْتَكْبِرُون عَنْ عِبادَتهِ﴾. All is correct.
His saying: ﴿أَشَهِدُواْ خَلْقَهُمْ﴾.
ʿĀṣim and al-Aʿmash gave the alif of "أشهدوا" fatḥa, and the people of the Ḥijāz gave it ḍamma, in the interpretation: أُشْهدوا خلقهم ("were they made to witness their creation?"), because its agent is not named; and the meaning is the same. They read it without hamza, intending the question. Abū ʿAbd Allāh said: so al-Farrāʾ said.

farraa:22-23.t:
His saying: ﴿بَلْ قَالُوۤاْ إِنَّا وَجَدْنَآ آبَآءَنَا عَلَىٰ أُمَّةٍ﴾.
The readers read it with ḍamma on the alif of "أُمّة", and Mujāhid and ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz read it with kasra. It is as though al-imma is like sunna (custom) and milla (creed); and al-imma is the way (ṭarīqa), and the maṣdar (verbal noun) of "I led (amamtu) the people". The Arabs say: "How fine is his imma, his ʿimma and his jilsa!", when it is a maṣdar. Al-imma is also dominion and bliss. ʿAdī said:
ثم بعْدَ الفلاحِ والمُلكِ والإمّة * وارثهمُ هناك القبورُ
(Then, after prosperity, dominion and imma, the graves there have concealed them.)
As though he meant the leadership of dominion and its bliss.
«[Translator's note: «وارثهم» as printed is translated by its evident sense "concealed them" (cf. واراهم); the verse is cited elsewhere as «وارتهم».]»
His saying: ﴿وَإِنَّا عَلَىٰ آثَارِهِم مُّهْتَدُونَ﴾ and ﴿مُّقْتَدُونَ﴾.
They are nominative; had they been accusative, that would have been allowed, because stopping before them is good. So you say to a man: "You came while we were following the track (متبعين / متبعون)".

farraa:26-26.t:
His saying: ﴿إِنَّنِي بَرَآءٌ مِّمَّا تَعْبُدُونَ﴾.
The Arabs say: "We are barāʾ and khalāʾ of you" (quit of you); and for the singular, the dual and the plural, feminine and masculine, one says: barāʾ, because it is a maṣdar (verbal noun). Had He said (برىء), one would say in the dual: بريئان, and of a group: بريئون and برءاء. In the reading of ʿAbd Allāh it is: "إنَّنى بَرِئٌ مِّمَّا تَعْبُدُون"; and had a reader read it so, it would be correct and in agreement with our reading [i.e. our codex], because the Arabs write يستهزىء as يستهزأ, writing the hamza with alif in all its states. They write شىء as شيأ, and the like is frequent in the codices of ʿAbd Allāh; and in our codex: ويهيىء لكم is written ويهيأ, with alif.

farraa:28-28.t:
His saying: ﴿وَجَعَلَهَا كَلِمَةً بَاقِيَةً فِي عَقِبِهِ﴾.
[It is] the name of Islam. He says: binding on whoever followed him and was of his offspring; perhaps the people of Mecca will follow this religion, since they are of the offspring of Abraham, Allah bless him. That is His saying: ﴿لَعَلَّهُمْ يَرْجِعُونَ﴾: to your religion and the religion of Abraham, Allah bless them both.

farraa:31-31.t:
His saying: ﴿لَوْلاَ نُزِّلَ هَـٰذَا ٱلْقُرْآنُ عَلَىٰ رَجُلٍ مِّنَ ٱلْقَرْيَتَيْنِ عَظِيمٍ﴾.
Its meaning is: on one of two men; he meant himself and Abū Masʿūd al-Thaqafī. It was al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīra al-Makhzūmī who said this. The two towns are Mecca and al-Ṭāʾif.

farraa:32-32.t:
His saying: ﴿وَرَفَعْنَا بَعْضَهُمْ فَوْقَ بَعْضٍ دَرَجَاتٍ﴾.
So We raised the master above his slave, and made some of them take others captive, so the slave and the one taken captive are made subservient to those above them.
His saying: ﴿لِّيَتَّخِذَ بَعْضُهُم بَعْضاً سُخْرِيّاً﴾, and "سِخْرِيّاً": they are one here and in "قد أفلح" [al-Muʾminūn] and in Ṣād; kasra and ḍamma in them are the same, two dialects.

farraa:33-33.t:
His saying: ﴿وَلَوْلاَ أَن يَكُونَ ٱلنَّاسُ أُمَّةً وَاحِدَةً﴾.
أن is in the position of the nominative.
His saying: ﴿لَّجَعَلْنَا لِمَن يَكْفُرُ بِٱلرَّحْمَـٰنِ لِبُيُوتِهِمْ﴾.
If you wish, you make the lām repeated in لبيوتهم, as He said: ﴿يسَأَلُونكَ عن الشَّهرِ الْحَرامِ قِتَالٍ فيه﴾; and if you wish, you make the two lāms different, as though the second were in the meaning of على, as though He said: "We would have made for them, on (على) their houses, roofs". And you say to a man to his face: "I made for you, for your people, the gifts", i.e. I made it for your sake for them.
And (السُّقُف): ʿĀṣim, al-Aʿmash and al-Ḥasan read it "سُقُفاً". If you wish, you make its singular saqīfa, and if you wish, you make it [the plural of] suqūf, so it is a plural of a plural, as the poet said:
حتى بلت حلاقيم الحُلُق * أهوى لأدْنى فقرة على شفق
(Until the throats of the throats [ḥuluq, plural of ḥalq] were worn out, he plunged to the nearest vertebra, with apprehension.)
And like it is the reading of whoever read "كُلوُا مِن ثُمُرِه", which is a plural whose singular is thimār; and like the saying of whoever read: "فَرُهُنٌ مَقْبوضَة", whose singular is rihān and ruhūn. Mujāhid and some of the people of the Ḥijāz read ﴿سَقْفاً﴾ like the singular, lightened, because saqf has the sense of a collective.
«[Translator's note: the verse is obscure as transmitted; the gloss is tentative.]»

farraa:35-35.t:
His saying: ﴿وَزُخْرُفاً﴾.
It is gold. It came in the exegesis: "We would make them for them of silver and of zukhruf". If you drop the من from الزخرف, you put it in the accusative by the verb, making it fall on it, i.e. "and zukhruf", We would make that for them of it. Others said: "and We would make for them, besides that, gold and wealth (غنى, shortened)", and it is the more likely of the two views to be correct.

farraa:36-36.t:
His saying: ﴿وَمَن يَعْشُ عَن ذِكْرِ ٱلرَّحْمَـٰنِ﴾.
He means: whoever turns away from it; and whoever read it: "ومن يَعْشَ عن" means: whoever is blind to it.

farraa:37-37.t:
His saying: ﴿وَإِنَّهُمْ لَيَصُدُّونَهُمْ عَنِ ٱلسَّبِيلِ﴾.
He means the devil, and it is in [170/b] the sense of a plural, though it was uttered as a singular. He says: the devils turn them away from the path, and they think that they are rightly guided.

farraa:38-38.t:
His saying: ﴿حَتَّىٰ إِذَا جَآءَنَا قَالَ يٰلَيْتَ بَيْنِي وَبَيْنَكَ بُعْدَ ٱلْمَشْرِقَيْنِ﴾.
So one says: (جاءنا) for one of the two, while the human and his companion came to Us. ʿĀṣim, al-Sulamī and al-Ḥasan read it جاءانا, in the dual; and the companions of ʿAbd Allāh, Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb and Ibrāhīm ibn Yazīd al-Nakhaʿī, read (جاءنا) in the singular, and that is a case where one of two suffices for both. Like it is the reading of whoever read ﴿كَلاَّ لَيُنْبَذَانِّ﴾: he says: he and his wealth will be thrown; and (ولَيُنبّذَنَّ), and the meaning is the same.
«[Translator's note: «فيقتل» at the start of this paragraph is evidently a corruption (perhaps of «فيقال», "so one says"); translated accordingly.]»
His saying: ﴿يٰلَيْتَ بَيْنِي وَبَيْنَكَ بُعْدَ ٱلْمَشْرِقَيْنِ﴾.
He means: what lies between the winter sunrise and the summer sunrise. It is also said that He meant the east and the west, and said "the two easts"; and this is the more likely of the two views to be correct, because the Arabs may combine two nouns under the name of the better known of them. So one says: "The two Zahdams have come to you", while only one of them is Zahdam. The poet said:
أخذنا بآفاق السماء عليكمُ * لنا قمراها والنجوم الطوالع
(We have taken the horizons of the sky against you: ours are its two moons and the rising stars.)
He means: the sun and the moon.
And another said:
قسموا البلاد فما بها لمقيلهم * تضغيث مفتصل يباع فصيله فقرى العراق مسير يوم واحد * فالبصرتان فواسط تكميله
(They divided the lands … the towns of Iraq are a single day's journey, then the two Baṣras, then Wāsiṭ completes it.)
He means: Baṣra and Kūfa.
«[Translator's note: the first half of this poetry is obscure as transmitted and is left unglossed.]»
He said: and a man of Ṭayyiʾ recited to me:
فبصرة الأزد منا، والعراق لنا * والموصلان ومنا مصر فالحرم
(The Baṣra of the Azd is ours, and Iraq is ours, and the two Mawṣils, and Egypt is ours, then the Sanctuary.)
He means: al-Jazīra and al-Mawṣil.

farraa:39-39.t:
His saying: ﴿وَلَن يَنفَعَكُمُ ٱلْيَوْمَ إِذ ظَّلَمْتُمْ أَنَّكُمْ فِي ٱلْعَذَابِ مُشْتَرِكُونَ﴾.
He says: your sharing will not benefit you, meaning [the devil] and his companion. And أنكم is in the position of the nominative.

farraa:44-44.t:
His saying: ﴿وَإِنَّهُ لَذِكْرٌ لَّكَ وَلِقَوْمِكَ﴾.
An honour for you and for your people, meaning: the Qurʾān and the religion; and you will be asked about thanks for it.

farraa:45-45.t:
His saying: ﴿وَسْئَلْ مَنْ أَرْسَلْنَا مِن قَبْلِكَ﴾.
Someone may say: how was he commanded to ask messengers who had passed away? There are two views on it. One of them: that he ask the people of the Torah and the Gospel, for they only inform him of the Books of the messengers that they brought; so if he [asks] the Books, it is as though he asked the prophets.
And some said: you will be taken on a night journey, O Muḥammad, and meet the prophets, so ask them about that. But he, Allah bless him, did not doubt and did not ask them.
His saying: [171/a] ﴿أَجَعَلْنَا مِن دُونِ ٱلرَّحْمَـٰنِ آلِهَةً يُعْبَدُونَ﴾.
He said: ﴿يُعبَدون﴾ (masculine plural, as for rational beings) of the gods, and did not say تعبد; and they are called يُعْبَدون because the gods are spoken to, called upon and exalted, so they were treated in the same way as kings, princes and their like.
«[Translator's note: «ولم يقل: تعبد ولا يُعْبَدون» is awkward as transmitted; translated by the evident sense.]»

farraa:48-48.t:
His saying: ﴿وَمَا نُرِيِهِم مِّنْ آيَةٍ إِلاَّ هِيَ أَكْبَرُ مِنْ أُخْتِهَا﴾.
He means: than the sign that passed before it.

farraa:52-52.t:
His saying: ﴿أَمْ أَنَآ خَيْرٌ مِّنْ هَـٰذَا ٱلَّذِي هُوَ مَهِينٌ﴾.
It is of the question that is made with أم because of its connection with speech before it; and if you wish, you refer it back to His saying: ﴿أَلَيْسَ لى مُلْكُ مِصْرَ﴾.
[Muḥammad narrated to us, saying:] al-Farrāʾ narrated to us, saying: one of the shaykhs informed me, I think it was al-Kisāʾī, that it had reached him that one of the readers read: "أَمَا أنا خير"; and the shaykh said to me: "Had I preserved the report about it, I would have read it so"; and it is good in meaning.

farraa:53-53.t:
His saying: ﴿فَلَوْلاَ أُلْقِيَ عَلَيْهِ أَسْوِرَةٌ مِّن ذَهَبٍ﴾.
He means: why have bracelets of gold not been cast upon him? Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb read it "أساورة من ذهب", and so did the people of Medina; and it is reported of al-Ḥasan: "أَسْوِرة"; and all is correct.
Whoever read "أساورة" made its singular iswār, and whoever read "اسورة", its singular is siwār. And أساورة may be the plural of أسورة, as one says in the plural of أسقية: أساقى, and in the plural of أكرع: أكارع.

farraa:54-54.t: His saying: ﴿فَٱسْتَخَفَّ قَوْمَهُ﴾: He means: he incited them (istafazzahum).

farraa:55-55.t: His saying: ﴿فَلَمَّآ آسَفُونَا﴾. He means: they angered Us.

farraa:56-56.t:
His saying: ﴿فَجَعَلْنَاهُمْ سَلَفاً﴾.
[Abū al-ʿAbbās narrated to us, saying: Muḥammad narrated to us, saying:] al-Farrāʾ narrated to us, saying: al-Qāsim ibn Maʿn narrated to me, from al-Aʿmash, from Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb, that he read it: "سُلُفا", with ḍamma and doubled vowels; and al-Qāsim [ibn Maʿn] claimed that he heard its singular as salīf. The generality still read: "سَلَفاً".
[Abū al-ʿAbbās narrated to us, saying: Muḥammad narrated to us:] al-Farrāʾ narrated to us, saying: Sufyān ibn ʿUyayna narrated to us that al-Aʿraj read it: "فجعلناهم سُلُفا", as though its singular were sulfa of people, i.e. a portion of people, like umma.

farraa:57-57.t:
His saying: ﴿مِنْهُ يَصِدُّونَ﴾.
[Muḥammad narrated to us, saying:] al-Farrāʾ narrated to us, saying: Abū Bakr ibn ʿAyyāsh narrated to me from ʿĀṣim that he abandoned يَصُدون from the reading of Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān and read يصِدون. (Al-Farrāʾ said:) And Abū Bakr said: ʿĀṣim narrated to me, from Abū Razīn, from Abū Yaḥyā, that Ibn ʿAbbās [171/b] read: (يَصِدون), i.e. they clamour and cry out.
And in another report: Ibn ʿAbbās met the nephew of ʿUbayd ibn ʿUmayr and said: "Your cousin is surely an Arab; so why does he make a mistake (yalḥan) in His saying: ﴿إذا قومك منه يصُدون﴾? It is only يصِدون." The Arabs say: يصِد and يصُد, like يشِد and يشُد, and ينمِ and ينُم from namīm (talebearing). يصدون منه and عنه are the same.
«[Translator's note: «أبى عبدالحمن» in the source is evidently Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān [al-Sulamī]; translated accordingly.]»

farraa:61-61.t: His saying: ﴿وَإِنَّهُ لَعِلْمٌ لِّلسَّاعَةِ﴾. In the reading of Ubayy: "وإنه لذكر للساعة"; and it has been narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās: "وإنه لَعَلَمٌ للساعة" and (عِلْمٌ), both; and all is correct and close in meaning.

farraa:68-68.t:
His saying: ﴿يٰعِبَادِ لاَ خَوْفٌ عَلَيْكُمُ ٱلْيَوْمَ﴾.
In the reading of the people of Medina it is: "ياعبادى", keeping the yāʾ; and ordinary speech and the reading of the generality drop the yāʾ.

farraa:71-71.t:
His saying: ﴿وَأَكْوَابٍ﴾.
The kūb is the round-headed [vessel] that has no handle (ear). ʿAdī said:
خيرٌ لها إن خشيت حجرة * من ربِّها زيدٍ بن أيوبِ متكئا تصفق أبوابه * يَسقِى عليه العبد بالكوب
(Better for her, if she fears a year of drought, than her master Zayd ibn Ayyūb, reclining while his doors are clapped open and shut, the slave serving him drink with the kūb.)
His saying: ﴿تَشْتَهِى الأَنْفُس﴾: in the codices of the people of Medina: تشتهيهِ الأنفسُ وتلدُّ.

farraa:75-75.t:
His saying: ﴿لاَ يُفَتَّرُ عَنْهُمْ وَهُمْ فِيهِ مُبْلِسُونَ﴾: in the punishment.
And in the reading of ʿAbd Allāh: "وهُم فيها مُبلسون", referring to Jahannam. The mublis is the despairing one, hopeless of deliverance.

farraa:76-76.t:
His saying: ﴿وَمَا ظَلَمْنَاهُمْ وَلَـٰكِن كَانُواْ هُمُ ٱلظَّالِمِينَ﴾.
You make (هم) here a support (ʿimād, the separating pronoun), and so الظالمين is accusative; whoever makes it a noun puts it in the nominative; and it is in the reading of ʿAbd Allāh: (ولكن كانُوا هُم الظَّالمون).

farraa:79-79.t:
His saying: ﴿أَمْ أَبْرَمُوۤاْ أَمْراً﴾.
He means: have they settled, in their own estimation, an affair that will save them from Our punishment? For We are settling [Our affair], punishing them.

farraa:88-88.t:
His saying: ﴿وَقِيلِهِ يٰرَبِّ﴾.
ʿĀṣim, al-Sulamī, Ḥamza and some of the companions of ʿAbd Allāh put it in the genitive, and the people of Medina and al-Ḥasan, as far as I know, put it in the accusative. Whoever puts it in the genitive says: "With Him is the knowledge of the Hour" and the knowledge of "his saying: O Lord". Whoever puts it in the accusative implies a verb of saying with it, as though He said: "and he said his saying", and complained his complaint to his Lord; and it is in one of the two readings [172/a]. Al-Farrāʾ said: I know it only in the reading of Ubayy, because I saw it in some codices of ʿAbd Allāh [as] وقيله. The accusative is also allowed from His saying: "نسمع سرهم ونجواهم", "and We hear his saying". And had someone said وقيلُه, in the nominative, it would be allowed, as you say: "and his call is this word: O Lord". Then He said: "فاصفَحْ عَنْهُمْ", connecting it to his supplication, as though it were from his saying, while it is from the command of Allah: He commanded him to pardon; He commanded him this before he was commanded to fight them.
«[Translator's note: the sentence about Ubayy and ʿAbd Allāh is garbled as transmitted (a reading attributed to Ubayy is justified by ʿAbd Allāh's codices); translated literally.]»

farraa:89-89.t:
﴿وَقُلْ سَلاَمٌ فَسَوْفَ يَعْلَمُونَ﴾.
سلام is nominative by an implied عليكم or the like; and had it been وقل سلاماً, it would have been correct, as He said: ﴿قالوا سَلاَماً قال سَلاَمٌ﴾.

harrat-mujtaba:2-2.t: (والكتاب المبين) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The wāw is for the oath, and the preposition phrase is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the implied (muqaddar) (أقسم) "I swear".

harrat-mujtaba:3-3.t: «قرآنا» is a second object, and the clause «لعلكم تعقلون» is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:4-4.t: The preposition phrase «في أم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «عَليّ»; «لدينا»: an adverb of place attached to «عليّ»; the clause «وإنه لعليّ» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause {إِنَّا جَعَلْنَاهُ}.

harrat-mujtaba:5-5.t: The clause «أفنضرب» is resumptive; «صفحا» is a substitute for the mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), a synonym of its governor in meaning standing in for it; «أن» is maṣdariyya, and the interpreted maṣdar «أن كنتم» is accusative by removal of the preposition (اللام).

harrat-mujtaba:6-6.t: The clause «أرسلنا» is resumptive; «كم» is the declarative (khabariyya) one, a mafʿūl bihi (direct object) placed first; the preposition phrase «من نبي» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of «كم»; the preposition phrase «في الأولين» is attached to «أرسلنا».

harrat-mujtaba:7-7.t: The clause «وما يأتيهم» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the earlier clause «أرسلنا»; «من» is redundant (zāʾida); «نبي» is the fāʿil (agent); «إلا» is for restriction; the clause «كانوا» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of «نبي», and what permits the indefiniteness is the preceding negation; the preposition phrase «به» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «يستهزئون».

harrat-mujtaba:8-8.t: The clause «فأهلكنا» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause «ما يأتيهم»; the preposition phrase «منهم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «أشد»; «بطشا» is tamyīz (specification).

harrat-mujtaba:9-9.t: The clause «ولئن سألتهم» is resumptive; the clause «من خلق» is the second object of the asking, which is suspended (muʿallaq); the clause «ليقولُن» is the answer to the oath; the verb is an imperfect, nominative (marfūʿ) by the retention of the nūn, which was dropped because of the succession of identical letters, and the wāw, dropped because of the meeting of two vowelless letters, is the fāʿil (agent); «العليم» is a naʿt (adjective).

harrat-mujtaba:10-10.t: «الذي» is a second naʿt (adjective) of «العزيز»; the preposition phrase «لكم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the second object of «جعل»; the preposition phrase «فيها» is attached to the [notion of] being-settled (istiqrār) to which the second object of the second «جعل» is attached; and the clause «لعلكم تهتدون» is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:11-11.t: His saying «والذي»: a noun conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the preceding relative noun; the preposition phrase «من السماء» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «نزل»; the preposition phrase «بقدر» is attached to a naʿt (adjective) of «ماء»; the clause «فأنشرنا» is conjoined to «نزل»; «بلدة» is described with «ميت» because it is in the sense of «البلد»; the clause «تخرجون» is parenthetical between the two conjoined items; and the kāf is a substitute for the mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), i.e.: you will be brought forth with a bringing-forth like that bringing-forth.

harrat-mujtaba:12-12.t: «والذي» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the preceding one; the preposition phrase «من الفلك» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) of «ما»; the preposition phrase «لكم» is attached to the second object of «جعل»; «ما» is a relative noun, the first object.

harrat-mujtaba:13-13.t: The interpreted maṣdar in the genitive «لتستووا» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «جعل»; «إذا» is a pure adverb attached to «تذكروا»; the clause «وما كنا له» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) clause.

harrat-mujtaba:14-14.t: The clause «وإنَّا ... لمنقلبون» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the preceding object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl); the preposition phrase «إلى ربنا» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «منقلبون».

harrat-mujtaba:15-15.t: The clause «وجعلوا» is resumptive; the preposition phrase «له» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the second object; «مبين» is a second khabar (predicate) of «إن».

harrat-mujtaba:16-16.t: «أم» is the disjunctive (munqaṭiʿa) one; the clause «اتخذ» is resumptive; «بنات» is the first object of «اتخذ»; the preposition phrase «مما» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the second object of «اتخذ».

harrat-mujtaba:17-17.t: The conditional clause is resumptive; «ضرب» here carries the meaning of «جعل» (to make): its first object is the implied (muqaddar) hāʾ and the second is «مثلا»; and the clause «وهو كظيم» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) clause.

harrat-mujtaba:18-18.t: The clause «أوَمَنْ ينشأ» is resumptive; «مَنْ» is a relative noun, the first mafʿūl bihi (direct object), the implied form being: do they make one who is brought up among ornaments a child [of Allah]? The preposition phrase «في الحلية» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «ينشَّأ»; the clause «وهو غير مبين» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) clause; the preposition phrase «في الخصام» is attached to «مبين»; it is permitted for the muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct) to govern what precedes the muḍāf because «غير» is in the sense of «لا».

harrat-mujtaba:19-19.t: The clause «وجعلوا» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the verb «يجعلون» implied (muqaddar) in the previous verse; «إناثا» is the second object of «جعلوا»; the interrogative clause is resumptive, and likewise the clause «ستكتب شهادتهم».

harrat-mujtaba:20-20.t: The clause «وقالوا» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the earlier clause {وَجَعَلُوا}, and the conditional clause is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl); the clause «ما لهم بذلك من علم» is resumptive; «علم» is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and «من» is redundant (zāʾida); the preposition phrase «لهم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar (predicate); the preposition phrase «بذلك» is attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) of «علم»; the clause «إن هم» is resumptive; «إن» is negative, and «إلا» is for restriction.

harrat-mujtaba:21-21.t: «أم» is the disjunctive (munqaṭiʿa) one, and the clause after it is resumptive; «كتابا» is a second object; the preposition phrase «من قبله» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of «كتابا»; the clause «فهم به مستمسكون» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause «آتيناهم»; the preposition phrase «به» is attached to the khabar (predicate).

harrat-mujtaba:22-22.t: The clause «قالوا» is resumptive; the preposition phrase «على أمة» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) of «آباءنا»; the preposition phrase «على آثارهم» is attached to «مهتدون».

harrat-mujtaba:23-23.t: The clause «أرسلنا» is resumptive; the kāf is attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e.: the matter is thus; the preposition phrase «من قبلك» is attached to «أرسلنا»; the preposition phrase «في قرية» is attached to «أرسلنا»; «نذير» is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), «من» is redundant (zāʾida) and «إلا» is for restriction; the clause «قال» is a ḥāl (circumstantial); the clause «وإنا مقتدون» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause «إنا وجدنا»; the preposition phrase «على آثارهم» is attached to «مقتدون».

harrat-mujtaba:24-24.t: (قال أولو جئتكم بأهدى) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The hamza is interrogative; the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya), and the conditional clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial) clause; the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl) is omitted, i.e.: will you do that even if I bring you; the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is implied (muqaddar), indicated by what precedes it; and the circumstantial wāw conjoins to an implied ḥāl for comprehensiveness, i.e.: will you do that in every state, even if I bring you something better guiding? The preposition phrase «بأهدى» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «جئتكم»; the preposition phrase «ممَّا» is attached to «أهدى»; the preposition phrase «عليه» is attached to a ḥāl of «آباءكم»; «كافرون» is the khabar (predicate) of «إن»; the preposition phrase «بما» is attached to «كافرون».

harrat-mujtaba:25-25.t: The clause «فانتقمنا» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause {قَالُوا}; the clause «فانظر» is conjoined to the clause «انتقمنا»; the clause «كان» is the object of the looking, suspended (muʿallaq) by the interrogative, [the looking] carrying the meaning of knowing; «كيف» is an interrogative noun, the khabar of kāna, and «عاقبة» is its noun.

harrat-mujtaba:26-26.t: The wāw is resumptive; «إذ»: an adverbial noun, the object of an implied (muqaddar) "remember"; «براء» is a maṣdar (verbal noun) occurring in the place of the adjective «بريء», and it is not put in the dual or plural or feminine; the preposition phrase «مما» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «براء».

harrat-mujtaba:27-27.t: «الذي» is accusative as an exception; the clause «فإنه سيهدين» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause «فطرني»; the verb is an imperfect, nominative (marfūʿ) with the ḍamma implied (muqaddar) on the first yāʾ; the nūn is of protection (nūn al-wiqāya), and the second yāʾ is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and it has been omitted for lightness.

harrat-mujtaba:28-28.t: The clause «وجعلها» is resumptive; the preposition phrase «في عقبه» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «باقية»; and the clause «لعلهم يرجعون» is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:29-29.t: The clause «متعت» is resumptive; «آباءهم» is a noun conjoined (maʿṭūf) to «هؤلاء»; the maṣdar «أن جاءهم» is genitive by «حتى», attached to (mutaʿalliq) «متَّعت»; «ورسول» is a noun conjoined to «الحق».

harrat-mujtaba:30-30.t: The conditional clause is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause {مَتَّعْتُ}; the clause «وإنا به كافرون» is conjoined to the clause «هذا سحر»; the preposition phrase «به» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «كافرون».

harrat-mujtaba:31-31.t: The clause «وقالوا» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the preceding clause «قالوا»; «لولا» is for urging (taḥḍīḍ); the preposition phrase «من القريتين» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of «رجل»; «عظيم» is a second naʿt of «رجل».

harrat-mujtaba:32-32.t: The preposition phrase «في الحياة» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) of «معيشتهم»; the adverb «فوق» is attached to «رفعنا»; «درجات» is a second object; the interpreted maṣdar of «يتخذ» is genitive, attached to «رفعنا»; «سخريا» is a second object; the clause «ورحمت ربك خير» is resumptive; the preposition phrase «مما» is attached to «خير».

harrat-mujtaba:33-33.t: The conditional clause is resumptive; the interpreted maṣdar «أن يكون» is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and its khabar (predicate) is omitted, its implied form being "existing"; the preposition phrase «لمن» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the second object; the preposition phrase «لبيوتهم» is a badal (substitute) from «لمن» and is attached to what it is attached to; the preposition phrase «من فضة» is attached to a naʿt (adjective) of «سقفا». The clause «يظهرون» is a naʿt of «معارج»; the preposition phrase «عليها» is attached to «يظهرون».

harrat-mujtaba:34-34.t: His saying «ولبيوتهم»: this preposition phrase is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to {لِمَنْ} and is attached to (mutaʿalliq) what it is attached to; «أبوابا» is a noun conjoined to {سُقُفًا}; the clause «يتكئون» is a naʿt (adjective) of «سررا»; the preposition phrase «عليها» is attached to «يتكئون».

harrat-mujtaba:35-35.t: His saying «وزخرفا»: a noun conjoined (maʿṭūf) to «سررا»; the clause «وإن كل ذلك» is resumptive; «إن» is lightened from the heavy one and inoperative; «كل» is a mubtadaʾ (subject); «لما», in the sense of «إلا», is a particle of restriction; «متاع» is the khabar (predicate) of «كل»; the differentiating lām (al-lām al-fāriqa) did not enter after the lightened «إن» because the context indicates affirmation. The clause «والآخرة للمتقين» is resumptive; the adverb «عند» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «المتقين».

harrat-mujtaba:36-36.t: The conditional clause is resumptive; «من» is a conditional noun, a mubtadaʾ (subject); the clause «فهو له قرين» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause «نقيِّض»; the preposition phrase «له» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «قرين».

harrat-mujtaba:37-37.t: The clause «وإنهم ليصدونهم» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause {فَهُوَ لَهُ قَرِينٌ}; the clause «ويحسبون» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the wāw in «يصدونهم», and the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya). He observed the wording of «مَنْ» first and so used the singular in His saying {نُقَيِّضْ لَهُ}, then observed its meaning and so used the plural in His saying «وإنهم ليصدونهم». The interpreted maṣdar from «أنَّ» and what follows it stands in place of the two objects of «حسب».

harrat-mujtaba:38-38.t: The clause after «حتى» is resumptive, and «حتى» is inceptive (ibtidāʾiyya); «بعد» is the noun of «ليت»; «يا» is for drawing attention; the clause «فبئس القرين» is resumptive, and the one specified for blame (al-makhṣūṣ bi-l-dhamm) is omitted, i.e.: you.

harrat-mujtaba:39-39.t: (ولن ينفعكم اليوم) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The clause is resumptive; «اليوم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «ينفعكم»; «إذ» is an adverb of time attached to «ينفعكم». [If it is asked:] «ينفعكم» is future because it is joined with «لن», which negates the future, so how can it govern an adverb indicating present time? The answer is that the present is close to the future; and the implied form of «إذ» is: when your wrongdoing became clear and established. The interpreted maṣdar from «أنَّ» and what follows it is the fāʿil (agent) of «ينفع»; the preposition phrase «في العذاب» is attached to «مشتركون».

harrat-mujtaba:40-40.t: The fāʾ is resumptive; «مَنْ» is a relative noun conjoined (maʿṭūf) to «العمي»; the preposition phrase «في ضلال» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar of «كان».

harrat-mujtaba:41-41.t: His saying «فإما»: the fāʾ is resumptive; «إن» is conditional, making [the verb] jussive; «ما» is redundant (zāʾida); [«نذهبن» is] an imperfect verb indeclinable (mabnī) on fatḥa in the position of the jussive; the preposition phrase «منهم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar (predicate) of «إن», «منتقمون».

harrat-mujtaba:42-42.t: The clause «فإنَّا عليهم مقتدرون» is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), and it is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the preceding apodosis by «أو»; the preposition phrase «عليهم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «مُقتدرون».

harrat-mujtaba:43-43.t: The clause «فاستمسك» is resumptive, and likewise the clause «إنك على صراط».

harrat-mujtaba:44-44.t: The clause «وإنه لذكر لك» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause {إِنَّكَ عَلَى صِرَاطٍ}; the preposition phrase «لك» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of «ذكر»; and the clause «وسوف تسألون» is parenthetical.

harrat-mujtaba:45-45.t: The clause «واسأل» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause «استمسك»; the preposition phrase «من قبلك» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «أرسلنا»; the preposition phrase «من رسلنا» is attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) of «مَنْ»; the clause «أجعلنا» is the second object of the asking, suspended (muʿallaq) by the interrogative; the preposition phrase «من دون» is attached to the second object; and the clause «يعبدون» is a naʿt (adjective) of «آلهة».

harrat-mujtaba:46-46.t: The clause «ولقد أرسلنا» is resumptive; the preposition phrase «بآياتنا» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) of «موسى»; the preposition phrase «إلى فرعون» is attached to «أرسلنا»; and the clause «فقال» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to «أرسلنا».

harrat-mujtaba:47-47.t: The conditional clause is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause {فَقَالَ}; «إذا» is of surprise (fujāʾiyya); the clause «هم منها يضحكون» is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), although the apodosis of «لما» may not be joined with the fāʾ; the preposition phrase «منها» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «يضحكون».

harrat-mujtaba:48-48.t: The clause «وما نريهم» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the preceding conditional clause; «آية» is the second object of «نريهم», and «من» is redundant (zāʾida); «إلا» is for restriction; the clause «هي أكبر» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of «آية», and what permits the owner of the ḥāl to be indefinite is the preceding negation; the preposition phrase «من أختها» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «أكبر»; the clause «وأخذناهم» is conjoined to the clause «ما نريهم»; the preposition phrase «بالعذاب» is attached to «أخذناهم»; and the clause «لعلهم يرجعون» is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:49-49.t: The clause «وقالوا» is resumptive. «أيها»: «أي» is the one addressed (munādā), indeclinable (mabnī) on ḍamma, and «ها» is for drawing attention; «الساحر» is ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition); the preposition phrase «بما» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «ادع»; and the clause «إننا لمهتدون» is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:50-50.t: The conditional clause is resumptive; «إذا» is of surprise (fujāʾiyya), and the clause after it is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ).

harrat-mujtaba:51-51.t: The clause «ونادى» is resumptive; the preposition phrase «في قومه» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «نادى»; the clause «قال» explains the calling; the clause «وهذه الأنهار تجري» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) clause; and the clause «تبصرون» is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:52-52.t: «أم» is the disjunctive (munqaṭiʿa) one, for digression (iḍrāb); the preposition phrase «من هذا» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «خير»; «الذي» is a badal (substitute) from the demonstrative; and the clause «ولا يكاد» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause «هو مهين».

harrat-mujtaba:53-53.t: The fāʾ links to the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of an implied (muqaddar) condition, i.e.: if he is truthful, then why have [bracelets] not been cast; «لولا» is a particle of urging (taḥḍīḍ); the preposition phrase «من ذهب» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of «أسورة»; «مقترنين» is a ḥāl (circumstantial).

harrat-mujtaba:54-54.t: The clause «فاستخفَّ» is resumptive; the clause «فأطاعوه» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause «استخف»; and the clause «إنهم كانوا» is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:55-55.t: The conditional clause is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause «أطاعوه»; «أجمعين» is a tawkīd (emphasis) of the third-person pronoun «هم».

harrat-mujtaba:56-56.t: «سلفا» is a second object; the preposition phrase «للآخرين» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of «مثلا».

harrat-mujtaba:57-57.t: The conditional clause is resumptive; «مثلا» is a second mafʿūl bihi (direct object), «ضرب» being made to carry the meaning of «جعل»; «إذا» is of surprise (fujāʾiyya); the preposition phrase «منه» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «يصدُّون».

harrat-mujtaba:58-58.t: «أم» is the connected (muttaṣila) conjunctive one; «هو» is a detached pronoun conjoined (maʿṭūf) to «آلهتنا»; the clause «ما ضربوه» is resumptive; «جدلا» is a ḥāl (circumstantial); the clause «بل هم قوم» is resumptive; and «خصمون» is a naʿt (adjective).

harrat-mujtaba:59-59.t: «إنْ» is negative; the clause «أنعمنا» is a naʿt (adjective) of «عبد»; the preposition phrase «لبني» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt of «مثلا».

harrat-mujtaba:60-60.t: The conditional clause is parenthetical between the two conjoined items; the preposition phrase «منكم» is in the sense of "instead of", and it is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the second object of «جعل»; the preposition phrase «في الأرض» is attached to «يخلفون»; and the clause «يخلفون» is a naʿt (adjective) of «ملائكة».

harrat-mujtaba:61-61.t: The clause «وإنه لعلم للساعة» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause {إِنْ هُوَ إِلا عَبْدٌ}; the clause «فلا تمترُنَّ» is conjoined to the clause «إنه لعلم للساعة»; [«تمترن» is] an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by the retention of the nūn, which was dropped because of the succession of identical letters, and the implied (muqaddar) wāw is the fāʿil (agent); the clause «واتبعون» is conjoined to the clause «لا تمترُنَّ»; and the clause «هذا صراط» is parenthetical between the two conjoined items.

harrat-mujtaba:62-62.t: The clause «ولا يصدنَّكم» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause «اتبعون»; the clause «إنه لكم عدو» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of «الشيطان»; the preposition phrase «لكم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «عدو».

harrat-mujtaba:63-63.t: The conditional clause is resumptive; the preposition phrase «بالحكمة» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «جئتكم»; the interpreted maṣdar in the genitive «لأبين» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to «بالحكمة» and is attached to what it is attached to, i.e.: I have come to you with wisdom and for making clear; the relative noun «الذي» is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the clause «فاتقوا» is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:64-64.t: «هو» is a pronoun of separation (ḍamīr faṣl); the fāʾ is conjunctive, and the clause «فاعبدوه» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the resumptive clause «إن الله ربي»; the clause «هذا صراط» is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:65-65.t: The clause «فاختلف الأحزاب» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause «لما جاء عيسى»; the preposition phrase «من بينهم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) of «الأحزاب»; the clause «فويل للذين» is conjoined to the clause «اختلف الأحزاب»; beginning with the indefinite «ويل» is permitted because it indicates an imprecation; the preposition phrase «للذين» is attached to the khabar (predicate) of «ويل»; and «من عذاب» is attached to the [notion of] being-settled (istiqrār) to which the khabar is attached.

harrat-mujtaba:66-66.t: «الساعة» is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the maṣdar «أن تأتيهم» is a badal of inclusion (badal ishtimāl) from «الساعة»; «بغتة» is a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the place of a ḥāl (circumstantial); and the clause «وهم لا يشعرون» is a ḥāl clause.

harrat-mujtaba:67-67.t: «يومئذ» is an adverb attached to (mutaʿalliq) «عدو»; «إذٍ» is an adverbial noun, indeclinable (mabnī) on sukūn, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), and the tanwīn is for compensation; the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject) is the clause «بعضهم لبعض عدو»; «بعضهم» is a second mubtadaʾ; the preposition phrase «لبعض» is attached to «عدو»; and «المتقين» is excepted.

harrat-mujtaba:68-68.t: The clause «يا عباد لا خوف عليكم» is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl) of an implied (muqaddar) resumptive saying; the clause «لا خوف عليكم» is the answer to the vocative, resumptive; «لا» is negative, operating like laysa; the adverb «اليوم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the [notion of] being-settled (istiqrār) to which the khabar (predicate) is attached.

harrat-mujtaba:69-69.t: «الذين» is the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), its implied form being "they"; and the clause «وكانوا» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause «آمنوا».

harrat-mujtaba:70-70.t: The clause «ادخلوا» is resumptive within the scope of the answer to the vocative; «أنتم» is a detached pronoun, a mubtadaʾ (subject); «وأزواجكم» is a noun conjoined (maʿṭūf) to «أنتم»; and the clause «تحبرون» is the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ «أنتم».

harrat-mujtaba:71-71.t: The clause «يطاف» is resumptive; «عليهم» is a preposition and its genitive noun, the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); the preposition phrase «من ذهب» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of «صحاف»; the clause «وفيها ما تشتهيه» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause «يطاف»; and the clause «وأنتم فيها خالدون» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the pronoun in «عليهم», by way of a shift of person (iltifāt).

harrat-mujtaba:72-72.t: His saying «وتلك الجنة»: a mubtadaʾ (subject), its khabar (predicate) being the clause {لَكُمْ فِيهَا فَاكِهَةٌ} in the next verse; «الجنة» is a badal (substitute); «التي» is a naʿt (adjective) of «الجنة»; and the preposition phrase «بما» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «أورثتموها».

harrat-mujtaba:73-73.t: The preposition phrase «فيها» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the [notion of] being-settled (istiqrār) to which the khabar (predicate) is attached; the clause «تأكلون» is a second naʿt (adjective) of «فاكهة»; the preposition phrase «منها» is attached to «تأكلون».

harrat-mujtaba:74-74.t: The preposition phrase «في عذاب» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar (predicate) «خالدون».

harrat-mujtaba:75-75.t: The clause «لا يفتَّر» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the pronoun in {خَالِدُونَ}; the clause «وهم فيه مبلسون» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause «لا يفتَّر»; the preposition phrase «فيه» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «مبلسون».

harrat-mujtaba:76-76.t: The clause «وما ظلمناهم» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause {لا يُفَتَّرُ}; the clause «ولكن كانوا» is conjoined to the clause «ما ظلمناهم»; «هم» is a tawkīd (emphasis) of the wāw in «كانوا».

harrat-mujtaba:77-77.t: The clause «ونادوا» is resumptive; the lām in «ليقض» is the lām of command that makes [the verb] jussive; and the clause «قال» is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:78-78.t: The clause «لقد جئناكم» is the answer to the oath; the clause «ولكن أكثركم كارهون» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause «جئناكم»; the preposition phrase «للحق» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «كارهون».

harrat-mujtaba:79-79.t: «أم» is the disjunctive (munqaṭiʿa) one, and the clause «فإنَّا مبرمون» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause «أبرموا».

harrat-mujtaba:80-80.t: The interpreted maṣdar stands in place of the two objects of «حسب»; «بلى» is a particle of answer; the clause «ورسلنا يكتبون» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) clause; «لديهم»: an adverb attached to (mutaʿalliq) «يكتبون»; and the implied (muqaddar) answer clause is resumptive, i.e.: yes, We hear.

harrat-mujtaba:81-81.t: «إن» is conditional, i.e.: if that were true, then I would be the first to worship him; but it is not true.

harrat-mujtaba:82-82.t: «سبحان» is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) whose governor is implied (muqaddar); the second «رب» is a badal (substitute); the preposition phrase «عَمَّا» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the implied verb «أسبِّح» (I glorify); and «ما» is maṣdariyya.

harrat-mujtaba:83-83.t: The clause «فذرهم» is resumptive; the clause «يخوضوا» is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of an implied (muqaddar) condition; the genitive maṣdar «حتى يُلاقوا» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «يخوضوا»; «الذي» is a naʿt (adjective).

harrat-mujtaba:84-84.t: The clause «وهو الذي» is resumptive, made up of a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate); the preposition phrase «في السماء» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «إله», because it is in the sense of "worshipped"; «إله» is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, its implied form being "He", and the clause «هو إله» is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, and this omitted [pronoun] is the returning pronoun, the implied form being: and He is the one who in heaven is God; it was omitted because of the length of the ṣila. His saying «وفي الأرض إله» is like its preceding counterpart; and the clause «وهو الحكيم» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause «وهو الذي».

harrat-mujtaba:85-85.t: The clause «وتبارك» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause {وَهُوَ الْحَكِيمُ}; «الذي» is the fāʿil (agent) of «تبارك»; the clause «له ملك» is the ṣila (relative clause); «ما» is conjoined to «الأرض»; the clause «عنده علم» is conjoined to the relative clause; and the clause «ترجعون» is conjoined to the clause «عنده علم الساعة».

harrat-mujtaba:86-86.t: The clause «ولا يملك» is resumptive; the preposition phrase «من دونه» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the omitted returning pronoun, i.e.: those whom they call upon, being other than Him, do not possess; «مَنْ» is a relative noun, excepted; and the clause «وهم يعلمون» is a ḥāl clause.

harrat-mujtaba:87-87.t: The clause «ولئن سألتهم» is resumptive; the clause «مَنْ خلقهم» is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of the asking, which is suspended (muʿallaq); the clause «ليقولُن» is the answer to the oath; «الله» is the fāʿil (agent) of an omitted verb, i.e.: Allah created us; the clause «فأنى يؤفكون» is resumptive; «أنى» is an interrogative noun, a ḥāl (circumstantial), in the sense of "how".

harrat-mujtaba:88-88.t: The wāw is a particle of oath and a preposition, and «قيله» is a genitive noun, that by which the oath is sworn, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the implied (muqaddar) «أقسم» (I swear); «القول», «القيل» and «القال» have one meaning. The clause «إن هؤلاء قوم» is the answer to the vocative, with no grammatical position, resumptive; the clause «يا رب إن هؤلاء قوم» is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl); the answer to the oath is omitted, i.e.: I shall surely do with them what I wish; and the clause «لا يؤمنون» is a naʿt (adjective) of «قوم».

harrat-mujtaba:89-89.t: The clause «فاصفح» is resumptive; «سلام» is a mubtadaʾ (subject), its khabar (predicate) being what the implied (muqaddar) preposition phrase «عليكم» is attached to; and the clause «فسوف يعلمون» is resumptive.

mekki-muskil:5-5.t:
His saying, the Exalted, {صفحا}: accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun), because the meaning of {أفنضرب} is أفنصفح ("shall We turn away?"). It has also been said that it is a ḥāl (circumstantial) in the sense of صافحين ("turning away").

His saying {إِن كُنْتُم}: whoever gave أن fatḥa made it a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose). Whoever gave it kasra made it conditional, with what precedes إن serving as its answer, since it has not governed anything in wording.

mekki-muskil:12-12.t: His saying خلق الأزواج: it is the plural of زوج. It ought to have had a plural on أفعُل, but the ḍamma is felt to be heavy on the wāw, so it was turned to the plural of فَعَل (أفعال), just as فَعَل was turned to the plural of أفعُل in their saying زمن and أزمُن.

mekki-muskil:17-17.t:
His saying {ظلّ وَجهه مسودا}: وجهه is the ism (noun) of ظلّ and مسودّا its khabar (predicate). It is also possible that in ظلّ there is a pronoun which is its ism, referring back to أحد, with وجهه a badal (substitute) for the pronoun and مسودّا the khabar of ظلّ. In (ordinary) speech it is permissible to put وجهه in the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject) and مسودّ in the nominative as its khabar, the clause being the khabar of ظلّ, with its ism (latent) in ظلّ.

His saying {وَهُوَ كظيم}: a mubtadaʾ and khabar in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial).

His saying {وَكم أرسلنَا من نَبِي}: كم is in the accusative position, governed by أرسلنا.

[Translator's note: وكم أرسلنا من نبي is in āya 6, though it is printed under this entry.]

mekki-muskil:18-18.t: His saying {أَو من ينشأ}: من is in the accusative position by an implied verb, as though He said "have you assigned (to Him) one who is brought up…". Al-Farrāʾ said it is in the nominative position as a mubtadaʾ (subject) with the khabar (predicate) omitted.

mekki-muskil:33-33.t: His saying {لجعلنا لمن يكفر بالرحمن لبيوتهم}: البيوت is a badal (substitute) for من, with the preposition repeated; it is a badal of inclusion (badal al-ishtimāl) from the side of the verb.

mekki-muskil:35-35.t:
His saying {وَإِن كل ذَلِك لما}: in the reading of whoever pronounced it without doubling (لَمَا), إن is lightened from the heavy (inna) according to the Basrans, and its ism (noun) is كل. But since it was lightened and its weight fell short of the weight of a verb, what follows it became nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), according to its original state. In (ordinary) speech it is permissible to put كل in the accusative by إن even though it is reduced, just as a (reduced) verb governs, as in لم يك زيد قائما. It is also possible that the ism of إن is latent, an omitted hāʾ, with كل nominative as a mubtadaʾ and what follows it the khabar (predicate), the clause being the khabar of إن; but there is ugliness in this because of the lām being placed late in the khabar. The lām is a lām of emphasis.

According to the Kufans, إن is in the sense of مَا, and لمّا in the sense of إلا in the reading of whoever doubled it. In the reading of whoever did not double it, مَا for them is redundant (zāʾida) and the lām enters upon متاع. It has also been said that مَا is an indefinite noun and متاع a badal (substitute) for مَا.

mekki-muskil:51-51.t: His saying {ملك مصر}: مصر is not fully declined (a diptote) because it is a masculine (noun) used to name something feminine, and because it is definite.

mekki-muskil:57-57.t: His saying {ابْن مَرْيَم}: مريم is not fully declined (a diptote) because it is a foreign noun and it is definite. It has also been said that it is a definite feminine noun, so it is not fully declined, and that it is Arabic, from رام, on the pattern مَفْعَل, but it came in the original form, like استحوذ. Had it followed the regular (phonological) course, it ought to have been said مَرام, just as one says, for مَفْعَل from دام, مَدام, and from كال, مَكال.

mekki-muskil:61-61.t: His saying {وَإنَّهُ لعلم}: the hāʾ is for Jesus, upon him be peace. It has also been said that it is for the Qurʾān, i.e. there is no Book after it.

mekki-muskil:81-81.t: His saying {قل إِن كَانَ للرحمن ولد فَأَنا أول العابدين}: إن is in the sense of مَا (negation), and the speech is taken at its apparent meaning, with العابدين from worship. It has also been said that إن is conditional and that the meaning of العابدين is "those who reject your saying that He has a son". It has also been said that إن is conditional and العابدين has its proper meaning, the sense being: "I am the first of those who worshipped Him on the basis that He has no son."

mekki-muskil:88-88.t:
His saying {وقيله يَا رب}: whoever put it in the accusative conjoined it to His saying {سرهم ونجواهم}, i.e. "We hear their secret and their private talk, and We hear his saying". It has also been said that it is conjoined to the omitted object of يعلمون, as though He said "while they know the truth and know his saying". It has also been said that it is conjoined to the omitted object of يكتبون, its implied form being "and Our messengers with them write that, and his saying", i.e. they write his saying. It has also been said that it is conjoined to the sense of وعنده علم الساعة, because its meaning is "and He knows the Hour", so it is as though He said "and He knows the Hour and knows his saying". It has also been said that it is accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. "and he says his saying".

Whoever read it in the genitive conjoined it to الساعة in His saying وعنده علم الساعة, "and the knowledge of his saying". Mujāhid and al-Aʿraj read it in the nominative, as a mubtadaʾ (subject) with the khabar (predicate) omitted, its implied form being "and his saying is the saying: O Lord"; it has also been said its implied form is "and his saying 'O Lord' is heard" or "accepted", and the like.

Abū Qilāba read يا ربَّ in the accusative, with قيله in the genitive; its implied form is that he replaced the yāʾ with an alif and dropped it, since the fatḥa indicates it, and because of the lightness of the alif. القول, القال and القيل have one meaning. The hāʾ in قيله refers to Jesus, upon him be peace; it has also been said to Muhammad, upon him be blessing and peace.

His saying {وَقل سَلام}: it is the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), its implied form being "and say: my affair is (one of) peaceful disengagement from you". He was not commanded to greet them with peace; he was only commanded to disavow them and to be at peace with (i.e. leave alone) their religion. This was before he was commanded to fight, because the surah is Meccan; then it was abrogated by the command to fight. Al-Farrāʾ said its meaning is "and say: peace be upon you"; this is rejected, because the prohibition has come against initiating the greeting of peace to them.

[Translator's note: وقل سلام is in āya 89, though it is printed under this entry.]

muyesser-irab:1-1.t: ﴿حم﴾: the discussion of the disjointed letters (al-ḥurūf al-muqaṭṭaʿa) has preceded at the beginning of Sūrat al-Baqara.

muyesser-irab:2-2.t: ﴿والكتاب المبين﴾: the wāw is the wāw of oath; «الكتاب»: genitive (majrūr) by the wāw of oath, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted verb, its implied form being «أُقسم» (I swear); «المبين»: a naʿt (adjective) of «الكتاب».

muyesser-irab:3-3.t: ﴿إنا جعلناه قرآنا عربيا لعلكم تعقلون﴾: «إن»: an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh); ﴿نا﴾ is the noun of «إن»; the clause ﴿جعلناه﴾ is the khabar (predicate) of «إن»; «جعلناه»: a verb, a fāʿil (agent) and a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); «قرآنًا»: a second mafʿūl bihi; «عربيًّا»: a naʿt (adjective); «لعل»: an abrogating particle; the kāf is the noun of «لعل»; the clause ﴿تعقلون﴾ is the khabar of «لعل»; the clause ﴿إنا جعلناه﴾ is the answer of the oath (jawāb al-qasam). It has been said: «قرآنًا» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the hāʾ in ﴿جعلناه﴾. The clause ﴿لعلكم تعقلون﴾ is causal (taʿlīliyya), with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:4-4.t: ﴿وإنه في أم الكتاب لدينا لعلي حكيم﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and the clause is conjoined to the answer of the oath, so it serves as a second answer; «إن»: an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh); the hāʾ: the noun of «إن»; «في أم»: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿علي﴾; «الكتاب»: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); «لدينا»: an adverb attached to ﴿علي﴾, or a badal (substitute) of the preposition and its genitive noun, or a ḥāl (circumstantial) of «الكتاب» or of «أم». The lām is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa); «علي»: the khabar (predicate) of «إن»; «حكيم»: a second khabar of ﴿إن﴾. Or: ﴿في أم الكتاب﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl, because it was originally a ṣifa (adjective) of ﴿علي﴾ and was put before it; and «لدينا» is an adverb attached to an omitted ḥāl, because it was originally a ṣifa of ﴿علي﴾ and was put before it.

muyesser-irab:5-5.t: ﴿أفنضرب عنكم الذكر صفحا أن كنتم قوما مسرفين﴾: the hamza is for disapproving interrogation (istifhām inkārī); the fāʾ is a conjunction, conjoining to an omitted [clause] implied between it and the hamza, its implied form being «أنهملكم فنضرب» (shall We neglect you and turn away…?); «نضرب»: an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and the fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "We" (نحن); «عنكم»: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿نضرب﴾; «الذكر»: mafʿūl bihi (direct object), i.e. the Quran; «صفحًا»: there are several views about it. The first: it is a maṣdar (verbal noun) synonymous with the meaning of ﴿نضرب﴾. The second: it is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the fāʿil of ﴿نضرب﴾, i.e. turning away. The third: it is accusative as an adverb in the sense of "side". The fourth: it is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose). «أن»: maṣdariyya, and it together with what it governs is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi; «كنتم»: an incomplete (nāqiṣ) past verb, and the tāʾ is its noun; «قوما»: its khabar (predicate); «مسرفين»: a naʿt (adjective) of ﴿قوما﴾, accusative with yāʾ because it is a sound masculine plural; the interpreted maṣdar from ﴿أن كنتم﴾ is genitive by an omitted preposition attached to ﴿نضرب﴾, i.e. «لكونكم» (because you are).

muyesser-irab:6-6.t: ﴿وكم أرسلنا من نبي في الأولين﴾: «كم»: predicative (khabariyya), in the position of an accusative (manṣūb), a fronted object of ﴿أرسلنا﴾; «أرسلنا»: a verb and its fāʿil (agent); «من نبي»: the tamyīz (specification) of the predicative ﴿كم﴾; «في الأولين»: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿أرسلنا﴾.

muyesser-irab:7-7.t: ﴿وما يأتيهم من نبي إلا كانوا به يستهزئون﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; «ما»: negative; «يأتيهم»: an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and a fronted mafʿūl bihi (direct object); «من»: a redundant (ṣila) preposition; «نبي»: genitive (majrūr) in form, nominative in position as the fāʿil (agent); «إلا»: a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr); «كان»: an incomplete (nāqiṣ) past verb, and the wāw is its noun; «به»: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿يستهزئون﴾; the clause ﴿يستهزئون﴾ is the khabar (predicate) of «كانوا».

muyesser-irab:8-8.t: ﴿فأهلكنا أشد منهم بطشا ومضى مثل الأولين﴾: the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (the eloquent fāʾ, implying an omitted clause); «أهلكنا»: a verb and its fāʿil (agent); «أشد»: mafʿūl bihi (direct object); «منهم»: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿أشد﴾; «بطشًا»: tamyīz (specification), and it has been said: a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the fāʿil of ﴿أهلكنا﴾, i.e. seizing with might; «مضى»: conjoined to ﴿فأهلكنا﴾; «مثل»: the fāʿil of «مضى»; «الأولين»: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).

muyesser-irab:9-9.t:
﴿ولئن سألتهم﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; the lām prepares for the oath (mūṭṭiʾa lil-qasam); «إن»: conditional; «سألتهم»: a past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on sukūn because it is attached to a moving nominative pronoun; the tāʾ: fāʿil (agent); the hāʾ: mafʿūl bihi (direct object).
﴿من خلق السماوات والأرض﴾: «من»: an interrogative noun in the position of a nominative (marfūʿ), mubtadaʾ (subject); the clause ﴿خلق السماوات والأرض﴾ is the khabar (predicate); the interrogative clause is in the position of an accusative (manṣūb) as the second object of ﴿سألتهم﴾, which is suspended from operation by the interrogation.
﴿ليقولن خلقهن العزيز العليم﴾: the lām occurs in the answer of the oath, because it is the one that came first, as the rule is; ﴿يقولن﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative by the retention of the nūn, which was dropped because of the succession of identical letters; the dropped wāw is the fāʿil, and the nūn is for emphasis; the clause ﴿خلقهن﴾ is the maqūl al-qawl (object of speech), and the verb is repeated for emphasis; «العزيز»: fāʿil; «العليم»: a ṣifa (adjective).

muyesser-irab:10-10.t:
﴿الذي جعل لكم الأرض مهدا﴾: «الذي»: a relative noun, a second ṣifa (adjective) of ﴿العليم﴾, or a badal (substitute); the clause ﴿جعل﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, a clause with no grammatical position; «لكم»: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿جعل﴾ on the basis that it means "created"; if it means "made [into]", the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial); «الأرض»: first mafʿūl bihi (direct object); «مهدًا»: second mafʿūl bihi, or a ḥāl.
﴿وجعل لكم فيها سبلا﴾: conjoined to what preceded; «لكم»: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿جعل﴾, or in the place of the second object; «فيها»: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the second mafʿūl bihi; «سبلًا»: mafʿūl bihi.
﴿لعلكم تهتدون﴾: «لعل»: an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh); the kāf is the noun of «لعل»; the clause ﴿تهتدون﴾ is the khabar (predicate).

muyesser-irab:11-11.t:
﴿والذي نزل من السماء ماء بقدر﴾: conjoined to the first relative noun; the clause ﴿نزل﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, a clause with no grammatical position; «من السماء»: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿نزل﴾; «ماء»: mafʿūl bihi (direct object); «بقدر»: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to a naʿt (adjective) of ﴿ماء﴾.
﴿فأنشرنا به بلدة ميتا كذلك تخرجون﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction; «أنشرنا»: conjoined to «نزل»; ﴿أنشرنا﴾ is a verb and its fāʿil (agent); «به»: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿أنشرنا﴾; «بلدة»: mafʿūl bihi; «ميتًا»: a ṣifa (adjective) of «بلدة»; «كذلك»: the kāf is a noun in the sense of «مثل» (like), indeclinable (mabnī) on fatḥa, in the position of an accusative (manṣūb), a ṣifa of an omitted maṣdar of ﴿تخرجون﴾, the implied form being «تخرجون إخراجا مثل ذلك الإخراج» (you will be brought out with a bringing-out like that bringing-out); ﴿ذلك﴾: ﴿ذا﴾ is a demonstrative in the position of a genitive as muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), the lām is for distance, and the kāf is a particle of address; «تخرجون»: a past verb built for that whose agent is not named (passive) [Translator's note: so in the text; «تخرجون» is an imperfect verb], and the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent).

muyesser-irab:12-12.t:
﴿والذي خلق الأزواج كلها﴾: also conjoined; the clause ﴿خلق الأزواج﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, a clause with no grammatical position; «كلها»: tawkīd (emphasis).
﴿وجعل لكم من الفلك والأنعام ما تركبون﴾: conjoined to ﴿خلق الأزواج﴾, falling within the scope of the ṣila; «لكم»: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted second mafʿūl bihi (direct object); «من الفلك»: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) of ﴿ما﴾; «الأنعام»: conjoined to ﴿الفلك﴾; «ما»: a relative noun, mafʿūl bihi; the clause ﴿تركبون﴾ is the ṣila of the relative noun, a clause with no grammatical position, and the returning pronoun is omitted, i.e. «ما تركبونه» (what you ride).

muyesser-irab:13-13.t:
﴿لتستووا على ظهوره ثم تذكروا نعمة ربكم إذا استويتم عليه﴾: the lām is causal (lil-taʿlīl); «تستووا»: an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an «أن» concealed after the lām, and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); the interpreted maṣdar from the concealed «أن» and the verb is genitive by the lām, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿جعل﴾ in the previous ayah; «على ظهوره»: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿تستووا﴾; «ثم»: a conjunction; «تذكروا»: conjoined to ﴿تستووا﴾; «نعمة»: the object of ﴿تذكروا﴾; «ربكم»: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); «إذا»: an adverb of future time, attached to its omitted apodosis, which is indicated by ﴿تذكروا﴾; the clause ﴿استويتم﴾ is in the position of a genitive by the annexation of the adverb to it; «عليه»: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿استويتم﴾.
﴿وتقولوا سبحان الذي سخر لنا هذا﴾: «تقولوا»: conjoined to what preceded; «سبحان»: a substitute for the mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), accusative by an omitted verb; «الذي»: muḍāf ilayhi; the clause ﴿سَخَّرَ﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, a clause with no grammatical position; «لنا»: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿سخر﴾; «هذا»: mafʿūl bihi (direct object).
﴿وما كنا له مقرنين﴾: the wāw is circumstantial (lil-ḥāl); «ما»: negative; «كان»: an incomplete (nāqiṣ) past verb, and «نا» is its noun; «له»: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿مقرنين﴾; «مقرنين»: the khabar (predicate) of «كان».

muyesser-irab:14-14.t: ﴿وإنا إلى ربنا لمنقلبون﴾: the wāw is also circumstantial (ḥāliyya); «إن»: an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh), and «نا» is the noun of «إن»; «إلى ربنا»: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿منقلبون﴾; the lām is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa); «منقلبون»: the khabar (predicate) of «إن».

muyesser-irab:15-15.t:
﴿وجعلوا له من عباده جزءا﴾: the wāw is a conjunction or resumptive; «جعلوا»: a verb and its fāʿil (agent), and «الجَعل» here means making [into] (taṣyīr); «له»: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the second mafʿūl bihi (direct object); «من عباده»: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) of ﴿جزءا﴾; «جزءًا»: the first object of «جعلوا»; the clause ﴿وجعلوا له...﴾ is conjoined, or resumptive with no grammatical position.
﴿إن الإنسان لكفور مبين﴾: «إن»: an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh); «الإنسان»: the noun of «إن»; the lām is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa); «كفور»: the khabar (predicate) of «إن»; «مبين»: a ṣifa (adjective).

muyesser-irab:16-16.t: ﴿أم اتخذ مما يخلق بنات وأصفاكم بالبنين﴾: «أم»: in the sense of «بل» (rather) and the hamza, for digression (iḍrāb), i.e. rather, has He taken; «اتخذ»: a past verb, its fāʿil (agent) latent (mustatir), its implied form being "he" (هو); «مما»: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted [word], which is the second object of ﴿اتخذ﴾; the clause ﴿يخلق﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, a clause with no grammatical position; «بنات»: the first object of ﴿اتخذ﴾; «أصفاكم»: conjoined to ﴿اتخذ﴾; «بالبنين»: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿أصفاكم﴾.

muyesser-irab:17-17.t:
﴿وإذا بشر أحدهم بما ضرب للرحمن مثلا﴾: the wāw is resumptive; «إذا»: an adverb of future time containing the sense of condition; «بشر»: a past verb built for that whose agent is not named (passive); «أحدهم»: nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); «بما»: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿بشر﴾; the clause ﴿ضرب﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, a clause with no grammatical position; «ضرب» includes the sense of «جعل» (to make), so ﴿للرحمن﴾ is attached to an omitted [word] in the place of the second object; «مثلًا»: the first object of «ضرب».
﴿ظل وجهه مسودا وهو كظيم﴾: «ظل»: an incomplete (nāqiṣ) past verb; «وجهه»: its noun; «مسودًا»: its khabar (predicate); the clause has no grammatical position, because it is the apodosis of a condition that does not make jussive; the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya); «هو»: mubtadaʾ (subject); «كظيم»: khabar; the clause is circumstantial; the clause ﴿وإذا بشر...﴾ is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:18-18.t: ﴿أومن ينشأ في الحلية وهو في الخصام غير مبين﴾: the hamza is for disapproving interrogation (istifhām inkārī); the wāw is a conjunction which conjoins the clause to an implied clause, i.e. they are so bold, and reach the farthest limits of ill manners, and assign to Allah one who is brought up among ornaments; «مَن»: a relative noun, the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of an omitted verb; and it has been said: it is a mubtadaʾ (subject) whose khabar (predicate) is omitted, its implied form being «جزء وولد» (a portion and a child); the clause ﴿يُنَشَّأ﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, a clause with no grammatical position; «يُنشأ»: built for that whose agent is not named (passive), and the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) is latent (mustatir), referring back to «مَن»; «في الحلية»: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿ينشأ﴾; «في الخصام»: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿مبين﴾; «غير مبين»: the khabar of «هو»; the clause ﴿وهو في الخصام غير مبين﴾ is circumstantial (ḥāliyya).

muyesser-irab:19-19.t:
﴿وجعلوا الملائكة الذين هم عباد الرحمن إناثا﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; «جعلوا»: a verb and its fāʿil (agent); «الملائكة»: the first object of «جعلوا»; «الذين»: a naʿt (adjective); «هم»: mubtadaʾ (subject); «عباد الرحمن»: its khabar (predicate); the clause ﴿هم عباد الرحمن﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of ﴿الذين﴾, with no grammatical position. «إناثًا»: the second object of «جعلوا».
﴿أشهدوا خلقهم ستكتب شهادتهم ويسألون﴾: the hamza is for disapproving interrogation (istifhām inkārī); «شهدوا»: a past verb and its fāʿil; «خلقهم»: mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative by fatḥa [Translator's note: the text has «بالفتة», evidently a misprint for «بالفتحة»], and the pronoun is in the position of a genitive as muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the clause ﴿أشهدوا خلقهم﴾ has no grammatical position, because it is resumptive; the sīn is a particle of the future; «تكتب»: an imperfect verb built for that whose agent is not named (passive); «شهادتهم»: nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); «يسألون»: conjoined to ﴿ستكتب﴾.

muyesser-irab:20-20.t:
﴿وقالوا لو شاء الرحمن ما عبدناهم﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; «قالوا»: a verb and its fāʿil (agent); «لو»: conditional; «شاء الرحمن»: a verb and its fāʿil, and the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) is omitted; «ما»: negative; «عبدناهم»: a verb, a fāʿil and a mafʿūl bihi; the clause has no grammatical position, because it occurs as the answer of «لو».
﴿ما لهم بذلك من علم إن هم إلا يخرصون﴾: «ما»: negative; «لهم»: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted fronted khabar (predicate); «بذلك»: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) of ﴿علم﴾; «من»: a redundant (ṣila) preposition; «علم»: a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative (marfūʿ) in position and genitive (majrūr) in form by ﴿مِن﴾; «إن»: negative; «هم»: mubtadaʾ; «إلا»: a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr); «يخرصون»: a verb and its fāʿil; the clause ﴿يخرصون﴾ is in the position of a nominative as khabar; the clause ﴿إن هم إلا يخرصون﴾ has no grammatical position, because it is causal (taʿlīliyya), or an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī).

muyesser-irab:21-21.t: ﴿أم آتيناهم كتابا من قبله فهم به مستمسكون﴾: «أم»: a conjunction balancing the interrogation in His words ﴿أشهدوا خلقهم﴾, so it is connected (muttaṣila); and it has been said: «أم» is disconnected (munqaṭiʿa), in the sense of ﴿بل والهمزة﴾ («بل» and the hamza); «آتيناهم»: a past verb, a fāʿil (agent) and a first mafʿūl bihi (direct object); «كتابا»: a second mafʿūl bihi; «من قبله»: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted naʿt (adjective), and the pronoun is in the position of a genitive as muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the clause ﴿أم آتيناهم...﴾ has no grammatical position, because it is resumptive; the fāʾ is a conjunction; «هم»: a pronoun in the position of a nominative (marfūʿ), mubtadaʾ (subject); «به»: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿مستمسكون﴾; «مستمسكون»: khabar (predicate), nominative with wāw; the clause ﴿فهم به مستمسكون﴾ has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the clause ﴿آتيناهم...﴾.

muyesser-irab:22-22.t:
﴿بل قالوا إنا وجدنا آباءنا على أمة﴾: «بل»: a particle of conjunction and digression (iḍrāb); «قالوا»: a verb and its fāʿil (agent); «إن» is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh) and ﴿نا﴾ is its noun; the clause ﴿وجدنا آباءنا﴾ is its khabar (predicate); the clause of «إن», its noun and its khabar is the maqūl al-qawl (object of speech) of their saying; «على أمة»: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) of ﴿آباءنا﴾.
﴿وإنا على آثارهم مهتدون﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; «إن»: an abrogating particle; «نا»: its noun; «على آثارهم»: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿مهتدون﴾; «مهتدون»: the khabar of «إن»; or: «على آثارهم» is a khabar, i.e. walking, and «مهتدون» is a second khabar.

muyesser-irab:23-23.t:
﴿وكذلك ما أرسلنا من قبلك في قرية من نذير﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; «كذلك»: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), its implied form being «الأمر كذلك» (the matter is thus) ﴿بعجزهم عن الإتيان بالحجة، وتمسكهم الأعمى بالتقليد﴾ (in their inability to bring a proof, and their blind clinging to imitation); the clause has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the clause ﴿قالوا..﴾ in the previous ayah; «ما»: negative; «أرسلنا»: a verb and its fāʿil (agent); «من قبلك»: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿أرسلنا﴾, or to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) of «نذير»; «في قرية»: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿أرسلنا﴾; «من»: a redundant (ṣila) preposition; «نذير»: genitive (majrūr) in form, accusative (manṣūb) in position as the object of ﴿أرسلنا﴾.
﴿إلا قال مترفوها إنا وجدنا آباءنا على أمة﴾: «إلا»: a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr), and the exception is from the most general of states; «قال مترفوها»: a verb and its fāʿil; «إن»: an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh); «نا»: the noun of «إن»; the clause ﴿وجدنا آباءنا﴾ is the khabar of «إن»; the clause of «إن», its noun and its khabar is the maqūl al-qawl (object of speech) of their saying; «على أمة»: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted second mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of ﴿وجدنا﴾.
﴿وإنا على آثارهم مقتدون﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; «إن»: an abrogating particle; «نا»: the noun of «إن»; «على آثارهم»: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿مقتدون﴾; «مقتدون»: its khabar; or: ﴿على آثارهم﴾ is a khabar, and «مقتدون» a second khabar.

muyesser-irab:24-24.t:
﴿قال أولو جئتكم بأهدى مما وجدتم عليه آباءكم﴾: «قال»: a past verb, and the fāʿil (agent) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "he" (هو); the hamza is for interrogation, and the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya), the implied form being «أتقتدون بآبائكم، ولو جئتكم بأهدى مما وجدتم عليه آباءكم من الضلالة» (will you follow your fathers, even if I have brought you better guidance than the error on which you found your fathers?); «لو»: conditional; «جئتكم»: a verb, a fāʿil and a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); «بأهدى»: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿جئتكم﴾; «مما»: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿أهدى﴾; the clause ﴿وجدتم﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, a clause with no grammatical position; «عليه»: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿وجدتم﴾.
﴿قالوا إنا بما أرسلتم به كافرون﴾: «قالوا»: a verb and its fāʿil; «إن»: an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh); «نا»: the noun of «إن»; «بما»: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿كافرون﴾; the clause ﴿أرسلتم﴾ is the ṣila of the relative noun, a clause with no grammatical position. «به»: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿أرسلتم﴾; «كافرون»: the khabar (predicate) of «إن».

muyesser-irab:25-25.t: ﴿فانتقمنا منهم فانظر كيف كان عاقبة المكذبين﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction; «انتقمنا»: a verb and its fāʿil (agent); «منهم»: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿انتقمنا﴾; «فانظر»: the fāʾ is a conjunction, and «انظر» is an imperative verb, its fāʿil latent (mustatir), its implied form being "you" (أنت); «كيف»: an interrogative noun in the position of an accusative (manṣūb), a fronted khabar (predicate) of «كان»; «كان»: an incomplete (nāqiṣ) past verb; «عاقبة المكذبين»: the postponed noun of «كان».

muyesser-irab:26-26.t: ﴿وإذ قال إبراهيم لأبيه وقومه إنني براء مما تعبدون﴾: the wāw is resumptive; «إذ»: a noun, indeclinable (mabnī) on sukūn, in the position of an accusative (manṣūb), the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of an omitted verb, its implied form being «اذكر» (remember); the clause ﴿قال إبراهيم﴾ is in the position of a genitive by annexation; «لأبيه»: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿قال﴾; «قومه»: conjoined to ﴿أبيه﴾; the clause ﴿إنني براء﴾ is in the position of an accusative as the maqūl al-qawl (object of speech); «مما»: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿براء﴾; the clause ﴿تعبدون﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of ﴿ما﴾, with no grammatical position. The clause ﴿وإذ قال إبراهيم...﴾ is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:27-27.t: ﴿إلا الذي فطرني فإنه سيهدين﴾: «إلا»: a particle of exception; «الذي»: excepted (mustathnā), and the exception is disconnected (munqaṭiʿ), as though he said: «لكن الذي فطرني فإنه سيهدين» (but the One who created me, He will guide me); or the exception is connected (muttaṣil), because they used to associate the idols with Allah. And it has been said: ﴿إلا﴾ is an adjective in the sense of «غير» (other than), on the basis that ﴿ما﴾ in ﴿مما تعبدون﴾ is a qualified indefinite (mawṣūfa), the implied form being «إنني براء من آلهة تعبدونها غير الذي فطرني» (I am free of gods you worship other than the One who created me), or on the basis of the exception being disconnected. The clause ﴿فطرني﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, a clause with no grammatical position. The fāʾ is causal (taʿlīliyya); «إن»: an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh); the hāʾ: the noun of «إن»; the clause ﴿سيهدين﴾ is the khabar (predicate) of «إن»; the sīn is for emphasis, not for the future, i.e. He will keep me continually guided; the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) is omitted out of regard for the endings of the ayahs, i.e. «سيهديني» (He will guide me).

muyesser-irab:28-28.t: ﴿وجعلها كلمة باقية في عقبه لعلهم يرجعون﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; «جعلها»: a verb, a latent (mustatir) fāʿil (agent) and a first mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the pronoun refers back to Ibrāhīm; «كلمة»: a second mafʿūl bihi; «باقية»: a ṣifa (adjective); «في عقبه»: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿باقية﴾; «لعلهم»: «لعل» is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh), the pronoun is its noun, and the clause ﴿يرجعون﴾ is its khabar (predicate).
