nahhas-irab:53-53.t: «فلولا ألقي عليه أساورة من ذهب»: this is the reading of the people of the two Sanctuaries, the people of Kufa and the people of Basra, except al-Ḥasan and Qatāda, and something narrated from ʿAbd Allāh [ibn Masʿūd] and Ubayy. As for al-Ḥasan and Qatāda, they read «لولا ألقي عليه أسورة»; and what was narrated from ʿAbd Allāh and Ubayy is «فلولا ألقي عليه أساوير». Abū Jaʿfar said: أساورة is the plural of إسوار. Al-Kisāʾī reported: إسوار, سِوار and سُوار with one meaning; and أساوير and أساورة are the same, like زنادقة and زناديق, except that when it has the hāʾ it is fully declined, because the case-ending falls on it, and it is like a noun joined to a noun. Abū Isḥāq [al-Zajjāj] said: it is fully declined only because it has a counterpart among singulars, such as علانية and عباقية. And أساور may be the plural of أسورة. (أَوْ جاءَ مَعَهُ الْمَلائِكَةُ مُقْتَرِنِينَ): [مقترنين is accusative] as a ḥāl (circumstantial).

nahhas-irab:54-55.t: (فَاسْتَخَفَّ قَوْمَهُ): that is, he made them light-minded by that speech, [leading them] to disbelief in Mūsā ﷺ. ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭalḥa said, from Ibn ʿAbbās, on (فَلَمَّا آسَفُونا): he said: He says, "they angered Us".

nahhas-irab:56-56.t: (فَجَعَلْناهُمْ سَلَفاً) is the reading of the Medinans, Abū ʿAmr and ʿĀṣim; Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb, al-Aʿmash, Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī read (سَلَفاً) [i.e. «سُلُفاً»], which is the plural of سليف; سليف has been heard from the Arabs. It is narrated from Ḥumayd al-Aʿraj that he read (سَلَفاً) [i.e. «سُلَفاً»] with ḍamma on the sīn and fatḥa on the lām, the plural of سُلْفة [Translator's note: the three readings are printed with the same vowelling in the source]; Abū Ḥātim did not know its meaning because of its anomalousness. Abū Isḥāq [al-Zajjāj] said: سلفة means a group that has gone ahead. Besides Abū Ḥātim's rejection of it, there is a point of criticism in it, because al-Kisāʾī narrated it from Ibn Ḥumayd [Translator's note: so in the source]: Ismāʿīl ibn Isḥāq al-Qāḍī mentioned, from ʿAlī ibn al-Madīnī, who said: I asked Ibn ʿUyayna about the reading of Ḥumayd (سَلَفاً) and he did not know it; I said to him: "Al-Kisāʾī narrated it from you," and he said: "We did not preserve it."

nahhas-irab:57-57.t:
(وَلَمَّا ضُرِبَ ابْنُ مَرْيَمَ مَثَلًا): مريم, peace be upon her, is a diptote because it is definite and a feminine name. It may also be a foreign name, and that would be a [further] cause; and it may be Arabic, built on the pattern مَفْعَل, coming in its original form, from رام يريم. (إِذا قَوْمُكَ مِنْهُ يَصِدُّونَ) [with kasra] is the reading of Mujāhid, Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, ʿIkrima, Abū ʿAmr, ʿĀṣim and Ḥamza, and it is narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās with a kasra on the ṣād. (يَصِدُّونَ) with a ḍamma [i.e. «يَصُدُّونَ»] is the reading of al-Ḥasan, Ibrāhīm, Abū Jaʿfar, Shayba, Nāfiʿ, Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb and al-Kisāʾī, and it is narrated from ʿAlī ibn [Abī] Ṭālib, may Allah be pleased with him, Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Sulamī and ʿUbayd ibn ʿUmayr al-Laythī.
Abū Jaʿfar said: Al-Kisāʾī and al-Farrāʾ reported that يصِدّون and يصُدّون are two dialectal forms with one meaning, as one says نمّ ينِمّ and ينُمّ, and شدّ يشِدّ and يشُدّ. Abū ʿUbayd al-Qāsim ibn Sallām distinguished between them, claiming that the meaning of يصِدّ is "to clamour" and the meaning of يصُدّ is from turning away (al-ṣudūd) from the truth; and he claimed that if it were يصُدّ with a ḍamma it would be «إذا قومك عنه يصدّون». Abū Jaʿfar said: This is a rejection of the community whose reading is authoritative, and with this view he has contradicted al-Kisāʾī and al-Farrāʾ. The proof he mentioned is not binding, because one says صددت من قوله, that is, "because of his saying"; on this [basis], the meaning of the verse — and Allah, Majestic and Mighty is He, knows best — is only "they turn away" because of that saying. And it may be that along with that turning away there was clamour, so the exegete says: its meaning is "they clamour".

nahhas-irab:58-58.t: (وَقالُوا أَآلِهَتُنا خَيْرٌ): a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate); «أم هو» is conjoined to «آلهتنا». (ما ضَرَبُوهُ لَكَ إِلَّا جَدَلًا): mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), that is, they did not say this by way of debate (munāẓara) nor by way of seeking certainty. This is the difference between disputation (jadal) and debate (munāẓara): in debate it may be that each of the two debaters is seeking what is right. The disputation with which they disputed with the Prophet ﷺ, according to what is narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās, is that when Allah, Majestic and Mighty is He, sent down إِنَّكُمْ وَما تَعْبُدُونَ مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ حَصَبُ جَهَنَّمَ أَنْتُمْ لَها وارِدُونَ [al-Anbiyāʾ: 98], they said: "Was not ʿĪsā ﷺ worshipped, and he is in your view a righteous man? Then you have placed him in the Fire with us." This is the disputation that came from them, because the speech does not entail this, since He, Majestic and Mighty is He, said إِنَّكُمْ وَما تَعْبُدُونَ and did not say «من تعبدون», and «ما» is only for other than the children of Ādam. (بَلْ هُمْ قَوْمٌ خَصِمُونَ): that is, much given to contention in what they use to repel the truth.

nahhas-irab:59-59.t: (إِنْ هُوَ إِلَّا عَبْدٌ أَنْعَمْنا عَلَيْهِ): that is, We blessed him by the appearance of signs at his hands. (وَجَعَلْناهُ مَثَلًا لِبَنِي إِسْرائِيلَ): Abū Isḥāq [al-Zajjāj] said: He means ʿĪsā ﷺ, that is, he guides them to his prophethood. Others said: We described him to the Children of Israel as being a likeness of Ādam, peace be upon him. It was also said: مَثَل and مِثْل are the same, that is, he is a human being like them.

nahhas-irab:60-60.t: ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭalḥa said, from Ibn ʿAbbās: He says: some of them succeeding others. And in [the narration of] Abū Ṣāliḥ from him: he said: "If We willed, We would make them successors and destroy them."

nahhas-irab:61-62.t:
(وَإِنَّهُ لَعِلْمٌ لِلسَّاعَةِ) is the reading of most people; it is narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās and Abū Hurayra that they read (وَإِنَّهُ لَعِلْمٌ لِلسَّاعَةِ) [Translator's note: printed identically in the source; their reading is «لَعَلَمٌ» (a sign), as the following shows]. Al-Farrāʾ claimed that the two are close in meaning. It is reported from Muḥammad ibn Yazīd [al-Mubarrad] that he said: the meaning of «لعِلم» is "a reminder, an alert and a making-known", and the meaning of «لعَلَم» is "an indication and a sign".
Abū Jaʿfar said: As for the pronoun in (وَإِنَّهُ), there are two views on its meaning. The position of Ibn ʿAbbās, Abū Hurayra, Abū Mālik, Mujāhid and al-Ḍaḥḥāk is that the pronoun refers to ʿĪsā ﷺ, the meaning being "his descent". The other view, which is the view of al-Ḥasan, is that the pronoun refers to the Quran, that is: the Quran is knowledge of the Hour, because no Book will be sent down after it. The first view is clearer, and most people hold it. It has been said: in this there is an indication that when ʿĪsā ﷺ descends, the trial (al-miḥna) will be lifted and no one's repentance will be accepted. In the ḥadīth from the Prophet ﷺ there is what indicates that, namely his saying: «He will surely break the cross and kill the swine, and the earth will cast out the pieces of its liver»; in this is an indication that no one will take zakāt from anyone, and that the trial will have been lifted and the Hour drawn near. (فَلا تَمْتَرُنَّ بِها): Abū Isḥāq [al-Zajjāj] said: that is, do not doubt. (وَاتَّبِعُونِ هذا صِراطٌ مُسْتَقِيمٌ): «مستقيم» is a naʿt (adjective) of صراط; it may also be a khabar (predicate) after a khabar.

nahhas-irab:63-64.t:
(وَلَمَّا جاءَ عِيسى بِالْبَيِّناتِ): Abū Isḥāq [al-Zajjāj] said: that is, with the miraculous signs. (قالَ قَدْ جِئْتُكُمْ بِالْحِكْمَةِ): he said: that is, with the Gospel. (وَلِأُبَيِّنَ لَكُمْ بَعْضَ الَّذِي تَخْتَلِفُونَ فِيهِ): Abū ʿUbayda said: بعض means "all", and he recited [metre: al-kāmil], verse 412:
أو يخترم بعض النّفوس حمامها
("…or its fated death carries off some souls")
Abū Jaʿfar said: This view is rejected by all the grammarians, and there is no proof for it from reason or report, because the meaning of بعض is contrary to the meaning of «كلّ» in all places. Abū Isḥāq said: the meaning is "and to make clear to you in the Gospel some of that about which you differ". Others said: he made clear to them only some of what they differed about, literally, namely what they asked him about, or that in which his informing them would be of benefit to them; and they may have differed about other things besides. The verse that Abū ʿUbayda recited contains no proof, because the meaning of «أو يخترم بعض النفوس» is that he means his own soul, [which is] some of the souls.

nahhas-irab:65-66.t: (فَاخْتَلَفَ الْأَحْزابُ مِنْ بَيْنِهِمْ): Abū Isḥāq [al-Zajjāj] said: the factions are the Jews and the Christians.

nahhas-irab:67-67.t: (الْأَخِلَّاءُ) is the plural of خليل; the pattern فُعَلاء was not used for it out of dislike of doubling. (بَعْضُهُمْ) is a badal (substitute) of الأخلاء; it may also be nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), with (لِبَعْضٍ عَدُوٌّ) as the khabar (predicate). Ibn Abī Ṭalḥa narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās on (الْأَخِلَّاءُ يَوْمَئِذٍ بَعْضُهُمْ لِبَعْضٍ عَدُوٌّ إِلَّا الْمُتَّقِينَ) (67): he said: every friendship will be enmity on the Day of Resurrection except the friendship of the God-fearing. (إِلَّا الْمُتَّقِينَ) is accusative as an exception from an affirmative [statement].

nahhas-irab:68-68.t: Whoever drops the yāʾ — and that is more frequent in the speech of the Arabs — says: the vocative is a place of omission. Whoever retains it says: it is a noun in the position of the genitive, so I retain it just as the overt noun is retained.

nahhas-irab:69-69.t: (الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا بِآياتِنا وَكانُوا) is in the position of the accusative as a naʿt (adjective) of «عبادي». What shows you that it is a naʿt of it, and makes it clear, is what Maymūn ibn Mihrān narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās; he said: While the people are at the Standing, a caller will come out from the veils and call: يا عِبادِ لا خَوْفٌ عَلَيْكُمُ الْيَوْمَ وَلا أَنْتُمْ تَحْزَنُونَ, and all the nations will rejoice and say: "We are all the servants of Allah." Then he will come out a second time and call: الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا بِآياتِنا وَكانُوا مُسْلِمِينَ, and all the nations will despair except the community of Muḥammad ﷺ and whoever was a Muslim.

nahhas-irab:70-70.t: (ادْخُلُوا الْجَنَّةَ): that is, that will be said to them. (أَنْتُمْ وَأَزْواجُكُمْ): [أزواجكم is] conjoined to the pronoun in ادخلوا, and «أنتم» is tawkīd (emphasis). (تُحْبَرُونَ) is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial). From Ibn ʿAbbās: «تحبرون» means "you will be honoured".

nahhas-irab:71-71.t: (يُطافُ عَلَيْهِمْ بِصِحافٍ مِنْ ذَهَبٍ وَأَكْوابٍ): there is reported, in the plural, كوبة and كيبان, and كياب is permissible. (وَفِيها ما تَشْتَهِيهِ الْأَنْفُسُ وَتَلَذُّ الْأَعْيُنُ): this is the reading of the people of Medina and the people of Syria, and so it is in their codices. The reading of the people of Iraq is (تَشْتَهِي) without the hāʾ. Both readings are good: retaining the hāʾ is according to the original, and dropping it is because of the length of the noun [i.e. the relative with its ṣila]. However, it is reported from Muḥammad ibn Yazīd [al-Mubarrad] that he preferred retaining the hāʾ and put it ahead of dropping it in the like of this; his reasoning in that is that the hāʾ is dropped in «الذي» only because of the length of the noun, and «ما» is shorter than «الذي»; and further, when you drop the yāʾ [Translator's note: so in the source; the hāʾ is apparently meant] in «الذي» and «التي», the masculine is still known from the feminine, whereas this is not so in «ما».

nahhas-irab:72-73.t: (وَتِلْكَ الْجَنَّةُ): [الجنة is] a naʿt (adjective) of تلك; «التي» [i.e. الَّتِي أُورِثْتُمُوها] is the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject).

nahhas-irab:74-75.t: (إِنَّ الْمُجْرِمِينَ فِي عَذابِ جَهَنَّمَ خالِدُونَ): [خالدون is] the khabar (predicate) of «إنّ»; the accusative is permissible outside the Quran as a ḥāl (circumstantial). And likewise (وَهُمْ فِيهِ مُبْلِسُونَ). Al-Farrāʾ said: in the reading of ʿAbd Allāh [ibn Masʿūd] it is «وهم فيها», meaning Jahannam; whoever says «فيه» means the punishment.

nahhas-irab:76-76.t: [الظالمين is] the khabar (predicate) of kāna. «هم», according to Sībawayh, is a separating [pronoun] (fāṣila) with no grammatical position, like «ما» in His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: فَبِما نَقْضِهِمْ مِيثاقَهُمْ [al-Nisāʾ: 155 and al-Māʾida: 13]; the Kufans say «هم» is a support (ʿimād). Al-Farrāʾ said: in the codex (ḥarf) of ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd it is «ولكن كانوا هم الظالمون». Abū Jaʿfar said: on this [reading], «هم» is in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject) and «الظالمون» is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ, and [the mubtadaʾ with] its khabar is the khabar of kāna, as you say: كان زيد أبوه خارج ("Zayd was such that his father was going out").

nahhas-irab:77-77.t:
(وَنادَوْا يا مالِكُ لِيَقْضِ عَلَيْنا رَبُّكَ): Mujāhid said: We did not know the meaning of «يا مالك» until we heard, in the reading of ʿAbd Allāh, «ونادوا يا مال». Abū Jaʿfar said: This is by way of curtailment (tarkhīm); the Arabs curtail مالك and عامر a great deal, except that this contradicts the main body [of the codices]. There are two usages in it. One says: يا مالِ أقبل ("O Māl, come forward") — this is the more eloquent of the two usages — as [the poet] said [metre: al-basīṭ], verse 413:
يا حار لا أرمين منكم بداهية ... لم يلقها سوقة قبلي ولا ملك
(O Ḥār[ith], let me not be struck by you with a calamity that no commoner before me nor king has met.)
And among the Arabs there are those who say: يا مالُ أقبل, making what remains a noun in its own right [Translator's note: the two forms are printed alike in the source; the distinction is between keeping the kasra and giving the curtailed name a ḍamma].

nahhas-irab:80-80.t: (أَمْ يَحْسَبُونَ أَنَّا لا نَسْمَعُ سِرَّهُمْ وَنَجْواهُمْ بَلى): the Kufans read (يَحْسَبُونَ) [with fatḥa on the sīn; Translator's note: the forms are not distinguished in the source]. One says حسب يحسِب and يحسَب, two dialectal forms; analogy requires the fatḥa, like حذر يحذر, except that the kasra is more frequent in the speech of the Arabs. It is said that the dialect of the Prophet ﷺ is the kasra. «أنّ» has a fatḥa because it is in the position of a noun.

nahhas-irab:81-83.t: If you make «إن» conditional, then كان is in the position of the jussive (jazm); and if you make it mean «ما» (negation), then كان has no position. ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭalḥa narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās on His saying, the Exalted: (قُلْ إِنْ كانَ لِلرَّحْمنِ وَلَدٌ): he said: He says, "The All-Merciful has no child." Abū Jaʿfar said: he made «إن» mean «ما», as He, Majestic and Mighty is He, said: إِنِ الْكافِرُونَ إِلَّا فِي غُرُورٍ [al-Mulk: 20], that is, the disbelievers are only in delusion.

nahhas-irab:84-85.t: (وَهُوَ الَّذِي فِي السَّماءِ إِلهٌ وَفِي الْأَرْضِ إِلهٌ): Abū Isḥāq [al-Zajjāj] said: that is, worshipped in the heaven and worshipped on earth. In the codex (ḥarf) of ʿAbd Allāh: «وهو الذي في السماء الله وفي الأرض الله».

nahhas-irab:86-87.t: (إِلَّا مَنْ شَهِدَ بِالْحَقِّ) is in the position of the accusative as an exception.

nahhas-irab:88-89.t:
(وَقِيلِهِ يا رَبِّ): this is the reading of the Medinans, Abū ʿAmr and al-Kisāʾī [Translator's note: from what follows, their reading is the accusative «وَقِيلَهُ»; the source's vowelling does not distinguish the readings], while the Kufans other than al-Kisāʾī read (وَقِيلِهِ) in the genitive; and Hārūn the reader claimed that al-Aʿraj read (وَقِيلِهِ) in the nominative [i.e. «وَقِيلُهُ»].
Abū Jaʿfar said: (وَقِيلِهِ) in the accusative is [explained] in five ways. Al-Akhfash Saʿīd said: «وقيله» in the accusative is from two ways: it may be in the sense of "or do they think that We do not hear their secret and their private talk, and his saying"; the second way is that it be a maṣdar (verbal noun). Abū Isḥāq [al-Zajjāj] said: the meaning is "and with Him is knowledge of the Hour, and He knows his saying", because the meaning of "and with Him is knowledge of the Hour" is "and He knows the Hour", that is, He knows the time of the Hour, which is the unseen, and He knows his saying, which is the witnessed. The fourth view is that the meaning is "except whoever bears witness to the truth while they know the truth and his saying". The fifth view: "and Our messengers with them write that, and his saying". Abū Isḥāq said: the genitive is in the sense of "and with Him is knowledge of the Hour and knowledge of his saying". Abū Jaʿfar said: the nominative is as a mubtadaʾ (subject). Al-Farrāʾ said: as you say, "his call is this word"; others construed it in the sense of "and his saying is: O Lord". One says قال قولا, قيلا and قالا with one meaning.
The clear reading is the accusative, from two angles. One of them is that, for [a word] conjoined to an accusative, it is acceptable to separate the two even if it is far, because of the separation of the governing word from what it governs in the case of the accusative, whereas in the genitive, separating them is ugly. The other angle is that the exegetes explain the verse according to the meaning of the accusative, as Ibn Abī Najīḥ narrated from Mujāhid on His saying, the Exalted: وَقِيلِهِ يا رَبِّ إِنَّ هؤُلاءِ قَوْمٌ لا يُؤْمِنُونَ; he said: Allah, Majestic and Mighty is He, is informing about Muḥammad ﷺ. And Maʿmar narrated from Qatāda on «وقيله يا رب»: he said: [it is] the saying of the Prophet ﷺ, "These are a people who do not believe." So the hāʾ in «وقيله», on this [view], refers back to the Prophet ﷺ. It was also said that the hāʾ refers back to His saying وَلَمَّا ضُرِبَ ابْنُ مَرْيَمَ مَثَلًا [al-Zukhruf: 57], that is: and He hears the saying of ʿĪsā son of Maryam ﷺ, when he despaired of his people's righteousness and faith: إِنَّ هؤُلاءِ قَوْمٌ لا يُؤْمِنُونَ. The view nearer to correctness is the first, that the hāʾ refers back to our Prophet ﷺ, for two reasons. One of them is that the mention of him is nearer to the pronoun, because the meaning is: "Say, O Muḥammad: if the All-Merciful had a child, I would be the first of the worshippers." The other reason is that what comes after it is, by consensus, an address to the Prophet ﷺ, namely (فَاصْفَحْ عَنْهُمْ), that is, turn away from them, (وَقُلْ سَلامٌ), that is, peaceable disengagement and leaving alone. The implied form in Arabic is: "my affair is peace (سلام)". Al-Farrāʾ claimed that the implied form is "peace be upon you", then [the rest] was omitted. This contradicts what the earlier [scholars] said. Sībawayh mentioned the like of this and said: it was revealed in Mecca before they were commanded to give the greeting of peace. Moreover, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade initiating the greeting of peace with the Jews and Christians, and prohibited it to the Muslims; so it is established that the meaning of وَإِذا خاطَبَهُمُ الْجاهِلُونَ قالُوا سَلاماً [al-Furqān: 63] is that it has nothing to do with the greeting of peace (al-taslīm), but is rather from disengagement and leaving alone (al-tasallum) [Translator's note: the source repeats «والتسليم» here; a word such as «التسلّم» is apparently meant]. And likewise (فَاصْفَحْ عَنْهُمْ وَقُلْ سَلامٌ). «فسوف تعلمون» is the reading of the Medinans, and on this it is part of one [continuous] speech; the reading of Ibn Kathīr, the Kufans and the Basrans is (فَسَوْفَ يَعْلَمُونَ) with the yāʾ, on the basis that the speech is complete at (وَقُلْ سَلامٌ). The meaning is: they will come to know the punishment, by way of threat.

nahhas-meani:1-2.t:
Among that is His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿ حـمۤ وَٱلْكِتَابِ ٱلْمُبِينِ﴾ [Verses 1 and 2].
That is, which has made guidance clear from misguidance, and truth from falsehood.
And ﴿المبينُ﴾ may mean: that which is clear.

nahhas-meani:3-3.t:
Then He said, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿إِنَّا جَعَلْنَاهُ قُرْآناً عَرَبِيّاً لَّعَلَّكُمْ تَعْقِلُونَ﴾.
That is, We have made it clear.

nahhas-meani:4-4.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿وَإِنَّهُ فِيۤ أُمِّ ٱلْكِتَابِ لَدَيْنَا لَعَلِيٌّ حَكِيمٌ﴾.
Maʿmar narrated from Qatāda, who said: ﴿فِيۤ أُمِّ ٱلْكِتَابِ﴾: he said: in
the origin of the Book and its entirety with Us.
Abū Jaʿfar said: The parallel of this, according to Qatāda's view, is ﴿إنَّهُ لَقُرْآنٌ مَجِيدٌ. فِى لَوْحٍ مَحْفُوظٍ﴾.
And it was said: ﴿وَإِنَّهُ فِيۤ أُمِّ ٱلْكِتَابِ﴾ means what has been decreed of good
and evil; ﴿ لَعَلِيٌّ﴾: overpowering, no one is able to repel it; ﴿حَكِيمٌ﴾: made firm (muḥkam).

nahhas-meani:5-5.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿أَفَنَضْرِبُ عَنكُمُ ٱلذِّكْرَ صَفْحاً أَن كُنتُمْ قَوْماً مُّسْرِفِينَ﴾.
Ismāʿīl narrated from Abū Ṣāliḥ: ﴿أَفَنَضْرِبُ عَنكُمُ ٱلذِّكْرَ﴾?
He said: the punishment.
And Ibn Abī Najīḥ narrated from Mujāhid, who said: Do you deny the Qurʾān and
not get punished?
Abū Jaʿfar said: The meaning on these two views is: Shall We turn away from you
the mention of the punishment?
And the position of Qatāda is that the meaning is: Shall We neglect you, and neither command you nor
forbid you?
Abū Jaʿfar said: It is said "ḍarabtu ʿanhu" and "aḍrabtu", i.e. I left it.
* Then He said, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿صَفْحاً﴾, that is, turning away.
It is possible that the meaning is: Shall We turn away from you a turning away (i.e. a mafʿūl muṭlaq, absolute object), as it is said:
"he leaves it a leaving."
And it is possible that the meaning is: Shall We turn the Reminder away from you, turning away (ṣāfiḥīn) — as
it is said: "So-and-so came walking (mashyan)" [Translator's note: i.e. as a ḥāl, circumstantial].
And the meaning of "ṣafaḥtu ʿanhu" is: I turned away from him, i.e. I turned to him the side (ṣafḥa) of my neck. The poet said:
صَفُوحاً فَمَا تَلْقَاكَ إلاَّ بَخِيلَةً * فَمَنْ مَلَّ مِنْهَا ذَلِكَ الوَصْلَ مَلَّتِ
(Turning away — she never meets you except as a miser; whoever grows weary of that union with her, she grows weary too.)
* Then He said, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿أَن كُنتُمْ قَوْماً مُّسْرِفِينَ﴾.
Qatāda said: that is, polytheists.
Abū Jaʿfar said: The meaning is "because you were", if you read ﴿أَنْ﴾ with fatḥa; and so
read al-Ḥasan, Abū ʿAmr and Ibn Kathīr.
The people of Medina and the people of Kufa read it with kasra, and according to some
lexicographers — among them Abū Ḥātim — this is a solecism (laḥn). It became a solecism in their view only because
they were rebuked for something that had already been established and had happened, so this is the place for "an" with fatḥa, as
He, Glorified is He, said ﴿عَبَسَ وَتَوَلَّى. أَنْ جَاءَهُ الأَعْمَى﴾.
Abū Jaʿfar said: But according to al-Khalīl, Sībawayh, al-Kisāʾī and the Qurʾān readers, this is good.
Sībawayh said: I asked al-Khalīl about his saying — meaning al-Farazdaq —:
أَتَغْضَبُ إنْ أُذْنَا قُتَيْبَةَ حُزَّتَا * جِهَاراً وَلَمْ تَغْضَبْ لَقَتْلِ ابنِ خَازِمٍ
(Are you angry that the two ears of Qutayba were cut off openly, when you were not angry at the killing of Ibn Khāzim?)
He said: It is "in" with kasra, because it is ugly to separate "an" from the verb.
Abū Jaʿfar said: And this is something that has already happened.
Abū Isḥāq said: This has the sense of the present state, when there is
in the speech a sense of rebuke and making [the addressee] acknowledge, i.e. "Is this your state?"
Abū Jaʿfar said: So on this basis is His saying ﴿أَن كُنتُمْ قَوْماً مُّسْرِفِينَ﴾.

nahhas-meani:8-8.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿فَأَهْلَكْنَآ أَشَدَّ مِنْهُم بَطْشاً وَمَضَىٰ مَثَلُ ٱلأَوَّلِينَ﴾.
Mujāhid said: that is, the way (sunna) of the former peoples.
Qatāda said: that is, the punishment of the former peoples.
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿وَجَعَلَ لَكُمْ فِيهَا سُبُلاً﴾, that is, roads.

nahhas-meani:12-12.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿وَٱلَّذِي خَلَقَ ٱلأَزْوَاجَ كُلَّهَا﴾.
That is, all the kinds.
* Then He said, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿وَجَعَلَ لَكُمْ مِّنَ ٱلْفُلْكِ وَٱلأَنْعَامِ مَا تَرْكَبُونَ﴾.
Mujāhid said: camels, horses, mules and donkeys.

nahhas-meani:13-13.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿لِتَسْتَوُواْ عَلَىٰ ظُهُورِهَِ﴾.
That is, on the backs of this kind.
﴿ثُمَّ تَذْكُرُواْ نِعْمَةَ رَبِّكُمْ إِذَا ٱسْتَوَيْتُمْ عَلَيْهِ﴾, that is, you say:
Praise be to Allah.
As Abū Isḥāq narrated from ʿAlī ibn Rabīʿa, who said: I saw ʿAlī
ibn Abī Ṭālib, Allah's blessings upon him, put his foot in the stirrup and say
﴿بِسْمِ اللهِ﴾; and when he had settled himself riding he said ﴿الحمدُ لله﴾, then he said
﴿سُبْحَانَ ٱلَّذِي سَخَّرَ لَنَا هَـٰذَا وَمَا كُنَّا لَهُ مُقْرِنِينَ﴾ — O Allah, there is no god but
You; I have done evil, so forgive me, for none forgives sins but You. Then
he said: I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ do as I have done.
And Ibn Abī Najīḥ narrated from Mujāhid: Whoever rides and does not say
﴿سُبْحَانَ ٱلَّذِي سَخَّرَ لَنَا هَـٰذَا وَمَا كُنَّا لَهُ مُقْرِنِينَ﴾, the devil says to him: Sing! And if he cannot do it well, he says to him: Wish [idle wishes]!
Qatāda said: ﴿مُقْرِنِينَ﴾, that is, in strength.
Abū Jaʿfar said: The lexicographers report that it is said "aqrana lahu" when
he was able to cope with it; and they recited:
رَكِبْتُمْ صَعْبَتِي أَشَرَاً وَحَيْناً * وَلَسْتُمْ لِلْصِّعَابِ بِمُقْرِنِينَا
(You mounted my unruly [she-camel] out of insolence and to your doom, yet you are not able to master the unruly.)
And the literal sense of "aqrantu lahu" is: I became a match (qirn) for him; it is said: he is his qirn (match) in
combat, and he is of his qarn, i.e. his equal in age.

nahhas-meani:14-14.t:
Then the Exalted said: ﴿وَإِنَّآ إِلَىٰ رَبِّنَا لَمُنقَلِبُونَ﴾.
That is, we shall surely be resurrected.

nahhas-meani:15-15.t:
Then He said, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿وَجَعَلُواْ لَهُ مِنْ عِبَادِهِ جُزْءًا إِنَّ ٱلإنسَانَ لَكَفُورٌ مُّبِينٌ﴾.
Qatāda said: ﴿جُزْءً﴾: that is, an equal.
Abū Jaʿfar said: The meaning on their view is that they worshipped the angels, and so assigned
to Allah, Majestic and Mighty, a likeness and an equal.
ʿAṭāʾ said: ﴿جُزْءً﴾: that is, a share and a partner.
Abū Jaʿfar said: This is clearer, as it is said: "This is so-and-so's portion." This was said
of them because they made the angels the daughters of Allah; this is the view of Mujāhid.
And the meaning of ﴿وَجَعَلُوا﴾ is: they said this and described it.

nahhas-meani:18-18.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿أَوَمَن يُنَشَّأُ فِي ٱلْحِلْيَةِ وَهُوَ فِي ٱلْخِصَامِ غَيْرُ مُبِينٍ﴾.
Ibn ʿAbbās said: He means women; their attire has been made different from the attire of men.
Abū Jaʿfar said: It is possible that the meaning is: Is it the one brought up in ornaments
that they assign as a share to Allah, Majestic and Mighty?
And it is possible that it is in the position of the nominative (marfūʿ).
* Then He said, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿وَهُوَ فِي ٱلْخِصَامِ غَيْرُ مُبِينٍ﴾.
Qatāda said: Rarely does a woman speak having an argument [in her favour] without turning it against herself.

nahhas-meani:19-19.t:
Then He said, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿وَجَعَلُواْ ٱلْمَلاَئِكَةَ ٱلَّذِينَ هُمْ عِبَادُ ٱلرَّحْمَـٰنِ إِنَاثاً﴾.
﴿جَعَلُواْ﴾ here means: they described; this is one of the senses of "jaʿala"
mentioned by al-Khalīl and Sībawayh, as you say: "I made so-and-so the most learned of people,"
i.e. I described him as such.

nahhas-meani:20-20.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿وَقَالُواْ لَوْ شَآءَ ٱلرَّحْمَـٰنُ مَا عَبَدْنَاهُمْ مَّا لَهُم بِذَلِكَ مِنْ عِلْمٍ إِنْ هُمْ إِلاَّ يَخْرُصُونَ﴾.
This is a difficult verse, and the scholars have discussed it.
a- Among the best of what they said is that His saying, Mighty and Majestic, ﴿مَّا لَهُم بِذَلِكَ مِنْ عِلْمٍ﴾ refers back to His saying ﴿وَجَعَلُوا المَلاَئِكَةَ الَّذِينَ هُمْ عِبَادُ الرَّحْمَنِ
إنَاثاً﴾.
So the meaning is: Allah, Majestic and Mighty, did not reject their saying ﴿لَوْ شَآءَ ٱلرَّحْمَـٰنُ مَا عَبَدْنَاهُمْ﴾; rather the meaning is: they have no knowledge for their saying that the angels are the daughters of Allah. And what follows indicates that this is the meaning, because after it comes ﴿أَمْ
آتَيْنَاهُمْ كِتَاباً مِنْ قَبْلِهِ﴾, i.e. or did We send down to them a book containing this?
b- And there is another view on the verse, namely that the meaning of ﴿مَّا لَهُم بِذَلِكَ مِنْ عِلْمٍ﴾ is: they have no excuse in this, because they considered that to be an excuse for them, so Allah rejected
that from them; so the rejection is taken according to the sense, as is His saying ﴿أَمْ آتَيْنَاهُمْ
كِتَاباً﴾.

nahhas-meani:22-22.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿بَلْ قَالُوۤاْ إِنَّا وَجَدْنَآ آبَآءَنَا عَلَىٰ أُمَّةٍ﴾.
Mujāhid and ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz read ﴿عَلَى إمَّةٍ﴾.
Al-Kisāʾī said: They are two dialectal forms with one meaning.
Abū Jaʿfar said: What is well known in the language is that "al-imma" with kasra is
the path in religion and the way followed, as the poet said:
حَلَفْتُ فَلَمْ أَتْرُكْ لِنَفْسِكَ رِيبَةً * وَهَلْ يَأْثَمَنْ ذُو إمَّةٍ وَهُوَ طَائِعُ
(I swore, and left no doubt for your soul; and does one who holds to a religion (imma) sin when he is obedient?)
And al-umma is the custom (sunna) and the creed (milla); it may have meanings other than this. And
al-imma may mean sovereignty and completeness, as the poet said:
 * ثُمَّ بَعْدَ الفَلاَحِ والمُلْكِ والإِمَّةِ وَارَتْهُمُوا هُنَاكَ القُبُورُ *
(Then, after prosperity, kingship and dominion (imma), the graves there hid them.)
And Ibn Abī Najīḥ narrated from Mujāhid: ﴿إِنَّا وَجَدْنَآ آبَآءَنَا عَلَىٰ أُمَّةٍ﴾: upon a creed.
* And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿وَإِنَّا عَلَىٰ آثَارِهِم مُّهْتَدُونَ﴾.
It is possible that it is a khabar (predicate) after a khabar.
And it is possible that the meaning is: guided upon their footsteps.

nahhas-meani:23-23.t:
Then He, Majestic and Mighty, informed that the prophets before him had been told the like of this, saying:
﴿وَكَذَلِكَ مَآ أَرْسَلْنَا مِن قَبْلِكَ فِي قَرْيَةٍ مِّن نَّذِيرٍ إِلاَّ قَالَ مُتْرَفُوهَآ إِنَّا وَجَدْنَآ آبَآءَنَا عَلَىٰ أُمَّةٍ وَإِنَّا عَلَىٰ آثَارِهِم مُّقْتَدُونََ﴾.

nahhas-meani:24-24.t:
Then He said, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿قُلْ أَوَلَوْ جِئْتُكُمْ بِأَهْدَىٰ مِمَّا وَجَدتُّمْ عَلَيْهِ آبَآءَكُمْ﴾.
The meaning is: Even if I brought you something better guiding than what you found your fathers upon, would you persist in
what your fathers were upon?

nahhas-meani:26-26.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿وَإِذْ قَالَ إِبْرَاهِيمُ لأَبِيهِ وَقَوْمِهِ إِنَّنِي بَرَآءٌ مِّمَّا تَعْبُدُونَ﴾.
In one reading: ﴿إنَّنِي بَرِيءٌ﴾.
Al-Farrāʾ reported that some people write the hamza as alif in every position.
So on this basis it is read ﴿بَرِيءٌ﴾ even though in the written text (al-sawād) it has an alif. And whoever
reads ﴿بَرَاءٌ﴾ says barāʾ also for the dual and the plural, meaning "possessors of disavowal (dhawī barāʾ)".

nahhas-meani:27-27.t:
Then He said, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿إِلاَّ ٱلَّذِي فَطَرَنِي فَإِنَّهُ سَيَهْدِينِ﴾.
Qatāda said: that is, who created me.
Abū Jaʿfar said: It is possible that it is an exception from the first.
And it is possible that "illā" means "lākin" (but).

nahhas-meani:28-28.t:
Then He said, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿وَجَعَلَهَا كَلِمَةً بَاقِيَةً فِي عَقِبِهِ لَعَلَّهُمْ يَرْجِعُونَ﴾.
Mujāhid said: ﴿كَلِمَةً بَاقِيَةً﴾ is: There is no god but Allah.
Qatāda said: the affirmation of oneness and sincere devotion among his posterity.
Mujāhid said: among his offspring.
Qatāda said: There will never cease to be among the offspring of Abraham ﷺ someone who worships Allah, Majestic
and Mighty, until the Day of Resurrection.
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty, ﴿لَعَلَّهُمْ يَرْجِعُونَ﴾: to your religion and the religion of Abraham,
Allah's blessings be upon them both, since they were among his offspring.

nahhas-meani:31-31.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿وَقَالُواْ لَوْلاَ نُزِّلَ هَـٰذَا ٱلْقُرْآنُ عَلَىٰ رَجُلٍ مِّنَ ٱلْقَرْيَتَيْنِ عَظِيمٍ﴾.
Ibn ʿAbbās said: The two towns are Mecca and al-Ṭāʾif.
Qatāda said: The two men are "Abū Masʿūd al-Thaqafī", whose name was ʿUrwa ibn
Masʿūd, of the people of al-Ṭāʾif, and "al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīra ibn ʿAbd Allāh
al-Makhzūmī", of the people of Mecca.
Mujāhid said: The two men are "ʿUtba ibn Rabīʿa", of the people of Mecca, and Abū
Masʿūd al-Thaqafī, whose name was "ʿUmayr ibn ʿAmr ibn Masʿūd".
Abū Jaʿfar said: This is narrated from a group of trustworthy narrators, among them "Ibn
Jurayj" and "Ibn Abī Najīḥ".
And trustworthy narrators also narrated that from Qatāda; but Qatāda's view is closer
to being correct, because Maʿmar narrated from him that he said: Al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīra said: If
what Muḥammad says were true, it would have been sent down to me or to Abū Masʿūd al-Thaqafī.
So Qatāda reported the occasion of the verse's revelation.
Abū al-ʿAbbās said: The implied structure in Arabic is: upon a man of two men
of the two towns.
Abū Jaʿfar said: The precise implied structure in Arabic is: upon a man of
the two men of the two towns, as He, Glorified is He, said ﴿وَاسْأَلِ القَرْيَةَ﴾.

nahhas-meani:32-32.t:
Then He said, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿أَهُمْ يَقْسِمُونَ رَحْمَتَ رَبِّكَ نَحْنُ قَسَمْنَا بَيْنَهُمْ مَّعِيشَتَهُمْ فِي ٱلْحَيَاةِ ٱلدُّنْيَا﴾.
That is, just as We have apportioned provision among them and preferred some of them over others, so We have preferred some of them over others by choosing [them] for the message.
* Then He said, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿لِّيَتَّخِذَ بَعْضُهُم بَعْضاً سُخْرِيّاً﴾.
That is, so that some of them may be servants (khawal) for others; and "sukhrī"
and "sikhrī" are the same.
Then He, Majestic and Mighty, informed that the mercy He has is better, saying
﴿وَرَحْمَتُ رَبِّكَ خَيْرٌ مِّمَّا يَجْمَعُونَ﴾.
Al-Ḥasan read: ﴿تَجْمَعُونَ﴾ with tāʾ.

nahhas-meani:33-33.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿وَلَوْلاَ أَن يَكُونَ ٱلنَّاسُ أُمَّةً وَاحِدَةً لَّجَعَلْنَا لِمَن يَكْفُرُ بِٱلرَّحْمَـٰنِ لِبُيُوتِهِمْ سُقُفاً مِّن فِضَّةٍ وَمَعَارِجَ عَلَيْهَا يَظْهَرُونَ﴾.
There are two views on the meaning of the verse:
Al-Ḥasan and Qatāda said: Were it not that all people would disbelieve, We would have done this.
Abū Jaʿfar said: The meaning of this view is: were it not that people would incline to
this world and so disbelieve, We would have given the disbeliever this, because of how insignificant this world is to Allah, Mighty and Majestic.
The other view — al-Kisāʾī stated it — he said: The meaning is: were it not for Our will
that among the disbelievers there be rich and poor, and among the Muslims likewise, We would have given
the disbelievers this of the world, because of how insignificant it is to Allah, Majestic and Mighty.
Al-Farrāʾ said: It is possible that the meaning of ﴿لِبُيُوتِهِمْ﴾ is "upon their houses".
Abū Jaʿfar said: Sufyān narrated from Ismāʿīl, from al-Shaʿbī:
﴿سُقُفاً مِّن فِضَّةٍ﴾: he said: juzūʿan «[Translator's note: so in the text (جُزُوعاً); presumably for جذوعاً, "beams"]»; ﴿وَمَعَارِجَ﴾: he said: steps;
﴿عَلَيْهَا يَظْهَرُونَ﴾: he said: they ascend.
A group read: ﴿سَقْفاً مِنْ فِضَّةٍ﴾, and some of the lexicographers rejected this reading,
saying: if it were so, He would have said "ʿalayhi" (upon it [masc.]).
Abū Jaʿfar said: This does not follow, because "ʿalayhā" may refer to the steps.

nahhas-meani:34-34.t:
Then He said, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿وَلِبُيُوتِهِمْ أَبْوَاباً﴾.
That is, of silver; ﴿وَسُرُراً﴾, that is, of silver; ﴿وَزُخْرُفاً﴾.
Shuʿba narrated from al-Ḥakam, from Mujāhid, who said: "I did not know what
﴿وزخرفاً﴾ meant until I found it in the reading of ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd:
﴿وَذَهَباً﴾."
Abū Jaʿfar said: There are two views on its meaning:
One of them: that the meaning is: and We would have made for them zukhruf, i.e. wealth.
The other: that the meaning is: of silver and of gold (zukhruf); then
"min" was omitted and it was put in the accusative.

nahhas-meani:36-36.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿وَمَن يَعْشُ عَن ذِكْرِ ٱلرَّحْمَـٰنِ نُقَيِّضْ لَهُ شَيْطَاناً فَهُوَ لَهُ قَرِينٌ﴾.
Saʿīd narrated from Qatāda, who said: ﴿يَعْشُ﴾: turns away.
Abū ʿUbayda said: ﴿يَعْشُ﴾: his eye grows dim.
And ʿIkrima narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās: he becomes blind.
Abū Jaʿfar said: On Ibn ʿAbbās's view the reading would have to be
﴿وَمَنْ يَعْشَ﴾ with fatḥa on the shīn.
As for Qatāda's saying that ﴿يَعْشُ﴾ means "turns away" — and it is the view of al-Farrāʾ — it is not
known in the language. It is only said "ʿashā yaʿshū" when one walks with weak
sight. Al-Ḥuṭayʾa said:
مَتَى تَأْتِهِ تَعْشُو إلَى ضَوْءِ نَارِهِ * تَجِدْ خَيْرَ نَارٍ عِنْدَهَا خَيْرُ مَوْقِدِ
(Whenever you come to him, making your dim way toward the light of his fire, you find the best of fires with the best of kindlers beside it.)
The parallel of this: "ʿaraja al-rajulu yaʿruju", i.e. he walked with the gait of a lame man;
and "ʿarija yaʿraju": he became lame.
The soundest view on this is that of Abū ʿUbayda; Allah, Majestic and Mighty, said
﴿الَّذِينَ كَانَتْ أَعْيُنُهُمْ فِي غِطَاءٍ عَنْ ذِكْرِي﴾.
And in the report: Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyab lost one of his eyes, and he used to "yaʿshū" with the other, i.e. see with it weakly.
* And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿نُقَيِّضْ لَهُ شَيْطَاناً فَهُوَ لَهُ قَرِينٌ﴾.
It was said: as a recompense for what he did.
Saʿīd al-Jurayrī said concerning the saying of the Exalted ﴿نُقَيِّضْ لَهُ شَيْطَاناً﴾:
He said: It has reached us that when the disbeliever comes out of his grave, a devil seizes him by the hand, and does not
cease to be with him until Allah, Mighty and Majestic, admits him into the Fire; and that is His saying, Majestic and Mighty,
﴿قَالَ يَا لَيْتَ بَيْنِي وَبَيْنَكَ بُعْدَ المَشْرِقَيْنِ فَبِئْسَ القَرِينُ﴾. And an angel is assigned
to the believer and does not cease to be with him until Allah judges between the creatures, or he reaches what Allah wills.

nahhas-meani:37-37.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿وَإِنَّهُمْ لَيَصُدُّونَهُمْ عَنِ ٱلسَّبِيلِ وَيَحْسَبُونَ أَنَّهُم مُّهْتَدُونَ﴾.
That is, the devils turn the disbeliever away from the path.
﴿وَيَحْسَبُونَ أَنَّهُم مُّهْتَدُونَ﴾, that is, and the disbelievers think that they are guided.

nahhas-meani:38-38.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿حَتَّىٰ إِذَا جَآءَنَا قَالَ يٰلَيْتَ بَيْنِي وَبَيْنَكَ بُعْدَ ٱلْمَشْرِقَيْنِ فَبِئْسَ ٱلْقَرِينُ﴾.
Qatāda said: ﴿حَتَّىإذَا جَآءَانَا﴾: he said: the disbeliever and his companion together.
Abū Jaʿfar said: And it is read ﴿حَتى إذا جاءنَا﴾, by which the disbeliever is meant
on the surface, while the meaning applies to both of them together, because that is known from what follows, as
the poet said:
وَعَيْنٌ لَهَا حَدْرَةٌ بَدْرَةٌ * شُقَّتْ مَآقِيهِمَا مِنْ أُخَرْ
(And an eye, large and full, whose [two] inner corners were slit from behind.) «[Translator's note: the singular "eye" is used while the dual pronoun shows that both are meant.]»
* And the saying of the Exalted: ﴿قَالَ يٰلَيْتَ بَيْنِي وَبَيْنَكَ بُعْدَ ٱلْمَشْرِقَيْنِ﴾.
There are two views on its meaning:
One of them: that "the winter sunrise point" and "the summer sunrise point" are meant.
The other: that the east and the west are meant; this follows the usage of the Arabs, because when two things are joined in one sense, one of them is given precedence «[Translator's note: and the dual is formed from it]», as the poet said:
أَخَذْنَا بِآفَاقِ السَّمَاءِ عَلَيْكُمُ * لَنَا قَمَرَاهَا وَالنُّجُومُ الطَّوَالِعُ
(We have taken hold of the horizons of the sky against you; ours are its two moons [the sun and the moon] and the rising stars.)
And Abū ʿUbayda recited the verse of Jarīr:
مَا كَانَ يَرْضَى رَسُولُ اللهِ فِعْلَهُمُ * وَالطَّيِّبَانِ أَبُو بَكْرٍ وَلاَ عُمَرُ
(The Messenger of Allah would not have approved their deed, nor the two good ones, Abū Bakr and ʿUmar.)
And Sībawayh recited:
 * "قَدْنِيَ منْ نَصْرِ الخُبَيْبَيْنِ قَدِي" *
(Enough for me of support for the two Khubaybs — enough!)
He means "ʿAbd Allāh" and "Muṣʿab", the two sons of al-Zubayr; whereas "Abū
Khubayb" was ʿAbd Allāh [alone].
And in the report: the people of the Camel said to ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib,
peace be upon him: Give us the practice of the two ʿUmars — meaning Abū Bakr and ʿUmar.

nahhas-meani:39-39.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿وَلَن يَنفَعَكُمُ ٱلْيَوْمَ إِذ ظَّلَمْتُمْ أَنَّكُمْ فِي ٱلْعَذَابِ مُشْتَرِكُونَ﴾.
The meaning is: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has denied the people of the Fire this measure of
relief, namely consolation through shared suffering (al-taʾassī): when one afflicted sees someone who equals him in
misfortune, that eases his grief — as al-Khansāʾ said:
فَلَوْلاَ كَثْرَةُ البَاكِينَ حَوْلِي * عَلَى إِخْوَانِهِمْ لَقَتَلْتُ نَفْسِي
وَمَا يَبْكُونَ مِثْلَ أَخِي وَلَكِنْ * أعَزِّي النَّفْسَ مِنْهُ بِالتَّأَسِّي
(Were it not for the many around me weeping for their brothers, I would have killed myself; they do not weep for one like my brother, but I console my soul for him by sharing in their grief.)

nahhas-meani:41-41.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿فَإِمَّا نَذْهَبَنَّ بِكَ فَإِنَّا مِنْهُم مُّنتَقِمُونَ﴾.
Qatāda said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ departed and the vengeance remained. There is no prophet
but that he saw the vengeance in his community, except Muḥammad ﷺ; but he was shown what would befall his community after him, and he was never seen thereafter laughing cheerfully.

nahhas-meani:42-42.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿أَوْ نُرِيَنَّكَ ٱلَّذِي وَعَدْنَاهُمْ فَإِنَّا عَلَيْهِمْ مُّقْتَدِرُونَ﴾.
It was said: the meaning is: that which We promised them, and promised you against them, of victory.
And it was said: "that which We promised them" refers back to the saying of the Exalted ﴿والآخِرَةُ عِنْدَ
رَبِّكَ لِلْمُتَّقِينَ﴾, i.e. that which We promised the God-fearing of victory, and they were indeed given victory.

nahhas-meani:43-43.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿فَٱسْتَمْسِكْ بِٱلَّذِيۤ أُوحِيَ إِلَيْكَ إِنَّكَ عَلَىٰ صِرَاطٍ مُّسْتَقِيمٍ﴾.
Qatāda said: that is, to the Qurʾān; ﴿إِنَّكَ عَلَىٰ صِرَاطٍ مُّسْتَقِيمٍ﴾:
he said: upon Islam.
﴿وإنَّهُ لَذِكْرٌ لَكَ وَلِقَوْمِكَ﴾: he said: the Qurʾān.
And Muḥammad ibn Yūsuf narrated from Sufyān: ﴿وَإنَّهُ لَذِكْرٌ لَكَ
وَلِقَوْمِكَ﴾: he said: an honour for you and for your people.

nahhas-meani:44-44.t:
Then He said, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿وَسَوْفَ تُسْأَلُونَ﴾.
Al-Farrāʾ said: that is, and you will be asked about the gratitude due for it.

nahhas-meani:45-45.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿وَسْئَلْ مَنْ أَرْسَلْنَا مِن قَبْلِكَ مِن رُّسُلِنَآ أَجَعَلْنَا مِن دُونِ ٱلرَّحْمَـٰنِ آلِهَةً يُعْبَدُونَ﴾.
Abū Jaʿfar said: This is a difficult verse, and there are two views on its meaning:
Abū ʿAwāna narrated from Abū Bishr, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, who said:
He met the messengers, Allah's blessings upon them, on the night he was taken on the Night Journey.
This is one view, and its meaning is: you will be taken on the Night Journey and will meet the messengers, so ask them.
The other view — the view of "Muḥammad ibn Yazīd" and a group of
scholars — is that this carries the sense of making [them] stand to account, making them acknowledge, and rebuke; and the meaning is:
and ask the nations of those of Our messengers whom We sent before you — as the Exalted said
﴿وَاسْأَلِ القَرْيَةَ﴾ — i.e. ask whoever worshipped the angels, or said that Allah is the third
of three, or worshipped other than Allah, Majestic and Mighty: did he find this in any of the books
of the prophets that Allah sent down to them? For he will not find in the book of any prophet that Allah commanded
that other than Him be worshipped. So in this there is the sense of making them acknowledge, rebuke, and making them stand to account for the fact that they
have disbelieved and done what Allah did not command. Its parallel is the saying of the Exalted ﴿قُلْ فَأْتُوا
بِالتَّوْرَاةِ فَاتْلُوهَا إنْ كُنْتُمْ صَادِقِينَ﴾.
What confirms this view is that ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam narrated from al-Ḍaḥḥāk,
who said: In the reading of ʿAbd Allāh it is ﴿وَاسْأَلِ الَّذِينَ يَقْرَءُونَ الكِتَابَ مِنْ
قَبْلِكَ﴾; he said: meaning the People of the Book.
Sufyān narrated from Ibn Abī Najīḥ, from Mujāhid, who said: in the reading of ʿAbd Allāh: ﴿واسْأَلْ مَنْ أَرْسَلْنَا إلَيْهِمْ قَبْلَكَ رُسُلَنَا﴾ — so this is an explanatory reading.
Qatāda said: that is, ask the People of the Book: did Allah command anything but the affirmation of His oneness and sincere devotion?
Ibn Qutayba claimed that the implied structure is: and ask those to whom We sent before you
messengers of Our messengers; so "ilayhi" (to whom) was omitted because the speech indicates it, and "rusulan" (messengers) was omitted because ﴿مِنْ رُسُلِنَا﴾ indicates it. And he claimed that the address is
to the Prophet ﷺ while those intended are the polytheists.

nahhas-meani:49-49.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿وَقَالُواْ يَٰأَيُّهَ ٱلسَّاحِرُ ٱدْعُ لَنَا رَبَّكَ بِمَا عَهِدَ عِندَكَ إِنَّنَا لَمُهْتَدُونَ﴾.
It may be asked: How could they say to him ﴿أَيُّهَ ٱلسَّاحِرُ﴾ when they said ﴿إِنَّنَا لَمُهْتَدُونَ﴾ regarding the future?
It was answered: when they said this to him — before he prayed for them — they knew him by it, so they addressed him by it.
And it was said: they used to call scholars "sorcerers", so the meaning is: O scholar.
Mujāhid said concerning the saying of the Exalted ﴿بِمَا عَهِدَ عِندَكَ﴾: that if we
believe, He will remove the punishment from us.
Abū Jaʿfar said: What indicates the correctness of this answer is the saying of the Exalted
﴿فَلَمَّا كَشَفْنَا عَنْهُمُ العَذَابَ إذَا هُمْ يَنْكُثُونَ﴾, i.e. they break the covenant.
And Saʿīd narrated from Qatāda: ﴿إذَا هُمْ يَنْكُثُونَ﴾: he said: they act treacherously.

nahhas-meani:51-51.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿وَنَادَىٰ فِرْعَوْنُ فِي قَوْمِهِ قَالَ يٰقَوْمِ أَلَيْسَ لِي مُلْكُ مِصْرَ وَهَـٰذِهِ ٱلأَنْهَارُ تَجْرِي مِن تَحْتِيۤ أَفَلاَ تُبْصِرُونَ﴾? [Verse 51].
Al-Akhfash said: There is an omission in the speech, and the meaning is: Do you not see? Or
do you see? As the poet said:
فَيَا ظَبْيَةَ الوَعْسَاءِ بَيْنَ جُلاَجِلٍ * وَبَيْنَ النَّقَا هَلْ أَنْتِ أَمْ أُمُّ سَالِمِ
(O gazelle of the sandy ground between Julājil and the dune: is it you, or Umm Sālim?)
That is: are you more beautiful, or Umm Sālim?
Abū Zayd said: The Arabs add «[Translator's note: i.e. أم as redundant]», and the meaning is: I am better.
And it was said: the meaning is "a-bal" (or rather?).
Abū Jaʿfar said: The best of what has been said about this verse — the view of al-Khalīl
and Sībawayh — is that the meaning is: Do you not see, or are you people of sight? And ﴿أَمْ
أَنَا خَيْرٌ﴾ would mean: or are you better? — because if they had said to him: "You are better," they would have been
people of sight in his view.

nahhas-meani:52-52.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿أَمْ أَنَآ خَيْرٌ مِّنْ هَـٰذَا ٱلَّذِي هُوَ مَهِينٌ وَلاَ يَكَادُ يُبِينُ﴾.
Al-mahīn: the lowly, from mahāna (contemptibility).
Saʿīd narrated from Qatāda: ﴿وَلاَ يَكَادُ يُبِينُ﴾: he said: inarticulate.
And it was said: this was only because of the lisp he had.

nahhas-meani:53-53.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿فَلَوْلاَ أُلْقِيَ عَلَيْهِ أَسَاوِرَةٌ مِّن ذَهَبٍ أَوْ جَآءَ مَعَهُ ٱلْمَلاَئِكَةُ مُقْتَرِنِينَ﴾.
That is, why were bracelets not cast upon him from Allah, indicating that he is
a messenger?!
And ﴿أَسَاوِرَةٌ﴾ is the plural of iswār; in the reading of Ubayy and ʿAbd Allāh: ﴿لَوْلاَ
أُلْقِيَ عَلَيْهِ أَسَاوِيرُ﴾, which has the same meaning as the first.
﴿أَوْ جَآءَ مَعَهُ ٱلْمَلاَئِكَةُ مُقْتَرِنِينَ﴾: Qatāda said: that is, one after another.
Mujāhid said: that is, walking with him together.
Abū Jaʿfar said: So they demanded this after there had come to them what indicated his prophethood.

nahhas-meani:54-54.t:
Then He said, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿فَٱسْتَخَفَّ قَوْمَهُ فَأَطَاعُوهُ إِنَّهُمْ كَانُواْ قَوْماً فَاسِقِينَ﴾.
That is, he incited them [lightly].

nahhas-meani:55-55.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿فَلَمَّآ آسَفُونَا ٱنتَقَمْنَا مِنْهُمْ فَأَغْرَقْنَاهُمْ أَجْمَعِينَ﴾.
Mujāhid and Qatāda said: that is, they angered Us.

nahhas-meani:56-56.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿فَجَعَلْنَاهُمْ سَلَفاً وَمَثَلاً لِّلآخِرِينَ﴾.
Lāḥiq ibn Ḥumayd said: that is, We made them a precedent for those who do as they did, and an example for those who do not do as they did.
Mujāhid said: They are Pharaoh's people, a precedent for the disbelievers of the community of Muḥammad ﷺ; he said: ﴿وَمَثَلاً﴾, that is, a lesson.
Qatāda said: ﴿سَلَفاً﴾: [going ahead] to the Fire; ﴿وَمَثَلاً﴾, that is, an admonition.
It was read before Abū al-Qāsim, the relative of "Aḥmad ibn Manīʿ", from Abū Kāmil
al-Jaḥdarī, from ʿAbd al-Wāḥid, from ʿĀṣim, from Abū Mijlaz: ﴿فَجَعَلْنَاهُمْ سَلَفاً وَمَثَلاً لِّلآخِرِينَ﴾: he said: a precedent for those who do the like of what they did, and an example for those who do not
do the like of what they did.
Abū Jaʿfar said: These views are close to one another. The root meaning of salaf in
the language is what has gone before; from it comes "tasallaftu from so-and-so" (I took an advance from him). The clearest of them is Qatāda's view, i.e.
We made them go ahead in destruction, and an admonition to those who come after them.
And it is read ﴿سُلُفاً﴾, plural of salīf.
And Ḥumayd al-Aʿraj read, according to what is narrated from him, ﴿سُلَفاً﴾, plural of sulfa, i.e.
a group that has gone ahead.
The clearest and most common is with fatḥa on the sīn and the lām, as it is said: So-and-so loves the salaf (predecessors).

nahhas-meani:57-57.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿وَلَمَّا ضُرِبَ ٱبْنُ مَرْيَمَ مَثَلاً إِذَا قَوْمُكَ مِنْهُ يَصِدُّونَ﴾.
Mujāhid said: They said: Muḥammad mentioned "Jesus", Allah's blessings upon them both, only
so that we would give him the rank the Christians give [Jesus].
Qatāda said: When the mention of Jesus was revealed to the Prophet ﷺ, that angered
Quraysh, and they said: Why did you mention Jesus? And they said: He mentioned him only so that we would treat him as the Christians treated Jesus. So Allah, Majestic and Mighty, revealed ﴿مَا ضَرَبُوهُ لَكَ إلاَّ جَدَلاً﴾.
And it was said: this was revealed about "Ibn al-Zibaʿrā": when Allah the Exalted revealed
﴿إنَّكُمْ وَمَا تَعْبُدُونَ مِنْ دُونِ اللهِ حَصَبُ جَهَنَّمَ أَنْتُمْ لَهَا
وَارِدُونَ﴾ he said: But the Christians worship the Messiah?? He, Majestic and Mighty, said ﴿مَا
ضَرَبُوهُ لَكَ إلاَّ جَدَلاً﴾, i.e. they knew that the Messiah was not meant by this, but only the idols they used to worship were meant by it.
* And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿إِذَا قَوْمُكَ مِنْهُ يَصِدُّونَ﴾.
Sufyān and Shuʿba narrated from ʿĀṣim, from Abū Razīn, from Ibn
ʿAbbās: ﴿إِذَا قَوْمُكَ مِنْهُ يَصِدُّونَ﴾: he said: they clamour.
And it is read ﴿يَصُدُّونَ﴾ with ḍamma on the ṣād; al-Nakhaʿī said: that is, they turn away.
Al-Kisāʾī said: They are two dialectal forms with one meaning.
Some lexicographers rejected the ḍamma, saying: if it were "yaṣuddūn",
it would be "ʿanhu" and not "minhu".
Abū Jaʿfar said: This does not follow, because the meaning of "yaṣuddūna minhu" is: on account of it.

nahhas-meani:58-58.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿وَقَالُوۤاْ أَآلِهَتُنَا خَيْرٌ أَمْ هُوَ؟﴾.
Qatāda said: ["Or he" — they mean Muḥammad ﷺ.] And in the reading of "Ubayy": ﴿وَقَالُوا أَأَلِهَتُنَا خَيْرٌ أَمْ هَذَا﴾, meaning Muḥammad ﷺ.
* Then He said, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿مَا ضَرَبُوهُ لَكَ إِلاَّ جَدَلاً﴾.
The meaning according to Qatāda's interpretation: they knew that you did not want them to give you the rank of the Messiah.
And according to the other view: they knew that by His saying, Majestic and Mighty,
﴿إنَّكُمْ وَمَا تَعْبُدُونَ مِنْ دُونِ اللهِ حَصَبُ جَهَنَّمَ﴾ the Messiah, peace be upon
him, was not meant, but only the idols were meant. And the language indicates this, because "mā" is for what
does not reason, so it is known that the meaning of ﴿وَمَا تَعْبُدُونَ مِنْ دُونِ اللهِ﴾ cannot
apply to the Messiah.
This is the soundest of what has been said about the saying of the Exalted ﴿إنَّكُمْ وَمَا تَعْبُدُونَ مِنْ
دُونِ اللهِ حَصَبُ جَهَنَّمَ﴾.
* Then He said, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿بَلْ هُمْ قَوْمٌ خَصِمُونَ﴾.
Sufyān said: A man told me that it was revealed about Ibn al-Zibaʿrā.

nahhas-meani:59-59.t:
Then He said, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿إِنْ هُوَ إِلاَّ عَبْدٌ أَنْعَمْنَا عَلَيْهِ وَجَعَلْنَاهُ مَثَلاً لِّبَنِيۤ إِسْرَائِيلَ﴾.
The meaning, according to those who said the verse was revealed about Ibn
al-Zibaʿrā, would be: the Messiah is nothing but a servant whom We favoured and made an example for the Children
of Israel, i.e. We made him an admonition for them, i.e. a source of admonition, i.e. he admonishes them.
And it is possible that the meaning of ﴿مَثَلاً﴾ is that he is a human being like them, who was given preference over them.
And it is possible that the meaning, according to Qatāda's view and also according to the other, is: Muḥammad
is nothing but a servant whom We favoured and made an example for the Children of Israel; and what is said about
"mathal" is as was said about it [above].

nahhas-meani:60-60.t:
Then He said, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿وَلَوْ نَشَآءُ لَجَعَلْنَا مِنكُمْ مَّلاَئِكَةً فِي ٱلأَرْضِ يَخْلُفُونَ﴾.
Mujāhid said: that is, they would inhabit it as you inhabit it, in place of you.
Qatāda said: that is, angels succeeding one another.

nahhas-meani:61-61.t:
Then He said, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿وَإِنَّهُ لَعِلْمٌ لِّلسَّاعَةِ فَلاَ تَمْتَرُنَّ بِهَا﴾.
Sufyān narrated from ʿĀṣim, from Abū Razīn, from Ibn ʿAbbās:
﴿وَإِنَّهُ لَعِلْمٌ لِّلسَّاعَةِ﴾: he said: the descent of Jesus.
Likewise Simāk narrated it from ʿIkrima, from Ibn ʿAbbās.
And likewise said Mujāhid and Abū Mālik.
And it is narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās and Abū Hurayra that they read ﴿وَإنَّهُ لَعَلَمٌ
لِلسَّاعَةِ﴾.
Al-Khalīl said: ʿalam and ʿalāma (sign) are the same.
Abū Jaʿfar said: The meaning of ﴿لَعِلْمٌ لِّلسَّاعَةِ﴾ is: by the descent of
Jesus ﷺ it will be known that the Hour has drawn near.
And it is authentically reported from the Prophet ﷺ that he said: "The son of Mary will surely descend as a just
judge, and he will break the cross and kill the swine…"
And it is possible that the meaning is: and Muḥammad ﷺ is a sign of the Hour, because he is
the Seal of the Prophets; Allah, Majestic and Mighty, said ﴿اقْتَرَبَتِ السَّاعَةُ وَانْشَقَّ
القَمَرُ﴾.
* Then the Exalted said: ﴿فَلاَ تَمْتَرُنَّ بِهَا﴾: that is, do not doubt.

nahhas-meani:63-63.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿وَلَمَّا جَآءَ عِيسَىٰ بِٱلْبَيِّنَاتِ قَالَ قَدْ جِئْتُكُم بِٱلْحِكْمَةِ وَلأُبَيِّنَ لَكُم بَعْضَ ٱلَّذِي تَخْتَلِفُونَ فِيهِ﴾.
Ibn Abī Najīḥ narrated from Mujāhid: ﴿وَلأُبَيِّنَ لَكُم بَعْضَ ٱلَّذِي تَخْتَلِفُونَ فِيهِ﴾: he said: the alteration of the Torah.

nahhas-meani:67-67.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿ٱلأَخِلاَّءُ يَوْمَئِذٍ بَعْضُهُمْ لِبَعْضٍ عَدُوٌّ إِلاَّ ٱلْمُتَّقِينَ﴾.
Mujāhid said: The people of sins will be enemies to one another on the Day of Resurrection.
Al-Ḥārith said: ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib was asked about His saying, Majestic and Mighty,
﴿ٱلأَخِلاَّءُ يَوْمَئِذٍ بَعْضُهُمْ لِبَعْضٍ عَدُوٌّ﴾, and he said: Two believing close friends and two disbelieving close friends. One of the two believers died and was given the glad tidings of Paradise, and he said: O Allah, do not
let my friend go astray, until he is given the glad tidings I was given, and You are pleased with him as You were pleased
with me. When [the other] died, they were brought together, and he said to him: May Allah reward you well as a friend,
a brother and a companion; what an excellent friend you were!
And of the two disbelievers, one says to the other: What an evil friend and companion
you were! Then he recited ﴿ٱلأَخِلاَّءُ يَوْمَئِذٍ بَعْضُهُمْ لِبَعْضٍ عَدُوٌّ إِلاَّ ٱلْمُتَّقِينَ﴾.
And Mujāhid said: Ibn ʿAbbās said: Love for Allah's sake, hate for Allah's sake, befriend for Allah's sake and take as enemy for Allah's sake; for what is with Allah is attained only through this, and no one will benefit from
much fasting, prayer and pilgrimage until he is like this. Yet today
people love and hate for the sake of this world, and that will not benefit its people. Then he recited
﴿ٱلأَخِلاَّءُ يَوْمَئِذٍ بَعْضُهُمْ لِبَعْضٍ عَدُوٌّ إِلاَّ ٱلْمُتَّقِينَ﴾.

nahhas-meani:70-70.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿ٱدْخُلُواْ ٱلْجَنَّةَ أَنتُمْ وَأَزْوَاجُكُمْ تُحْبَرُونَ﴾.
Yaḥyā ibn Abī Kathīr said: The Prophet ﷺ was asked about the saying of the Exalted ﴿أَنتُمْ وَأَزْوَاجُكُمْ تُحْبَرُونَ﴾ and he said: "Delight, and listening to whatever Allah wills of His remembrance."
Qatāda said: ﴿تُحْبَرُونَ﴾: you will be made to enjoy bliss.

nahhas-meani:71-71.t:
Then He said, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿يُطَافُ عَلَيْهِمْ بِصِحَافٍ مِّن ذَهَبٍ وَأَكْوَابٍ﴾.
Saʿīd narrated from Qatāda, who said: The akwāb are smaller than the ewers (abārīq). He said:
And it has reached me that they are round; and so they are according to the lexicographers, except that they have no ears [spouts]
and no handles.

nahhas-meani:75-75.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿لاَ يُفَتَّرُ عَنْهُمْ وَهُمْ فِيهِ مُبْلِسُونَ﴾.
It is taken from al-fatra, al-futūr and al-fatr (abatement).
And al-mublis is the bewildered one who has despaired of any good.

nahhas-meani:77-77.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿وَنَادَوْاْ يٰمَالِكُ لِيَقْضِ عَلَيْنَا رَبُّكَ قَالَ إِنَّكُمْ مَّاكِثُونَ﴾.
Mujāhid said: We did not know what ﴿وَنَادَوْاْ يٰمَالِكُ﴾ meant
until we found in the reading of ʿAbd Allāh ﴿وَنَادَوْا يَا مَالِ﴾.
ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ said: They will call Mālik for forty years, then he will answer them after that: ﴿إِنَّكُمْ مَّاكِثُونَ﴾. Then they will call the Lord of Might: ﴿رَبَّنَا
أَخْرِجْنَا مِنْهَا فَإنْ عُدْنَا فَإنَّا ظَالِمُونَ﴾, and He will remain silent towards them for the like of the lifespan
of the world; then He will say: ﴿اخْسَئُوا فِيهَا وَلا تُكَلِّمُونِ﴾. He said: After that there will be
nothing but braying like the braying of donkeys, beginning with a sighing out (zafīr) and ending with a gasping in (shahīq).

nahhas-meani:79-79.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿أَمْ أَبْرَمُوۤاْ أَمْراً فَإِنَّا مُبْرِمُونَ﴾.
Mujāhid said: that is, or have they agreed upon a plot or an evil? Then We shall plot against them.
Al-Farrāʾ said: that is, or have they firmly settled a matter that will save them from Our punishment, as they claim? Then We shall punish them.
Abū Jaʿfar said: It is said "abrama al-amr" when one goes to great lengths in making it firm; and "abrama" is said of the rope-twister when he makes the twist firm, which is the second twisting, the first being saḥīl, as
the poet said:
 * "مِنْ سَحِيلٍ وَمُبْرَمِ" *
(Of single-twisted and double-twisted [rope].)
And from it: a man is baram when he does not take part in maysir (the gambling with arrows), or when he is ill-
natured and does not mix with people, as the poet said:
وَلاَ بَرَماً تُهْدَى النَّسَاءُ لِعِرْسِهِ * إذَا القَشْعُ مِنْ بَرُدِ الشِّتَاءِ تَقَعْقَعَا
(Nor a niggard whose wife has to be sent [food] by the women, when the dry hide rattles with the winter cold.)
And "burma" (stone cooking-pot) is from this; it was so named because of the insistent kindling of fire under it.

nahhas-meani:81-81.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿قُلْ إِن كَانَ لِلرَّحْمَـٰنِ وَلَدٌ فَأَنَاْ أَوَّلُ ٱلْعَابِدِينَ﴾.
There are three views on its meaning:
a- Mujāhid said: that is, say: if the Most Merciful had a son — according to what you say — then I would be
the first to worship Him, affirm His oneness, and declare you liars.
b- Al-Ḥasan said: He is saying: the Most Merciful has no son.
c- And it was said: it is from ʿabida, i.e. to disdain, as the poet said:
* "وأَعْبَدُ أَنْ تُهْجَى تَمِيمٌ بَدَارِمِ" *
(And I disdain that Tamīm be lampooned by [mention of] Dārim.)
Abū Jaʿfar said: The best of them is Mujāhid's view, because it is unlikely that "in"
here means "mā" (not), since that is hardly ever used without "illā" coming after "in".
Moreover, there is an alif after it «[Translator's note: i.e. the word is العابدين, with an alif after the ʿayn]», whereas what is mostly said, when a person disdains,
is angry and rejects something, is: ʿabida, so he is ʿabid — as it is said: ḥadhira, so he is ḥadhir.
And Mujāhid's view is clear, i.e. if the Most Merciful had a son — according to your claim
and your saying — as the Exalted said ﴿أَيْنَ شُرَكَائِي﴾? — then I would be the first to
oppose you and affirm the oneness of Allah, Majestic and Mighty.
And the meaning of ﴿ٱلْعَابِدِينَ﴾ is like the meaning of "those who affirm the oneness [of Allah]", because "worshipper" is said only of one who affirms His oneness.

nahhas-meani:84-84.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿وَهُوَ ٱلَّذِي فِي ٱلسَّمآءِ إِلَـٰهٌ وَفِي ٱلأَرْضِ إِلَـٰهٌ وَهُوَ ٱلْحَكِيمُ ٱلْعَلِيمُ﴾.
Qatāda said: that is, He is worshipped in the heaven and in the earth.
And it is narrated from ʿUmar, Ubayy and Ibn Masʿūd: ﴿وَهُوَ الَّذِي فِي
السَّمَاءِ اللهُ وَفي الأرضِ اللهُ﴾.

nahhas-meani:86-86.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿وَلاَ يَمْلِكُ ٱلَّذِينَ يَدْعُونَ مِن دُونِهِ ٱلشَّفَاعَةَ إِلاَّ مَن شَهِدَ بِٱلْحَقِّ﴾.
Qatāda said: The Messiah and ʿUzayr were worshipped besides Allah, and they have intercession.
Mujāhid said: The Messiah, ʿUzayr and the angels intercede only for those who
bore witness to the truth; he said: "There is no god but Allah."
Abū Jaʿfar said: Qatāda's view is clearer, and Mujāhid's view is on the basis that it is an exception
not of the same kind as the first (istithnāʾ munqaṭiʿ).

nahhas-meani:88-88.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿وَقِيلِهِ يٰرَبِّ إِنَّ هَـٰؤُلاَءِ قَوْمٌ لاَّ يُؤْمِنُونَ﴾.
We shall explain the meaning of ﴿وَقِيلِهِ يٰرَبِّ﴾ in the I'rab [book], if Allah wills.

nahhas-meani:89-89.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿فَٱصْفَحْ عَنْهُمْ وَقُلْ سَلاَمٌ فَسَوْفَ يَعْلَمُونَ﴾.
Qatāda said concerning His saying ﴿فَٱصْفَحْ عَنْهُمْ﴾: This was said to him, then it was
abrogated by the command to fight.

safi-cedvel:36-38.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive; (من) a jussive conditional noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject); (عن ذكر) attached to (mutaʿalliq) (يعش); (له) attached to (نقيّض); (الفاء) conjunction; the second (له) attached to (قرين).
The clause «من يعش ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «يعش» is in the position of nominative as khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (من) [Note: The khabar may also be the protasis and apodosis clauses together.].
The clause «نقيّض ...» has no grammatical position: apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) not joined with fāʾ.
The clause «هو له قرين» is in the position of accusative, conjoined (maʿṭūf) to an implied clause which is a naʿt (adjective) of (شيطانا), i.e.: a devil who tempts him, and so he is a companion to him.
37- (الواو) conjunction; (اللام) the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa), for emphasis; (عن السبيل) attached to (يصدّونهم) ... (الواو) circumstantial (ḥāliyya).
The interpreted maṣdar (أنّهم مهتدون) is in the position of accusative, standing in place of the two objects of يحسبون; the pronoun in it refers back to (العاشين), "those who turn away", in His words: من يعش ...
The clause «إنّهم ليصدون» is in the position of accusative, conjoined to the clause هو له قرين.
The clause «يصدّون ...» is in the position of nominative as khabar of إنّ.
The clause «يحسبون ...» is in the position of accusative as ḥāl (circumstantial).
38- (حتّى) a particle of commencement (ḥarf ibtidāʾ); (يا) for drawing attention (tanbīh); (بيني) an accusative adverb (ẓarf), attached to an omitted khabar of ليت; (بينك) an accusative adverb conjoined to the first adverb; (بعد) the noun of ليت, accusative; (الفاء) linking the apodosis of an implied condition; (القرين) fāʿil (agent) of بئس.
The one specified for blame (al-makhṣūṣ bi-l-dhamm) is omitted, its implied form being "أنت".
The clause «جاءنا ...» is in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «قال ...» has no grammatical position: apodosis of a non-jussive condition.
The clause «ليت بيني ... بعد» is in the position of accusative as the object of speech (maqūl al-qawl).
The clause «بئس القرين» is in the position of jussive as apodosis of an implied condition, i.e.: if I took you as a companion, then how evil a companion you are.

* Morphology:
(36) يعش: it contains iʿlāl (weak-letter change) by deletion on account of the jussive. Its pattern is يفع with ḍamma on the ʿayn, because the deleted letter is a wāw. عشا يعشو means "he turned away".

* Rhetoric:
1- The indefinite noun occurring in the context of a condition: in the words of Allah the Exalted «وَمَنْ يَعْشُ عَنْ ذِكْرِ الرَّحْمنِ نُقَيِّضْ لَهُ شَيْطاناً». In this noble verse there is a fine subtlety, namely that an indefinite noun occurring in the context of a condition conveys generality, since He intended devils in general, not a single one; that is because He referred back to it with a plural pronoun in the following verse, in His words «وإنهم», which refers back to the devil without disagreement.
2- Taghlīb (giving one term predominance over another): in the words of Allah the Exalted «بُعْدَ الْمَشْرِقَيْنِ».
This figure is to let one thing predominate over what belongs to another, by applying its name to the other and putting it in the dual on that basis, because of the correspondence between them.
In the verse "the two easts" (المشرقين) are mentioned, while the east and the west are meant; but the east was given predominance over the west and the two were put in the dual, as in their saying الأبوين ("the two fathers") for the father and the mother. Of this kind are the words of Allah the Exalted «وَلِأَبَوَيْهِ لِكُلِّ واحِدٍ مِنْهُمَا السُّدُسُ», and their saying القمرين ("the two moons") for the sun and the moon.
Similar is الخافقان for the east and the west, whereas the خافق is properly the west; moreover it was only called خافق figuratively, for it is really the place in which [the sun] sets (مخفوق فيه); and القمرين for the sun and the moon. It is said that of this kind is the verse of al-Farazdaq:
أخذنا بآفاق السماء عليكم ... لنا قمراها والنجوم الطوالع
(We have taken the horizons of the sky against you: ours are its two moons and the rising stars.)
It is also said that by the "two moons" he meant Muhammad and al-Khalīl [Abraham], upon both be blessings and peace, because his lineage goes back to both of them in some way, and that the stars meant are the Companions. They also said العمرين ("the two ʿUmars") for Abū Bakr and ʿUmar, العجّاجين for Ruʾba and al-ʿAjjāj, and المروتين for al-Ṣafā and al-Marwa.
Because of mixing [of rational and non-rational beings], (من) was applied to what is not rational in the words of Allah the Exalted: فَمِنْهُمْ مَنْ يَمْشِي عَلى بَطْنِهِ وَمِنْهُمْ مَنْ يَمْشِي عَلى رِجْلَيْنِ وَمِنْهُمْ مَنْ يَمْشِي عَلى أَرْبَعٍ, for the mixing is present in the preceding general term in the words of Allah the Exalted (كُلَّ دَابَّةٍ مِنْ ماءٍ). Likewise the name of "the masculine ones" was applied to a female so that she was counted among them — Maryam daughter of ʿImrān, may Allah be pleased with them both — in the words of Allah the Exalted وَكانَتْ مِنَ الْقانِتِينَ; and the angels [were made predominant] over Iblīs so that he was excepted from them in (فَسَجَدُوا إِلَّا إِبْلِيسَ). Al-Zamakhsharī said: the exception is connected (muttaṣil), because he was a single one in the midst of thousands of angels, so they were made predominant over him in (فسجدوا), and then he was excepted from them as one of them is excepted. Then he said: the exception may also be disconnected (munqaṭiʿ).

* Benefits:
- A stylistic point.
In this verse occur the words of Allah the Exalted وَإِنَّهُمْ لَيَصُدُّونَهُمْ عَنِ السَّبِيلِ وَيَحْسَبُونَ أَنَّهُمْ مُهْتَدُونَ. He combined in the plural the pronoun of (من) and the pronoun of the devil occurring in the previous verse, because (من) is indefinite (mubham), covering the genus of the one who turns away, and an indefinite devil of his kind has been assigned to him, so it was permissible for the pronoun to refer back to both of them in the plural.

safi-cedvel:39-39.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive; (اليوم) an accusative adverb of time, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (ينفعكم); (إذ) an adverb of past time, attached to (ينفعكم) on the implied reading: "when your wrongdoing has become clear" [Note: Were it not for this implied reading, attaching it to (ينفعكم) would not be correct, because that is for the future and إذ is for the past.. and it may be] [Translator's note: the footnote breaks off here in the source.]; (في العذاب) attached to (مشتركون).
The interpreted maṣdar (أنّكم في العذاب مشتركون) is in the position of nominative as fāʿil (agent) of ينفعكم, i.e.: your sharing in the punishment will not benefit you by way of consolation [Note: The fāʿil may be a latent (mustatir) pronoun referring to the wishing understood from the context in His words: ليت بيني ...; the interpreted maṣdar is then in the position of genitive by an implied lām, attached to (ينفعكم), i.e.: the wishing will not benefit you, because you are sharers in the punishment.].

safi-cedvel:40-40.t:
* I'rab:
(الهمزة) for the interrogative of wonder; (الفاء) resumptive; (أو، الواو) both conjunctions; (من) a relative noun in the position of accusative, conjoined (maʿṭūf) to العمي; (في ضلال) attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar of كان.
The clause «أنت تسمع ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «تسمع ...» is in the position of nominative as khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject) (أنت).
The clause «تهدي ...» is in the position of nominative, conjoined to the clause تسمع.
The clause «كان في ضلال ...» has no grammatical position: ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (من).

safi-cedvel:41-42.t:
* I'rab:
(الفاء) resumptive; (إن) a jussive conditional particle; (ما) redundant (zāʾida); (نذهبنّ) an imperfect verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on fatḥa, in the position of jussive as protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); (بك) attached to (mutaʿalliq) (نذهبنّ); (الفاء) linking the apodosis in both verses; (منهم) attached to the khabar (predicate) (منتقمون).
The clause «نذهبنّ ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «إنّا منهم منتقمون» is in the position of jussive as apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), joined with fāʾ.
42- (أو) a conjunction; (نرينّك) like نذهبنّ, and conjoined to it [Note: Or it is the protasis of an implied conditional particle.]; (الذي) a relative noun in the position of accusative as second mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (إنّا عليهم مقتدرون) like إنّا منهم منتقمون.
The clause «نرينّك ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause نذهبنّ ...
The clause «وعدناهم ...» has no grammatical position: ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (الذي).
The clause «إنّا عليهم مقتدرون» is in the position of jussive as apodosis, joined with fāʾ, and it is conjoined to the previous apodosis by (أو).

safi-cedvel:43-45.t:
* I'rab:
(الفاء) linking the apodosis of an implied condition; (بالذي) attached to (mutaʿalliq) (استمسك); (إليك) attached to (أوحي), and the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) is the resumptive pronoun (al-ʿāʾid); (على صراط) attached to the khabar of إنّ.
The clause «استمسك ...» is in the position of jussive as apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of an implied condition, i.e.: if the revelation has come to you, then hold fast.
The clause «أوحي إليك ...» has no grammatical position: ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (الذي).
The clause «إنّك على صراط ...» has no grammatical position: causal (taʿlīliyya).
44- (الواو) conjunction; (اللام) the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa), for emphasis; (لك) attached to (ذكر), and likewise (لقومك); (الواو) parenthetical, and the wāw in (تسألون) is the nāʾib fāʿil.
The clause «إنّه لذكر ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the causal clause.
The clause «سوف تسألون ...» has no grammatical position: parenthetical.
45- (الواو) conjunction; (من) a relative noun in the position of accusative as mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (من قبلك) attached to (أرسلنا); (من رسلنا) a tamyīz (specification) of the relative noun — or a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the implied resumptive pronoun —; (الهمزة) for the interrogative of denial (inkārī); (من دون) attached to an omitted second mafʿūl bihi.
The clause «اسأل ...» is in the position of jussive, conjoined to the clause استمسك.
The clause «أرسلنا ...» has no grammatical position: ṣila of the relative noun (من).
The clause «جعلنا ...» has no grammatical position: an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī).
The clause «يعبدون» is in the position of accusative as naʿt (adjective) of آلهة.

* Rhetoric:
Majāz (figurative usage): in the words of Allah the Exalted «وَسْئَلْ مَنْ أَرْسَلْنا مِنْ قَبْلِكَ مِنْ رُسُلِنا».
He directed the asking at the messengers, although what is meant is their nations and the scholars of their religions, as in the words of Allah the Exalted «فَسْئَلِ الَّذِينَ يَقْرَؤُنَ الْكِتابَ مِنْ قَبْلِكَ». The benefit of this figure is to point out that what is asked about is what the tongues of the messengers uttered, not what their nations and scholars say of their own accord.
For they only inform him about the Book of the messengers, so if he asks them, it is as though he asked the prophets, upon them be peace.

safi-cedvel:46-48.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive; (اللام) the lām of the oath, for an implied oath; (قد) a particle of realisation (taḥqīq); (بآياتنا) attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) of موسى; (إلى فرعون) attached to (أرسلنا); (الفاء) conjunction.
The clause «أرسلنا ...» has no grammatical position: the answer to the implied oath; the implied oath clause is resumptive.
The clause «قال ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause answering the oath.
The clause «إنّي رسول ...» is in the position of accusative as the object of speech (maqūl al-qawl).
47- (الفاء) conjunction; (لمّا) an adverb meaning "when", containing the sense of a condition, attached to the content of the apodosis; (بآياتنا) attached to a ḥāl of the fāʿil (agent) of جاءهم, which is a pronoun referring to موسى; (إذا) of surprise (fujāʾiyya); (منها) attached to (يضحكون).
The clause «جاءهم ...» is in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «هم منها يضحكون» has no grammatical position: apodosis of a non-jussive condition.
The clause «يضحكون» is in the position of nominative as khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject) (هم).
48- (الواو) conjunction in both places; (ما) negative; (آية) genitive in form, accusative in position, as second mafʿūl bihi (direct object) — the seeing being visual —; (إلّا) for restriction (ḥaṣr); (من أختها) attached to (أكبر); (بالعذاب) attached to a ḥāl of the third-person pronoun in (أخذناهم).
The clause «ما نريهم ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause answering the oath [Note: The clause may be parenthetical between two conjoined elements.. the clause أخذناهم [being conjoined] to the resumptive clause.].
The clause «هي أكبر ...» is in the position of accusative as ḥāl of آية.
The clause «أخذناهم ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to an implied resumption, i.e.:
So We took vengeance on them and seized them ...
The clause «لعلّهم يرجعون» has no grammatical position: an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī).
The clause «يرجعون» is in the position of nominative as khabar of لعلّ.

* Rhetoric:
Comprehensive and exclusive speech (al-kalām al-jāmiʿ al-māniʿ): in the words of Allah the Exalted «وَما نُرِيهِمْ مِنْ آيَةٍ إِلَّا هِيَ أَكْبَرُ مِنْ أُخْتِها».
That is, each one of these signs, when you consider it alone, its greatness absorbs and dazzles the mind, until one is certain that it is the utmost, and that every other sign is below it. Then when one moves one's thought to its sister, it too fills one's mind with its greatness, and one forgets the first, and is certain that this is the utmost and that every other sign is below it. The upshot is that the mind is unable to hold two of the signs together so as to establish which is superior and which inferior; rather, whichever one it considers alone, it is certain that it is the utmost.
Everything of this kind that occurs follows this interpretation.

* Benefits:
- Omission of the adjective.
Among the styles of the Arabs is that they omit the adjective in the course of speech when it is understood. This occurs in the noble verse under discussion, in the words of Allah the Exalted وَما نُرِيهِمْ مِنْ آيَةٍ إِلَّا هِيَ أَكْبَرُ مِنْ أُخْتِها.
That is, than its preceding sister. This occurs in several places in the Noble Quran, such as: (يَأْخُذُ كُلَّ سَفِينَةٍ غَصْباً), i.e. every sound ship, as shown by the fact that it was also read that way. Of this kind is (تُدَمِّرُ كُلَّ شَيْءٍ), i.e. everything it was sent against; and (قالُوا الْآنَ جِئْتَ بِالْحَقِّ), i.e. the clear [truth]. It also occurs in poetry; al-ʿAbbās ibn Mirdās said:
وقد كنت في الحرب ذا تدرأ ... فلم أعط شيئا ولم أمنع
(I was a man of force in war, yet I was given nothing and was not withheld.)
The implied sense is: and I was not given anything worthwhile. Of this kind is the saying of ʿImrān ibn Ḥiṭṭān:
وليس لعيشنا هذا مهاه ... وليس دارنا هاتا بدار
(This life of ours has no beauty, and this abode of ours is no abode.)
The implied sense is: no lasting abode. مهاه means beauty, and تدرأ means strength. Of this kind are the words of Allah the Exalted قُلْ يا أَهْلَ الْكِتابِ لَسْتُمْ عَلى شَيْءٍ, i.e. anything beneficial, and (إن نظن إلا ظنا), i.e. a weak supposition.

safi-cedvel:49-49.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive; (لنا) attached to (mutaʿalliq) (ادع); (بما) attached to (ادع), and (الباء) is causal [Note: ما is a relative noun, and the resumptive pronoun (al-ʿāʾid) is omitted, indicating the supplication.. or it is a maṣdar-forming particle.]; (عندك) an accusative adverb (ẓarf), attached to (عهد); (اللام) the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa), for emphasis.
The clause «قالوا ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «the vocative and its answer ...» is in the position of accusative as the object of speech (maqūl al-qawl).
The clause «ادع ...» has no grammatical position: answer to the vocative.
The clause «عهد ...» has no grammatical position: ṣila (relative clause) of (ما), whether nominal or particle.
The clause «إنّنا لمهتدون» has no grammatical position: an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī) [Note: There is an omission in the speech, i.e.: call upon your Lord for us to remove the punishment from us.. It is as though Mūsā asks them: what will your stance be then? And the answer is: إنّنا لمهتدون.].

safi-cedvel:50-50.t:
* I'rab:
The i'rab of its counterpart [Note: In verse (47) of this sura.] has already been given, both words and clauses.

safi-cedvel:51-56.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive; (في قومه) attached to (mutaʿalliq) (نادى); (قوم) a muḍāf vocative (munādā), accusative, the sign of the accusative being the fatḥa implied (muqaddar) on the letter before the first-person yāʾ, which is deleted for lightness; (الهمزة) for the interrogative of affirmation (taqrīrī); (ليّ) attached to the khabar of ليس; (الواو) circumstantial (ḥāliyya) [Note: Or conjunctive, conjoining the demonstrative to ملك.. and the clause تجري is a ḥāl.]; (هذه) a demonstrative, mubtadaʾ (subject), whose khabar (predicate) is the clause تجري; (الأنهار) a badal (substitute) of the demonstrative — or an ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition) to it —; (من تحتي) attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the fāʿil (agent) of تجري, with a muḍāf omitted, i.e. from beneath my palace; (الهمزة) for the interrogative of denial (inkārī); (الفاء) conjunction; (لا) negative.
The clause «نادى فرعون ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «قال ...» has no grammatical position: an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī).
The clause «the vocative and its answer ...» is in the position of accusative as the object of speech (maqūl al-qawl).
The clause «أليس لي ملك مصر ...» has no grammatical position: answer to the vocative.
The clause «هذه الأنهار تجري» is in the position of accusative as ḥāl.
The clause «تجري ...» is in the position of nominative as khabar of the mubtadaʾ (هذه).
The clause «لا تبصرون» has no grammatical position, conjoined (maʿṭūf) to an implied resumption, i.e.:
Have you become heedless, so that you do not see?
