52- (أم) is the disconnected one (al-munqaṭiʿa) meaning بل, for transitional digression (iḍrāb intiqālī) [Note: Ibn Hishām permitted making it connected (muttaṣila), so that it conjoins the clause أنا خير to the clause لا تبصرون, because the clause أنا خير means "you see"; Ibn Hishām follows al-Zamakhsharī in this.]; (من هذا) attached to (خير); (الذي) a relative noun in the position of genitive as badal of the demonstrative.
The clause «أنا خير ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «هو مهين ...» has no grammatical position: ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (الذي).
The clause «لا يكاد يبين» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the ṣila clause.
The clause «يبين» is in the position of accusative as khabar of يكاد.
53- (الفاء) linking the apodosis of an implied condition; (لولا) a particle of urging (taḥḍīḍ); (عليه) attached to (ألقي); (من ذهب) attached to a naʿt (adjective) of (أسورة); (معه) an accusative adverb, attached to a ḥāl of الملائكة [Note: Or attached to (جاء).]; (مقترنين) an accusative ḥāl of الملائكة, the sign of the accusative being the yāʾ.
The clause «ألقي عليه أسورة» is in the position of jussive as apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of an implied condition, i.e.: if he is truthful, then why have not been placed ...
The clause «جاء معه الملائكة ...» is in the position of jussive, conjoined to the clause ألقي.
54- (الفاء) conjunction in both places; (فاسقين) a naʿt of (قوما), accusative, the sign of the accusative being the yāʾ.
The clause «استخف ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause نادى فرعون.. or to the clause قال, with what lies between the two clauses being the object of speech.
The clause «أطاعوه» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause استخفّ.
The clause «إنّهم كانوا قوما ...» has no grammatical position: causal (taʿlīliyya).
The clause «كانوا قوما ...» is in the position of nominative as khabar of إنّ.
55- (الفاء) conjunction; (لمّا) an adverb meaning "when", containing the sense of a condition, in the position of accusative, attached to the apodosis انتقمنا; (منهم) attached to (انتقمنا); (الفاء) conjunction; (أجمعين) a tawkīd (emphasis) in meaning (maʿnawī) of the third-person pronoun in (أغرقناهم) — or a ḥāl of it —.
The clause «آسفونا ...» is in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «انتقمنا ...» has no grammatical position: apodosis of a non-jussive condition.
The clause «أغرقناهم ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause انتقمنا.
56- (الفاء) conjunction; (سلفا) an accusative second mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (للآخرين) attached to (مثلا).
The clause «جعلناهم ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause أغرقناهم.

* Morphology:
(53) مقترنين: plural of مقترن, an active participle of the five-letter verb اقترن; its pattern is مفتعل with ḍamma on the mīm and kasra on the ʿayn.
(55) آسفونا: in it the fāʾ of the verb [i.e. its first radical] is merged with the hamza of transitivity before it, because the verb is on the pattern أفعل, i.e. أأسف.. the two hamzas came together, the second being vowelless; they were merged and a madda was placed over them.
(56) سلفا: a collective noun (ism jamʿ) with no singular from its own root, meaning "those who went before"; it is also said to be a plural whose singular is سالف, like خدم and خادم; its pattern is فعل with two fatḥas.
(الآخرين): plural of الآخر — with kasra on the khāʾ.. see verse (8) of Sūrat al-Baqara.

* Rhetoric:
Majāz mursal (metonymic figure): in the words of Allah the Exalted «وَنادى فِرْعَوْنُ فِي قَوْمِهِ».
The calling out is attributed to him figuratively; what is meant is that he ordered it to be proclaimed in the markets, the lanes and the gathering places of people. This is like saying: the prince built the city. The relationship here is one of place (maḥalliyya), for He made his people the place of his proclamation and its location, by saying «في قومه», i.e. in their gatherings and places.

safi-cedvel:57-62.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive; (لما) an adverb meaning "when", containing the sense of a condition, in the position of accusative, attached to the content of the apodosis; (ابن) nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); (مثلا) an accusative mafʿūl bihi (direct object), by ضرب being made to carry the meaning of جعل (taḍmīn); (إذا) of surprise (fujāʾiyya); (منه) attached to (mutaʿalliq) (يصدّون).
The clause «ضرب ابن مريم ...» is in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «قومك منه يصدّون» has no grammatical position: apodosis of a non-jussive condition.
The clause «يصدّون» is in the position of nominative as khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject) (قومك).
58- (الواو) conjunction; (الهمزة) interrogative; (أم) a conjunction counterbalancing the hamza; (هو) a detached pronoun in the position of nominative, conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the mubtadaʾ (آلهتنا); (ما) negative; (لك) attached to (ضربوه); (إلّا) for restriction (ḥaṣr); (جدلا) an accusative mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose) [Note: Or an accusative maṣdar in the place of a ḥāl.]; (بل) for transitional digression (iḍrāb intiqālī).
The clause «قالوا ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the apodosis clause.
The clause «آلهتنا خير ...» is in the position of accusative as the object of speech (maqūl al-qawl).
The clause «ما ضربوه ... إلّا جدلا» has no grammatical position: an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī).
The clause «هم قوم ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
59- (إن) a particle of negation; (إلّا) for restriction; (عليه) attached to (أنعمنا); (لبني) attached to a naʿt (adjective) of (مثلا) [Note: Or attached to (جعلناه).].
The clause «إن هو إلّا عبد ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «أنعمنا ...» is in the position of nominative as naʿt of عبد.
The clause «جعلناه ...» is in the position of nominative, conjoined to the clause أنعمنا.
60- (الواو) parenthetical; (لو) a non-jussive conditional particle; (اللام) linking the apodosis; (منكم) in the place of the second object; it is said to be partitive, and it is said to mean "in place of you"; (في الأرض) attached to (جعلنا) — or to (يخلفون) —.
The clause «نشاء ...» has no grammatical position: parenthetical.
The clause «جعلنا ...» has no grammatical position: apodosis of a non-jussive condition.
The clause «يخلفون» is in the position of accusative as naʿt of ملائكة.
61- (الواو) conjunction; the pronoun in (إنّه) refers to ʿĪsā, upon him be peace, with a muḍāf omitted, i.e. his descent [Note: It may refer to the Noble Quran.]; (اللام) the shifted lām (muzaḥlaqa), for emphasis; (للساعة) attached to a naʿt of (علم) — and (اللام) means على, i.e. of the Hour, i.e. of its nearness —; (الفاء) linking the apodosis of an implied condition; (لا) prohibitive, making jussive; (تمترنّ) a jussive imperfect verb, the sign of the jussive being the deletion of the nūn; the wāw, deleted because of the meeting of two vowelless letters, is the fāʿil (agent), and (النون) is for emphasis; (بها) attached to (تمترنّ); the nūn in (اتّبعون) is the nūn of protection (wiqāya) before the first-person yāʾ, which is deleted for lightness.
The clause «إنّه لعلم ...» is in the position of nominative, conjoined to the clause أنعمنا [Note: It may be resumptive, and so have no grammatical position.].
The clause «لا تمترنّ بها» is in the position of jussive as apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of an implied condition, i.e.: if news of it comes to you, then do not doubt it.
The clause «اتّبعون» is in the position of accusative as the object of an implied speech verb [Note: The implied speech clause is resumptive.. The words may also be from the speech of Allah the Exalted, i.e.: follow My guidance, or My law, or My Messenger; the clause is then conjoined to the apodosis.. and the clause لا يصدنّكم is conjoined to the clause اتبعون, likewise having no grammatical position.], i.e.: say to them ...
The clause «هذا صراط ...» has no grammatical position: giving the reason for the preceding command.
62- (الواو) conjunction; (لا يصدنّكم): (لا) prohibitive, (يصدنّكم) an imperfect verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on fatḥa, in the position of jussive, and (النون) is for emphasis; (الشيطان) fāʿil; the verb is indeclinable on fatḥa in the position of jussive; (لكم) attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) of عدوّ ...
The clause «لا يصدنّكم الشيطان» is in the position of accusative, conjoined to the clause اتّبعون.
The clause «إنّه لكم عدو ...» has no grammatical position: causal (taʿlīliyya).

* Morphology:
(خصمون): plural of خصم, a ṣifa mushabbaha (resembling adjective) from the triliteral خصم of the ḍaraba class; its pattern is فعل with fatḥa then kasra.

* Benefits:
- The obstinacy and quibbling of the deniers.
The exegetes relate an engaging story as the occasion of revelation of this verse. Ibn ʿAbbās said: this verse was revealed concerning the dispute of ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Zibaʿrā with the Prophet ﷺ regarding ʿĪsā son of Maryam, upon him be blessings and peace. That was when the words of Allah the Exalted were revealed: إِنَّكُمْ وَما تَعْبُدُونَ مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ حَصَبُ جَهَنَّمَ. Ibn al-Zibaʿrā stood up among a group of his companions, including al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīra and al-Naḍr ibn al-Ḥārith, and they said: O Muhammad, do you not claim that everything worshipped besides Allah is in Hell, as was revealed to you? He said: Yes. They said: The Christians worship ʿĪsā, the Jews worship ʿUzayr, and we worship the angels; if the matter is so, then ʿĪsā, ʿUzayr and the angels are in Hell. He, upon him be blessings and peace, said: That is for everyone who is worshipped besides Allah while being content to be worshipped. Then Allah Mighty and Majestic revealed وَلَمَّا ضُرِبَ ابْنُ مَرْيَمَ مَثَلًا, i.e. the disbelievers of Quraysh struck him as an example of what is worshipped besides Allah and [claimed] that he is in Hell, as mentioned; (إِذا قَوْمُكَ مِنْهُ يَصِدُّونَ), i.e. an uproar, shouting and rejoicing rises from them.

safi-cedvel:63-65.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive; (بالبيّنات) attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) of عيسى «1»; (بالحكمة) attached to a ḥāl of the fāʿil (agent) of جئتكم «2» [Translator's note: the footnotes marked «1» and «2» are not given in the source.]; (الواو) conjunction in both places; (اللام) for giving the reason (taʿlīl); (أبيّن) an imperfect verb, accusative by an implied أن after the lām; (لكم) attached to (أبيّن).
The interpreted maṣdar (أن أبين..) is in the position of genitive by the lām, attached to an omitted verb, its implied form being "جئتكم".
(الذي) a relative noun in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi; (فيه) attached to (تختلفون); (الفاء) linking the apodosis of an implied condition; the (النون) in (أطيعون) is the nūn of protection (wiqāya), coming before the first-person yāʾ, which is deleted to suit the verse-ending (fāṣila).
The clause «جاء عيسى ...» is in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi ... and the conditional clause — its protasis and apodosis — has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «قال ...» has no grammatical position: apodosis of a non-jussive condition.
The clause «قد جئتكم ...» is in the position of accusative as the object of speech (maqūl al-qawl).
The clause «أبيّن ...» has no grammatical position: ṣila of the implied particle-relative (أن).
The clause «تختلفون ...» has no grammatical position: ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (الذي).
The clause «اتّقوا الله ...» is in the position of jussive as apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of an implied condition, i.e.: if what I say reaches you, then fear ...
The clause «أطيعون ...» is in the position of jussive, conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause اتّقوا الله.
64- (هو) a separating pronoun (ḍamīr faṣl) [Note: Or a detached pronoun, mubtadaʾ (subject), whose khabar (predicate) is ربّي, and the nominal clause is the khabar of إنّ.]; (الفاء) for linking.
The clause «إنّ الله ... ربّي ...» has no grammatical position: an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī).
The clause «اعبدوه» has no grammatical position, conjoined to an implied resumption, i.e.: take heed, and worship Him.
The clause «هذا صراط ...» has no grammatical position: causal (taʿlīliyya) [Note: Or a resumption from the speech of Allah, not from the speech of ʿĪsā.].
65- (الفاء) conjunction in both places; (من بينهم) attached to a ḥāl of الأحزاب [Note: I.e. in the state of the factions being some of the Christians.]; (ويل) a nominative mubtadaʾ [Note: It came indefinite because it is in the context of blame.]; (للذين) attached to the khabar of the mubtadaʾ ويل; (من عذاب) attached to the omitted khabar [Note: Or a ḥāl of the pronoun concealed in the khabar, the governing factor being the sense of "being established" (al-istiqrār), i.e. in the state of its being from the punishment of the Hereafter, not from the punishment of this world.].
The clause «اختلف الأحزاب ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the resumptive clause in His words (ولمّا جاء عيسى بالبيّنات).
The clause «ويل للذين ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause اختلف الأحزاب.
The clause «ظلموا ...» has no grammatical position: ṣila of the relative noun (الذين).

safi-cedvel:66-66.t:
* I'rab:
(هل) an interrogative particle carrying the sense of negation; (إلّا) for restriction (ḥaṣr); (بغتة) a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the place of a ḥāl (circumstantial) [Note: Or a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) standing in for the maṣdar, since "coming upon them" carries the meaning.. see verse (31) of Sūrat al-Anʿām.]; (الواو) circumstantial (ḥāliyya).
The interpreted maṣdar (أن تأتيهم ...) is in the position of accusative as badal (substitute) of الساعة.
The clause «ينظرون ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «تأتيهم ...» has no grammatical position: ṣila of the particle-relative (أن).
The clause «هم لا يشعرون» is in the position of accusative as ḥāl.
The clause «لا يشعرون» is in the position of nominative as khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject) (هم).

* Benefits:
- هل.
هل is an interrogative particle, but it occurs with a number of meanings. In the noble verse under discussion it has left the meaning of interrogation for the meaning of negation, in the words of Allah the Exalted (هَلْ يَنْظُرُونَ إِلَّا السَّاعَةَ أَنْ تَأْتِيَهُمْ بَغْتَةً وَهُمْ لا يَشْعُرُونَ). The meaning is: they await nothing but the Hour, that it come upon them. Ibn Hishām mentioned this, saying:
Negation is intended by the interrogative with it; for that reason (إلا) entered upon the predicate after it in the words of Allah the Exalted هَلْ جَزاءُ الْإِحْسانِ إِلَّا الْإِحْسانُ, and the bāʾ in the saying of al-Farazdaq: (ألا هل أخو عيش لذيذ بدائم) (Is the one who has a sweet life lasting?), and conjunction was valid in the saying of Imruʾ al-Qays:
وإن شفائي عبرة مهراقة ... وهل عند رسم دارس من معول
(My cure is a tear poured out — yet is there any recourse at an effaced trace of a dwelling?)
since an inshāʾ (non-declarative) sentence is not conjoined to a khabar (declarative) one. The first half of the verse is declarative, and the conjunction shows that the second half of the verse is declarative, i.e. هل cannot validly be interrogative here; rather it is negative.
The hamza comes for denial (inkār), as in the words of Allah the Exalted أَفَأَصْفاكُمْ رَبُّكُمْ بِالْبَنِينَ, as a denial against whoever claimed that; the sense of negation follows from that, not that it is for negation. For this reason you may not say أقام إلا زيد؟ as you may say هل قام إلا زيد!

safi-cedvel:67-67.t:
* I'rab:
(يومئذ) an accusative adverb (ẓarf), annexed to an indeclinable adverb, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (عدوّ); the tanwīn is a substitute for an omitted clause, i.e. on the day when the Hour comes upon them; (بعضهم) a nominative second mubtadaʾ (subject); (لبعض) attached to (عدوّ); (إلّا) for exception; (المتّقين) excepted by إلّا, accusative.
The clause «الأخلّاء ... عدوّ» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «بعضهم لبعض عدوّ» is in the position of nominative as khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (الأخلّاء).

safi-cedvel:68-73.t:
* I'rab:
(عباد) a muḍāf vocative (munādā), accusative, the sign of the accusative being the fatḥa implied (muqaddar) on the letter before the first-person yāʾ, which is deleted for lightness; (لا) negative, non-governing (muhmala) [Note: Or governing like ليس, with خوف as its noun and عليكم as its khabar.]; (خوف) a nominative mubtadaʾ (subject) [Note: The indefinite noun relies on a negation.]; (عليكم) attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ; (اليوم) an accusative adverb, attached to the omitted khabar; (الواو) conjunction; (لا) redundant (zāʾida), to reinforce the negation, its repetition being obligatory; (أنتم تحزنون) like خوف عليكم.
The clause «يا عباد ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive [Note: Or in the position of accusative as the object of an implied speech verb.].
The clause «لا خوف عليكم ...» has no grammatical position: answer to the vocative.
The clause «أنتم تحزنون» has no grammatical position, conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause لا خوف عليكم.
69- (الذين) a relative noun in the position of accusative as naʿt (adjective) of عبادي; (بآياتنا) attached to (آمنوا); (الواو) conjunction — or circumstantial —.
The clause «آمنوا ...» has no grammatical position: ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (الذين).
The clause «كانوا مسلمين ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the ṣila [Note: Or in the position of accusative as ḥāl (circumstantial) of the fāʿil (agent) of آمنوا.].
70- (أنتم) a detached pronoun in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ; (أزواجكم) is conjoined to it by the wāw, and it is nominative ... The wāw in (تحبرون) is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent).
The clause «ادخلوا ...» has no grammatical position: a resumption within the scope of the vocative.
The clause «أنتم ... تحبرون» is in the position of accusative as ḥāl of the fāʿil of ادخلوا.
The clause «تحبرون» is in the position of nominative as khabar of the mubtadaʾ (أنتم).
71- (عليهم) the nāʾib fāʿil of the passive (يطاف); (بصحاف) attached to (يطاف); (من ذهب) attached to a naʿt of (صحاف); (الواو) conjunction; (فيها) attached to a fronted khabar of the mubtadaʾ (ما); and the second (فيها) is attached to (خالدون).
The clause «يطاف عليهم» has no grammatical position: an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī) [Note: Or it is the apodosis of an implied condition, i.e.: when they enter it, there will be passed around them.. Some permitted making it a ḥāl of الجنّة, the link in it being implied, its implied form being "فيها".].
The clause «فيها ما تشتهيه الأنفس» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause يطاف.
The clause «تشتهيه الأنفس ...» has no grammatical position: ṣila of the relative noun (ما).
The clause «تلذّ الأعين ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause تشتهيه الأنفس.
The clause «أنتم فيها خالدون» is in the position of accusative, conjoined to the clause أنتم ... تحبرون, what lies between them being a parenthesis containing iltifāt (shift of person) [Note: It may be a ḥāl of the pronoun in (عليهم), on the assumption of iltifāt.].
72- (الواو) conjunction; (تلك) a demonstrative, mubtadaʾ, whose khabar is the clause لكم فيها فواكه [Translator's note: the source writes فواكه here; the verse has فاكهة.].
(التي) a relative noun, a nominative naʿt of الجنّة; the second-person pronoun in (أورثتموها) is the nāʾib fāʿil, the wāw is redundant, a lengthening (ishbāʿ) of the vowel of the mīm, and the third-person pronoun is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (ما) maṣdar-forming [Note: Or a relative noun in the position of genitive, the resumptive pronoun being omitted and the clause after it being the ṣila.].
The interpreted maṣdar (ما كنتم تعملون) is in the position of genitive by the causal bāʾ, attached to (أورثتموها).
The clause «تلك الجنّة ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the answer to the vocative.
The clause «أورثتموها ...» has no grammatical position: ṣila of the relative noun (التي).
The clause «كنتم تعملون» has no grammatical position: ṣila of the particle-relative (ما).
The clause «تعملون» is in the position of accusative as khabar of كنتم.
73- (لكم) attached to a fronted khabar; (فيها) attached to the omitted khabar; (فاكهة) a nominative delayed mubtadaʾ; (منها) attached to the verb (تأكلون).
The clause «لكم فيها فاكهة ...» is in the position of nominative as khabar of the mubtadaʾ تلك.
The clause «تأكلون ...» is in the position of nominative as naʿt of فاكهة.

* Morphology:
(71) صحاف: plural of صحفة, a primitive (jāmid) noun for a large vessel; its pattern is فعلة with fatḥa then sukūn, and the pattern of صحاف is فعال with kasra on the fāʾ.
(أكواب): plural of كوب, a primitive noun for a cup that has no handle; its pattern is فعل with ḍamma then sukūn, and the pattern of أكواب is أفعال — a plural of paucity (jamʿ qilla) —.

* Rhetoric:
1- Concision (ījāz): in the words of Allah the Exalted «وَفِيها ما تَشْتَهِيهِ الْأَنْفُسُ وَتَلَذُّ الْأَعْيُنُ».
This is an exhaustive enumeration of the kinds of blessings, for they are either desired in the hearts or delightful to the eyes.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to a Bedouin: If Allah admits you into Paradise, you will find in it whatever your soul desires and your eye delights in.
2- Dependent metaphor (al-istiʿāra al-tabaʿiyya): in the words of Allah the Exalted «وَتِلْكَ الْجَنَّةُ الَّتِي أُورِثْتُمُوها».
For what they deserved through their good deeds — Paradise and its everlasting bliss for them — is likened to the property and provisions a man leaves behind for his heir; this entails likening the deed itself to the bequeather (al-mūrith, active participle). So "inheritance" was borrowed for what they deserved, and then أورثتموها was derived from it, so there is a dependent metaphor.
It is also said that the inheritance is a majāz mursal (metonymic figure) for obtaining and taking.

* Benefits:
- The bounty and beneficence of Allah.
In this verse He, Glorified be He, set out the bliss of Paradise: in it is whatever souls desire and eyes delight in.
It is reported in the hadith from Abū Hurayra, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: Allah the Exalted said: I have prepared for My righteous servants what no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and has never occurred to the heart of a human being. Recite if you wish: «فَلا تَعْلَمُ نَفْسٌ ما أُخْفِيَ لَهُمْ مِنْ قُرَّةِ أَعْيُنٍ». Agreed upon.
From Abū Hurayra, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: The first group to enter Paradise will be in the form of the moon on the night of the full moon; then those who follow them will be like the most brilliantly shining star in the sky. They will not urinate, nor relieve themselves, nor spit, nor blow their noses. Their combs will be gold, their sweat musk, and their censers aloeswood (al-uluwwa, fragrant wood). Their spouses will be the wide-eyed houris. [They will be] in the make of a single man, in the form of their father Ādam, sixty cubits tall. Agreed upon. In a narration of al-Bukhārī and Muslim: "Their vessels in it will be gold, their sweat in it musk, and each of them will have two wives, the marrow of whose shins will be seen through the flesh because of beauty. There will be no disagreement among them and no mutual hatred; their hearts will be as the heart of one man; they will glorify Allah morning and evening."
From Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī, may Allah be pleased with him, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: In Paradise there is a tree in whose shade a rider on a swift, lean-trained horse would travel for a hundred years without crossing it. Agreed upon.
From Abū Hurayra, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: When the people of Paradise enter Paradise, a caller will call out: It is for you to be healthy and never fall ill, it is for you to live and never die, it is for you to be young and never grow old, and it is for you to enjoy bliss and never be wretched. Narrated by Muslim.

safi-cedvel:74-76.t:
* I'rab:
(في عذاب) attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar (predicate) (خالدون) [Note: Or it is a first khabar.].
The clause «إنّ المجرمين ... خالدون» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
75- (لا) negative; the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun referring to the punishment; (عنهم) attached to (يفتّر); (الواو) conjunction — or circumstantial —; (فيه) attached to the khabar (مبلسون).
The clause «لا يفتّر عنهم ...» has no grammatical position: an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī) [Note: Or in the position of accusative as ḥāl (circumstantial) of the pronoun in (خالدون), or of عذاب.].
The clause «هم فيه مبلسون» has no grammatical position, conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause لا يفتّر [Note: Or in the position of accusative as ḥāl of the pronoun in (عنهم).].
76- (الواو) conjunction; (ما) negative; the second (الواو) conjunction; (لكن) for rectification (istidrāk), non-governing; (هم) a separating pronoun (ḍamīr faṣl) [Note: It may be a tawkīd (emphasis) of the third-person pronoun that is the noun of كانوا, in the position of nominative.].
The clause «ما ظلمناهم ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause لا يفتّر.
The clause «كانوا هم الظالمين» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause ما ظلمناهم.

safi-cedvel:77-78.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive; (اللام) the lām of command; (علينا) attached to (mutaʿalliq) (يقض).
The clause «نادوا ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «يا مالك ...» has no grammatical position: an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī).
The clause «ليقض علينا ربّك ...» has no grammatical position: answer to the vocative.
The clause «قال ...» has no grammatical position: an explanatory resumption.
The clause «إنّكم ماكثون» is in the position of accusative as the object of speech (maqūl al-qawl).
78- (اللام) the lām of the oath, for an implied oath; (قد) a particle of realisation (taḥqīq); (بالحقّ) attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the fāʿil (agent) of جئناكم; (الواو) conjunction; (للحقّ) attached to the khabar (predicate) (كارهون).
The clause «جئناكم ...» has no grammatical position: the answer to the implied oath; the implied oath clause is a resumption within the scope of the speech [Note: Or it is the object of an implied speech verb from Allah, Mighty and Majestic.].
The clause «لكنّ أكثركم ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause answering the oath.

* Morphology:
(مالك): a proper name for the keeper of the Fire.
(يقض): it contains iʿlāl (weak-letter change) by deletion on account of the jussive; its pattern is يفع.

safi-cedvel:79-80.t:
* I'rab:
(أم) disconnected (munqaṭiʿa), meaning بل plus the hamza; (الفاء) linking the apodosis of an implied condition.
The clause «أبرموا ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «إنّا مبرمون» is in the position of jussive as apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of an implied condition, i.e.: if they have done that, then We are determining.
80- (أم) like the first; (لا) negative; (بلى) a particle of answer; (الواو) circumstantial (ḥāliyya); (لديهم) an adverb (ẓarf), indeclinable (mabnī) on sukūn, in the position of accusative, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (يكتبون).
The clause «يحسبون ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «لا نسمع ...» is in the position of nominative as khabar (predicate) of أنّ.
The interpreted maṣdar (أنا لا نسمع) is in the position of accusative, standing in place of the two objects of يحسبون.
The clause «رسلنا لديهم يكتبون» is in the position of accusative as ḥāl (circumstantial).
The clause «يكتبون» is in the position of nominative as khabar of the mubtadaʾ (subject) (رسلنا).

* Morphology:
(مبرمون): plural of مبرم, active participle of the four-letter (أبرم); its pattern is مفعل with ḍamma on the mīm and kasra on the ʿayn.

safi-cedvel:81-82.t:
* I'rab:
(كان) a deficient (nāqiṣ) past verb in the position of jussive as protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); (للرحمن) attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar of كان; (الفاء) linking the apodosis.
The clause «كان للرحمن ولد ...» is in the position of accusative as the object of speech (maqūl al-qawl) of the resumptive قل.
The clause «أنا أوّل ...» is in the position of jussive as apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), joined with fāʾ.
82- (سبحان) a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) of an omitted verb; the second (ربّ) a genitive badal (substitute) of the first; (عمّا) attached to the omitted verb governing سبحان; (ما) is a relative noun and the resumptive pronoun is omitted ...
The clause «نسبّح سبحان ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive — or parenthetical —.
The clause «يصفون» has no grammatical position: ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (ما).

* Benefits:
- Allah is One, without partner ...
This verse denied that the All-Merciful has a son, in the words of Allah the Exalted قُلْ إِنْ كانَ لِلرَّحْمنِ وَلَدٌ فَأَنَا أَوَّلُ الْعابِدِينَ. The views of the exegetes on the meaning of this verse branched out. It was said:
Its meaning is: if the All-Merciful had a son, in your statement and by your claim, then I am the first to worship the All-Merciful, for He has no partner and no son. Ibn ʿAbbās said: (إن كان) means (ما كان): the All-Merciful has no son, (فأنا أول العابدين), i.e. the first of those who bear witness to Him in that. It was said: its meaning is: if the All-Merciful had a son, I would be the first to worship Him with that, but He has no son. It was said: العابدين means "those who disdain", i.e. I am the first of those who reject and deny what you have said, and I am the first to be angered for the sake of the All-Merciful that it should be said He has a son.
Al-Zamakhsharī said on the meaning of the verse: If the All-Merciful had a son, and that were sound and established by a valid proof that you bring forward and a clear argument that you adduce, then I would be the first to honour that son and the foremost of you in obeying him, just as men honour the son of the king out of honour for his father. This is speech made by way of supposition and illustration, for a purpose, namely emphasis and amplification in negating the son, together with expressing his own firm footing in the matter of tawḥīd. That is because he made the worship conditional upon the existence of the son, which is impossible in itself, so what is made conditional upon it is impossible like it.

safi-cedvel:83-83.t:
* I'rab:
(الفاء) linking the apodosis of an implied condition; (يخوضوا) an imperfect verb, jussive as the answer to the request (jawāb al-ṭalab), and likewise (يلعبوا) conjoined to it; (حتّى) a particle of limit and genitive; (يلاقوا) an imperfect verb, accusative by an implied أن after حتّى; (الذي) a relative noun in the position of accusative as naʿt (adjective) of يومهم; the wāw in (يوعدون) is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent).
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يلاقوا..) is in the position of genitive by (حتّى), attached to (mutaʿalliq) (يخوضوا ويلعبوا).
The clause «ذرهم ...» is in the position of jussive as apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of an implied condition, i.e.: if they turn away from faith, then leave them.
The clause «يخوضوا ...» has no grammatical position: apodosis of an implied condition, i.e.: if you leave them, they will plunge ...
The clause «يلعبوا ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause يخوضوا.
The clause «يلاقوا ...» has no grammatical position: ṣila of the implied particle-relative (أن).
The clause «يوعدون» has no grammatical position: ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (الذي).

* Morphology:
(يلاقوا): it contains iʿlāl (weak-letter change) by making vowelless and iʿlāl by deletion.. its original form is يلاقيوا; the ḍamma on the yāʾ was felt heavy, so it was made vowelless and its vowel was moved to the qāf before it — iʿlāl by making vowelless — then the yāʾ was deleted because, being vowelless, it met the wāw, so it became يلاقوا; its pattern is يفاعوا.

safi-cedvel:84-85.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive; (في السماء) attached to (mutaʿalliq) (إله) in the sense of "one worshipped"; the first (إله) is the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), its implied form being "هو"; (في الأرض) like في السماء; the second (إله) like the first, nominative like it; (الواو) conjunction.
The clause «هو الذي ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «(هو) ... إله» has no grammatical position: ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (الذي).
The clause «(هو) في الأرض إله» has no grammatical position, conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the ṣila clause.
The clause «هو الحكيم ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the resumptive clause.
85- (الواو) conjunction in all five places; (له) attached to a fronted khabar of the delayed mubtadaʾ (ملك); (ما) a relative noun in the position of nominative, conjoined to ملك; (بينهما) an accusative adverb, attached to an omitted ṣila of ما; (عنده) an accusative adverb, attached to a fronted khabar of the delayed mubtadaʾ (علم); (إليه) attached to the passive (ترجعون), and the wāw in it is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent).
The clause «تبارك الذي ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause هو الذي.
The clause «له ملك ...» has no grammatical position: ṣila of the relative noun (الذي).
The clause «عنده علم ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the ṣila clause.
The clause «ترجعون» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the ṣila clause.

safi-cedvel:86-86.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive; (لا) negative; (من دونه) attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the omitted resumptive pronoun, and the pronoun refers to Allah; (الشفاعة) mafʿūl bihi (direct object), governed by (يملك); (إلّا) for exception; (من) a relative noun, badal (substitute) of الذين [Note: What is meant by it is the things worshipped besides Allah.. whether idols or otherwise. (من) may also be in the position of accusative as a connected or disconnected exception, depending on the interpretation of (الذين).], in the position of nominative; (بالحقّ) attached to (شهد); (الواو) circumstantial (ḥāliyya).
The clause «لا يملك الذين ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «يدعون ...» has no grammatical position: ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (الذين).
The clause «شهد ...» has no grammatical position: ṣila of the relative noun (من).
The clause «هم يعلمون» is in the position of accusative as ḥāl.
The clause «يعلمون» is in the position of nominative as khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject) (هم).

safi-cedvel:87-87.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive; (اللام) preparing (muwaṭṭiʾa) for an implied oath; (سألتهم) a past verb in the position of jussive as protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); (من) an interrogative noun in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject), whose khabar (predicate) is the clause خلقهم; (اللام) the lām of the oath; (يقولنّ) a nominative imperfect verb, the sign of the nominative being the retention of the nūn, which was deleted because of the succession of identical letters; the wāw, deleted because of the meeting of two vowelless letters, is the fāʿil (agent), and (النون) is the nūn of emphasis; (الله) the Majestic Name, fāʿil of an omitted verb, its implied form being "خلقهم" [Note: By analogy with the words of Allah the Exalted in verse (9) of this sura «... ليقولنّ خلقهنّ العزيز ...». The Majestic Name may also be a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is omitted, its implied form being "خالقهم".]; (الفاء) linking the apodosis of an implied condition; (أنّى) an indeclinable interrogative noun in the position of accusative as an adverb of place, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (يؤفكون).
The clause «إن سألتهم ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «من خلقهم ...» is in the position of accusative as the object of the verb of asking, suspended (muʿallaq) by the interrogative (من), with a preposition implied.
The clause «خلقهم ...» is in the position of nominative as khabar of the mubtadaʾ (من).
The clause «يقولنّ ...» has no grammatical position: answer to the oath.. the apodosis is omitted, indicated by the answer to the oath.
The clause «(خلقهم) الله ...» is in the position of accusative as the object of speech (maqūl al-qawl).
The clause «أنّى يؤفكون» is in the position of jussive as apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of an implied condition, i.e.: if they know that, then how are they turned away?

safi-cedvel:88-89.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) conjunction; (قيله) conjoined (maʿṭūf) to (الساعة) [Note: I.e. with Him is the knowledge of the Hour and the knowledge of his saying.. This is the view of Ibn Kathīr and al-ʿUkbarī. It may also be genitive by the wāw of the oath, the answer to the oath being His words «إنّ هؤلاء قوم لا يؤمنون»; this is the choice of al-Zamakhsharī.]; the pronoun in قيله refers to the Messenger, upon him be peace; (ربّ) a muḍāf vocative (munādā), accusative, the sign of the accusative being the fatḥa implied (muqaddar) on the letter before the first-person yāʾ, which is deleted for lightness; (لا) negative.
The clause «يا ربّ ...» is in the position of accusative as the object of speech (maqūl al-qawl) of the maṣdar قيله.
The clause «إنّ هؤلاء قوم ...» has no grammatical position: answer to the vocative.
The clause «لا يؤمنون» is in the position of nominative as naʿt (adjective) of قوم.
89- (الفاء) linking the apodosis of an implied condition; (عنهم) attached to (mutaʿalliq) (اصفح); (سلام) khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), its implied form being "أمري" or "شأني"; (الفاء) for linking; (سوف) a particle of the future.
The clause «اصفح ...» is in the position of jussive as apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of an implied condition, i.e.: if they oppose you, then pardon ...
The clause «قل ...» is conjoined to the clause اصفح.
The clause «(أمري) سلام» is in the position of accusative as the object of speech.
The clause «سوف يعلمون» is in the position of jussive as apodosis of another implied condition, i.e.: if they resist you and fight you, then they will come to know ...

* Morphology:
(قيله): an aural (samāʿī) maṣdar of the verb قال, like القول, القال and المقالة.. its pattern is فعل with kasra then sukūn. It contains iʿlāl (weak-letter change) by substitution: its original form is قول with kasra then sukūn; the wāw was changed to yāʾ because the letter before it has kasra.

safi-cedvel:1-5.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) the wāw of oath. (الكتاب) genitive (majrūr) by the wāw, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted verb, its implied form being أقسم (I swear). (قرآنا) second mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb).
The clause «(أقسم) بالكتاب ...» has no grammatical position, being initial (ibtidāʾiyya).
The clause «إنّا جعلناه ...» has no grammatical position, being the answer of the oath.
The clause «جعلناه ...» is in the position of nominative as khabar (predicate) of إنّ.
The clause «لعلّكم تعقلون» has no grammatical position, being an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī).
The clause «تعقلون» is in the position of nominative as khabar of لعلّ.
4- (الواو) conjunction. (في أم) attached to (عليّ). (لدينا) an adverb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn, in the position of accusative, attached to (عليّ). (اللام) the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa) for emphasis.
The clause «إنّه ... لعليّ ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause that is the answer of the oath.
5- (الهمزة) for the interrogative of denial (istifhām inkārī). (الفاء) conjunction. (عنكم) attached to (نضرب), by making it include the sense of نمسك (We withhold) or نعرض (We turn away). (صفحا) mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) standing in for the maṣdar, as it agrees with it in meaning [Note: or it is a maṣdar in the place of a ḥāl (circumstantial).]. (أن) a maṣdar-forming particle (ḥarf maṣdarī)..
The interpreted maṣdar (أن كنتم قوما..) is in the position of genitive by an omitted preposition, attached to (نضرب), i.e. لأن كنتم (because you were) [Note: The clause نضرب ... has no grammatical position, conjoined to an implied resumption, i.e. أنهملكم (shall We neglect you?).
The clause كنتم قوما has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the particle relative (al-mawṣūl al-ḥarfī) (أن).] ...

* Morphology:
(صفحا) maṣdar of the triliteral صفح; its pattern is فعل, with fatḥa then sukūn.

* Rhetoric:
1- The art of congruity (al-tanāsub): in the saying of Allah the Exalted «وَالْكِتابِ الْمُبِينِ: إِنَّا جَعَلْناهُ قُرْآناً عَرَبِيًّا لَعَلَّكُمْ تَعْقِلُونَ». In this noble verse Allah the Exalted swore by the Quran — and He swears only by something mighty — then He made the thing sworn upon the glorification of the Quran, in that it is an Arabic Quran by which it is hoped the worlds will understand, i.e. comprehend the signs of Allah the Exalted. So the answer of the oath validated the oath.
This is what is called the art of congruity, for congruity has occurred between the oath and what is sworn by, because they are one thing.
2- Explicit metaphor (al-istiʿāra al-taṣrīḥiyya): in the saying of Allah the Exalted «وَإِنَّهُ فِي أُمِّ الْكِتابِ».
He borrowed the word الأم (the mother) for the origin, which is the Preserved Tablet; that is the omitted thing likened (al-mushabbah).
This metaphor serves to represent what is not visible so that it becomes visible, and the benefit of this metaphor is manifestness, because the mother is more manifest to the senses than the origin.
3- Representational metaphor (al-istiʿāra al-tamthīliyya): in the saying of Allah the Exalted «أَفَنَضْرِبُ عَنْكُمُ الذِّكْرَ».
I.e. shall We put it aside and remove it from you — by way of representational metaphor, from their saying «ضرب الغرائب عن الحوض» (he beat the stray camels away from the watering-trough): the state of the Reminder and its being put aside is likened to the state of stray camels and their being driven away from the trough when they enter with others at watering time; then what belonged to that story was used here. Of this kind is the saying of al-Ḥajjāj: لأضربنكم ضرب غرائب الإبل (I will surely beat you as stray camels are beaten).

safi-cedvel:6-8.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive (istiʾnāfiyya). (كم) declarative (khabariyya), an allusive noun (ism kināya), in the position of accusative as a fronted mafʿūl bihi (direct object). (من نبيّ) tamyīz (specification) of كم. (في الأوّلين) attached to (mutaʿalliq) (أرسلنا).
The clause «أرسلنا ...» has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
7- (الواو) conjunction. (ما) negating. (نبيّ) genitive in form by من, nominative in position, as the fāʿil (agent) of يأتيهم. (إلّا) for restriction (ḥaṣr). (به) attached to (يستهزئ).
The clause «ما يأتيهم من نبيّ ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the resumptive clause.
The clause «كانوا به يستهزئون» is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial).
The clause «يستهزئون ...» is in the position of accusative as khabar of كانوا.
8- (الفاء) conjunction. (أشدّ) the object of أهلكنا; it is originally a naʿt (adjective) of an implied qualified noun, i.e. قوما أشدّ (a people stronger). (منهم) attached to (أشدّ). (بطشا) tamyīz, accusative. (الواو) resumptive ...
The clause «أهلكنا ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause ما يأتيهم.
The clause «مضى مثل ...» has no grammatical position, being resumptive.

* Morphology:
(بطشا) a heard (samāʿī) maṣdar of the triliteral بطش, of the class of ضرب; its pattern is فعل, with fatḥa then sukūn.
(مضى) contains iʿlāl (weak-letter change) by qalb (conversion). Its origin is مضي — with a yāʾ at its end; the yāʾ was vowelled after a fatḥa, so it was converted to alif.

* Benefits:
- Interrogative كم and declarative كم ...
1- Interrogative (كم) is used to ask for the specification of a number, and its specifier (mumayyiz) is always accusative, e.g. (كم كتابا قرأت)? (how many books did you read?) — except when it is accompanied by a preposition, in which case its specifier is genitive, e.g.: (بكم ليرة اشتريت الكتاب)? (for how many liras did you buy the book?)
2- Declarative كم conveys information and abundance, and its specifier is genitive by annexation, e.g.: (كم فارس تبارز في الميدان) (how many a horseman dueled in the arena). Its specifier also comes genitive by من, e.g.: (كم من شهيد سقط دفاعا عن الكرامة) (how many a martyr fell defending dignity), the meaning being: many martyrs fell defending dignity.
3- Interrogative كم and declarative كم are parsed according to the speech that follows them.
a- They are parsed in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject) if a noun follows them, e.g.:
كم فارسا في الميدان؟ كم بطل في الساحة! And in our saying كم مالك؟ it is permissible for (كم) to be a mubtadaʾ or a fronted khabar (predicate).
Likewise, if an intransitive verb follows them, they are parsed as mubtadaʾ, e.g.:
كم رجلا جاء للمشاركة في الاحتفال؟ ... كم شهيد سار على درب النضال!
Likewise, if a transitive verb that has taken its object follows them, they are parsed as mubtadaʾ: كم كتابا قرأته؟
كم صديق زرته لله!
b- They are parsed in the position of accusative as mafʿūl bihi if a transitive verb that has not taken its object follows them: (كم كتابا قرأت؟ كم صديق زرت الله) [Translator's note: the source has «زرت الله» here; the parallel example above has «زرته لله».].
c- They are parsed in the position of accusative as an adverb of time or place if an adverb of time or place follows them, provided the verb does not require a mafʿūl bihi..
كم ساعة سرت في الطريق؟ كم ميل مشيت إليك!
d- They are parsed in the position of accusative as a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) if a maṣdar from the verb's root follows them:
كم ضربة ضربت العدو؟ كم طعنة طعنها العدو!
c- [Translator's note: the source repeats the letter ج here.] Interrogative كم is parsed as the khabar of an incomplete (nāqiṣ) verb if such a verb follows it: كم أصبح أولادك؟ كم كان مالك؟
An important remark:
1- The specifier of interrogative and declarative كم may be omitted if it is understood from the context: كم صمت, i.e. كم يوما صمت (how many days did you fast?). كم مشينا على الخطوب كراما, i.e. كم مشية مشينا (how many a walk we walked nobly through calamities).
2- The specifier of interrogative كم is parsed as an accusative tamyīz, and the specifier of declarative كم is parsed as muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).

safi-cedvel:9-14.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive (istiʾnāfiyya). (اللام) preparing for the oath (muwaṭṭiʾa li-l-qasam). (سألتهم) past verb, in the position of jussive (majzūm) as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ). (من) an interrogative noun, mubtadaʾ (subject), whose khabar (predicate) is the clause خلق. (اللام) the lām of the oath. (يقولّن) imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and the sign of the nominative is the retention of the nūn — it was deleted because of the succession of identical letters — and (الواو), [deleted] because of the meeting of two vowelless letters, is the fāʿil (agent), and (النون) is for emphasis. (العليم) naʿt (adjective) of العزيز, nominative.
The clause «سألتهم ...» has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
The clause «من خلق السموات ...» is in the position of accusative as the object of the asking, which is suspended (muʿallaq) by the interrogative, with the preposition implied.
The clause «يقولّن ...» has no grammatical position, being the answer of the oath.. and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, indicated by the answer of the oath.
The clause «خلقهنّ العزيز ...» is in the position of accusative as maqūl al-qawl (the object of speech).
10- (الذي) relative noun, in the position of nominative as a second naʿt of العزيز [Note: or the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, its implied form being هو, and the clause is resumptive.]. (لكم) attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the second mafʿūl bihi (direct object) مهدا. The second (لكم) is attached to an omitted second mafʿūl bihi. (فيها) attached to the second object — or to (جعل)..
The clause «جعل (the first) ...» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (الذي).
The clause «جعل (the second) ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause جعل (the first).
The clause «لعلّكم تهتدون» has no grammatical position, being an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī).
The clause «تهتدون» is in the position of nominative as khabar of لعلّ.
11- (الواو) conjunction. (الذي) relative noun, in the position of nominative, conjoined to the first relative noun. (من السماء) attached to (نزّل). (بقدر) attached to a naʿt of (ماء). (الفاء) conjunction. (به) attached to (أنشرنا). (كذلك) attached to an omitted mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) whose governor is (تخرجون).. and (الواو) in it is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent).
The clause «نزّل ...» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the second relative noun (الذي).
The clause «أنشرنا ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the ṣila clause, and it contains iltifāt (shift of person).
The clause «تخرجون» has no grammatical position, being parenthetical (iʿtirāḍiyya).
12- (الواو) conjunction in the three places. (الذي) relative noun, in the position of nominative, conjoined to the first relative noun. (كلّها) tawkīd maʿnawī (semantic emphasis) of (الأزواج), accusative like it. (لكم) attached to an omitted second mafʿūl bihi. (من الفلك) attached to a ḥāl of (ما), the first object [Note: ما is a relative noun or a qualified indefinite noun (nakira mawṣūfa), and the resumptive pronoun is omitted, i.e. تركبونها.]..
The clause «خلق ...» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the third relative noun (الذي).
The clause «جعل ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause خلق.
The clause «تركبون» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the relative noun (ما) [Note: or in the position of accusative as a naʿt of (ما).].
13- (اللام) the lām of consequence or outcome (lām al-ʿāqiba aw al-ṣayrūra). (تستووا) imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an implied أن after the lām. (على ظهوره) attached to (تستووا). (تذكروا) imperfect verb, accusative, conjoined to (تستووا). (إذا) an adverb of the future, stripped of the conditional sense, attached to (تذكروا). (عليه) attached to (استويتم). (الواو) conjunction. (تقولوا) imperfect verb, accusative, conjoined to (تذكروا). (سبحان) mafʿūl muṭlaq of an omitted verb, accusative. (الذي) relative noun, in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). (لنا) attached to (سخّر). (الواو) circumstantial (ḥāliyya). (ما) negating. (له) attached to the khabar (مقرنين).
The interpreted maṣdar (أن تستووا ...) is in the position of genitive by the lām, attached to (جعل).
The clause «تستووا ...» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the implied particle relative (al-mawṣūl al-ḥarfī) (أن).
The clause «تذكروا ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause تستووا.
The clause «استويتم ...» is in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «تقولوا ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause تذكروا.
The clause «(نسبّح) سبحان ...» is in the position of accusative as maqūl al-qawl.
The clause «سخّر ...» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the relative noun (الذي).
The clause «ما كنّا له مقرنين» is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl.
(إلى ربّنا) attached to (منقلبون). (اللام) the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa) for emphasis.
The clause «إنّا ... لمنقلبون» is in the position of accusative, conjoined to the maqūl al-qawl clause.

* Morphology:
(13) مقرنين: plural of مقرن, active participle of (أقرنه), i.e. he was able to manage it; its pattern is مفعل, with ḍamma on the mīm and kasra on the ʿayn.

* Rhetoric:
1- The art of ellipsis (al-ḥadhf): in the saying of Allah the Exalted «لَيَقُولُنَّ خَلَقَهُنَّ الْعَزِيزُ الْعَلِيمُ».
The qualified noun — namely Allah, glory be to Him, the Exalted — was omitted and His attributes were put in its place, because the speech is divided: part of it is their saying and part of it is the saying of Allah the Exalted. What is their saying is «خلقهن», and what follows it is the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic. The original speech is that they said: خلقهن الله (Allah created them), as is indicated by His saying in the other verse: «وَلَئِنْ سَأَلْتَهُمْ مَنْ خَلَقَ السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضَ لَيَقُولُنَّ اللَّهُ». Then, when they said "Allah created them", He described Himself with these attributes; and since the whole speech was brought in a single flow, the qualified noun was omitted from their speech and the mentioned attributes, from the speech of Allah the Exalted, were put in its place, as though it were one speech. An analogue of this is that you say to a man: "Who among the people honoured you?" and he says: "Zayd honoured me", and you say, describing the one mentioned: "the generous, the munificent, whose description is such-and-such".
2- Iltifāt (shift of person): in the saying of Allah the Exalted «فَأَنْشَرْنا».
Here the transition occurred from their speech to the speech of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: its beginning came in the third person, and its end shifted from that to the first person, in His saying «فأنشرنا». Of this pattern is the saying of Allah the Exalted, relating from Mūsā: «قالَ عِلْمُها عِنْدَ رَبِّي فِي كِتابٍ لا يَضِلُّ رَبِّي وَلا يَنْسى الَّذِي جَعَلَ لَكُمُ الْأَرْضَ مَهْداً وَسَلَكَ لَكُمْ فِيها سُبُلًا وَأَنْزَلَ مِنَ السَّماءِ ماءً فَأَخْرَجْنا بِهِ أَزْواجاً مِنْ نَباتٍ شَتَّى». The beginning of the speech came as a report from Mūsā up to His saying (ولا ينسى), then the transition occurred from the speech of Mūsā to the speech of Allah the Exalted, and He described Himself with attributes connected to the speech of Mūsā, as though it were one speech. He began mentioning His attributes in the third person up to His saying «فَأَخْرَجْنا بِهِ أَزْواجاً مِنْ نَباتٍ شَتَّى».
3- The secret of the circumstance: in the saying of Allah the Exalted «وَإِنَّا إِلى رَبِّنا لَمُنْقَلِبُونَ».
How many a rider of a beast has had it stumble with him, or balk, or plunge, or he fell from its back and perished; and how many riders in a ship had it break apart with them and they drowned. Since riding is directly engaging in a dangerous matter, and a connection with one of the causes of destruction, it is the due of the rider — having connected himself with one of the causes of destruction — not to forget, when connecting with it, its ill omen, and that he is perishing without doubt, and so returning to Allah, not escaping His decree; and he should not abandon remembering that with his heart and his tongue, so that he is prepared to meet Allah by reforming himself.

safi-cedvel:15-15.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive (istiʾnāfiyya). (له) attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted second mafʿūl bihi (direct object). (من عباده) attached to (جعلوا). (اللام) shifted (muzaḥlaqa).
The clause «جعلوا ...» has no grammatical position, being resumptive [Note: The clause may be a ḥāl (circumstantial), with قد implied, connected with the saying of Allah the Exalted: ولئن سألتهم ...; so they contradict their acknowledgement of Allah's lordship by making some of His servants related to Him.].
The clause «إنّ الإنسان لكفور ...» has no grammatical position, being resumptive.

safi-cedvel:16-16.t:
* I'rab:
(أم) meaning بل, or meaning the hamza, or meaning بل together with the hamza, and it is for denial [Note: Abū Ḥayyān permitted that.]. (ممّا) attached to (mutaʿalliq) (اتخذ), and it is in the place of the second object. (بنات) first mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb), and the sign of the accusative is the kasra, as it is assimilated to the feminine plural. (الواو) conjunction — or circumstantial (ḥāliyya). (بالبنين) attached to (أصفاكم)..
The clause «اتّخذ ...» is in the position of accusative as maqūl al-qawl (the object of speech) of an implied saying, i.e.: or do you say: He has taken ...
The clause «يخلق ...» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (ما).
The clause «أصفاكم ...» is in the position of accusative, conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause اتّخذ [Note: It may be a ḥāl (circumstantial), with (قد) implied.].

safi-cedvel:17-17.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive (istiʾnāfiyya). (بما) attached to (mutaʿalliq) (بشّر). (للرحمن) attached to (ضرب). (مثلا) second mafʿūl bihi (direct object), whose governor is ضرب, by making it include the sense of جعل; the first mafʿūl bihi is omitted, i.e. ضربه. (الواو) circumstantial (ḥāliyya)..
The clause «بشّر أحدهم ...» is in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).
The clause «ضرب ...» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (ما).
The clause «ظلّ وجهه ...» has no grammatical position, being the apodosis of a non-jussive condition.
The clause «هو كظيم ...» is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial).

safi-cedvel:18-18.t:
* I'rab:
(الهمزة) for the interrogative of denial (istifhām inkārī). (الواو) resumptive (istiʾnāfiyya). (من) relative noun, in the position of accusative as the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of an omitted verb, its implied form being يجعلون [Note: i.e.: do they make one who is brought up ... a child [of Allah]? It is also permissible for the relative noun to be a mubtadaʾ (subject) with the khabar (predicate) omitted, i.e.: أو من ينشّأ.. ولد.], and the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) of the verb (ينشأ) is a pronoun referring to (من). (في الحلية) attached to (mutaʿalliq) (ينشّأ). (الواو) circumstantial (ḥāliyya). (في الخصام) attached to (مبين) [Note: It is not prohibited here for the muḍāf ilayhi to govern what precedes it, because the muḍāf is the word غير, which has the sense of negation..]..
The clause «(يجعلون) من ...» has no grammatical position, being resumptive [Note: They permitted its being conjoined to an implied resumptive clause, i.e.: do they dare and make one who is brought up ...].
The clause «ينشّأ ...» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (من).
The clause «هو ... غير مبين» is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial).

safi-cedvel:19-23.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive (istiʾnāfiyya) — or conjunction. (الذين) relative noun, in the position of accusative as a naʿt (adjective) of الملائكة. (إناثا) second mafʿūl bihi (direct object), whose governor is جعلوا. (الهمزة) for the interrogative of denial (istifhām inkārī)..
The clause «جعلوا ...» has no grammatical position, being resumptive — or conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the implied resumptive clause in the previous verse. The clause «هم عباد الرحمن ...» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (الذين).
The clause «شهدوا ...» has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
The clause «ستكتب شهادتهم ...» has no grammatical position, being an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī).
The clause «يسألون» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause ستكتب.
20- (الواو) conjunction. (لو) a non-jussive conditional particle. (ما) negating in both places. (لهم) attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted fronted khabar (predicate). (بذلك) attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) of علم. (علم) genitive in form, nominative in position, a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject). (إن) a particle of negation. (إلّا) for restriction (ḥaṣr).
The clause «قالوا ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause جعلوا..
The clause «شاء الرحمن ...» is in the position of accusative as maqūl al-qawl (the object of speech).
The clause «ما عبدناهم ...» has no grammatical position, being the apodosis of a non-jussive condition.
The clause «ما لهم بذلك من علم» has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
The clause «إن هم إلّا يخرصون» has no grammatical position, being an explanatory resumption — or causal (taʿlīliyya). The clause «يخرصون» is in the position of nominative as khabar of the mubtadaʾ (هم).
21- (أم) disconnected (munqaṭiʿa), meaning بل with the hamza of denial [Note: The digression (iḍrāb) here is from negating that they have a rational support to denying that they have a transmitted authority.]. (كتابا) second mafʿūl bihi, accusative (manṣūb). (من قبله) attached to a naʿt of (كتابا), and the pronoun in (قبله) refers to the Mighty Quran [Note: or attached to (آتيناهم).]. (الفاء) conjunction. (به) attached to (مستمسكون).
The clause «آتيناهم ...» has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
The clause «هم به مستمسكون» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause آتيناهم.
22- (بل) for transitional digression (al-iḍrāb al-intiqālī). (على أمّة) attached to a ḥāl of آباء. (على آثارهم) attached to the khabar (مهتدون) [Note: It may be attached to an omitted khabar.. with (مهتدون) as a second khabar.].
The clause «قالوا ...» has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
The clause «إنّا وجدنا ...» is in the position of accusative as maqūl al-qawl.
The clause «وجدنا ...» is in the position of nominative as khabar of إنّ.
The clause «إنّا على آثارهم ...» is in the position of accusative, conjoined to the maqūl al-qawl clause.
23- (الواو) conjunction. (كذلك) attached to an omitted khabar, with the mubtadaʾ implied, i.e. "the matter is like that", by their inability to produce an argument and their clinging to blind imitation. (ما) negating. (من قبلك) attached to a ḥāl of نذير [Note: or attached to (أرسلنا).]. (في قرية) attached to (أرسلنا). (إلّا) for restriction. (إنّا وجدنا ... مقتدون) is like إنا وجدنا ... مهتدون (in the previous verse).
The clause «(الأمر) كذلك ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause قالوا ...
The clause «ما أرسلنا ...» has no grammatical position, being an explanatory resumption.
The clause «قال مترفوها ...» is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl.
The clause «إنّا وجدنا ...» is in the position of accusative as maqūl al-qawl.
The clause «وجدنا ...» is in the position of nominative as khabar of إنّ.
The clause «إنّا على آثارهم ...» is in the position of accusative, conjoined to the clause إنّا وجدنا.

* Morphology:
(21) مستمسكون: plural of مستمسك, active participle of the six-letter verb استمسك; its pattern is مستفعل, with ḍamma on the mīm and kasra on the ʿayn.
(23) مقتدون: plural of المقتدي, active participle of the five-letter verb اقتدى; its pattern is مفتع — [i.e.] المفتعل — with ḍamma on the mīm and kasra on the ʿayn ... In (مقتدون) there is iʿlāl (weak-letter change) by deletion. Its origin is مقتديون — with kasra on the dāl and ḍamma on the yāʾ: the ḍamma on the yāʾ was felt heavy, so it was made vowelless and the ḍamma was transferred to the dāl — iʿlāl by making vowelless — then the yāʾ was deleted because of the meeting of two vowelless letters, and it became مقتدون; its pattern is مفتعون.

* Benefits:
- Making the verb passive..
The verb is divided into active (mabnī li-l-maʿlūm) and passive (mabnī li-l-majhūl). The first is that with which its agent is mentioned, e.g.: كسر الولد الزجاج (the boy broke the glass); the second is that whose agent is omitted and something else is made to deputize for it, e.g.: كسر الزجاج (the glass was broken).
When making it passive, the form of the verb must be changed: if it is past, the letter before the last is given kasra and every vowelled letter before it is given ḍamma, e.g.: (حفظ الكتاب), (تقبّلت الصدقة), (استخرج المعدن).
If it is imperfect, its first letter is given ḍamma and the letter before the last is given fatḥa: (يقطع الغصن), (يتعلّم الحساب), (يستخرج المعدن).
If the letter before the last of the past verb is an alif, it is converted to yāʾ and the letter before it is given kasra; so we say for قال and اختار: قيل and اختير.
If the letter before the last of the imperfect is a letter of prolongation, it is converted to alif: يقول and يبيع become يقال and يباع.
Remark: the intransitive verb is not made passive unless the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) is a maṣdar, an adverb, or a preposition and its genitive noun, e.g.: (احتفل احتفال عظيم) (a great celebration was held), (ذهب أمام الأمير) (there was going before the prince), and (فرح بالعيد) (there was rejoicing at the feast).
2- With a verb transitive to two objects, the first object becomes the nāʾib fāʿil and the second object stays as it is, e.g.: (أعطي الفقير مالا) (the poor man was given money): الفقير is the nāʾib fāʿil, and مالا is a second mafʿūl bihi.

safi-cedvel:24-25.t:
* I'rab:
(الهمزة) interrogative. (الواو) circumstantial (ḥāliyya). (لو) a non-jussive conditional particle. (بأهدى) attached to (mutaʿalliq) (جئتكم) — or to a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the second-person pronoun in (جئتكم). (ممّا) attached to (أهدى). (عليه) attached to a ḥāl of (آباءكم). (بما) attached to (كافرون). (به) attached to (أرسلتم), and the second-person pronoun is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent).
The clause «قال ...» has no grammatical position, being an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī).
The clause «جئتكم ...» is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl.. and the maqūl al-qawl (object of speech) is omitted, i.e. "will you do that even if I have brought you ...", and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is implied, indicated by the omitted maqūl al-qawl.
The clause «وجدتم ...» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (ما).
The clause «قالوا ...» has no grammatical position, being resumptive (istiʾnāfiyya).
The clause «إنّا ... كافرون» is in the position of accusative as maqūl al-qawl.
The clause «أرسلتم به» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the second relative noun (ما).
25- (الفاء) conjunction, to link the effect to the cause. (منهم) attached to (انتقمنا). The second (الفاء) links the apodosis of an implied condition. (كيف) an interrogative noun, in the position of accusative as the khabar (predicate) of كان..
The clause «انتقمنا ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause قالوا.
The clause «انظر ...» is in the position of jussive (majzūm) as the apodosis of an implied condition, i.e. "if your people deny you, then look ...".
The clause «كان عاقبة ...» is in the position of accusative as the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of the verb of looking, which is suspended (muʿallaq) from direct governing by the interrogative, with the preposition implied..

* Rhetoric:
The art of constraining (al-iljāʾ): in the saying of Allah the Exalted «قالَ أَوَلَوْ جِئْتُكُمْ بِأَهْدى مِمَّا وَجَدْتُمْ» (the verse). The meaning of this rhetorical art is that the speaker confronts the opponent at once with what compels him to admit the truth of himself and the secret of his heart.
In the noble verse, the expression with the elative (tafḍīl), which implies that what their fathers followed contains guidance, was only to compel them to admit the truth of the intentions they conceal. It is as though he comes down to their level to the farthest limit and slackens the rein for them, so that they confess.

* Benefits:
- Interrogative كيف..
It is a noun, because it is used as a predicate and directly precedes the verb (كيف كنت) (how were you?); here it is in the position of accusative as a fronted khabar of كنت, and this is a proof that it is a noun.
It has occurred in the verse we are dealing with as the khabar of كان, in the saying of Allah the Exalted (فانظر كيف كان عاقبة المكذبين). Its i'rab is:
1- A khabar if a noun follows it, e.g.: كيف أنت, or an incomplete (nāqiṣ) verb, e.g.: كيف كنت.
2- It is parsed as a ḥāl if a complete verb (i.e. not incomplete) follows it, e.g.:
كيف جاء زيد (how did Zayd come?). Many grammarians, among them Ibn Hishām, parse it in such cases as a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), as in the saying of Allah the Exalted: (أَلَمْ تَرَ كَيْفَ فَعَلَ رَبُّكَ بِأَصْحابِ الْفِيلِ), i.e. (أيّ فعل فعل) (what manner of action He did).
Remark:
كيف is an interrogative noun that is always indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa..

safi-cedvel:26-28.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive (istiʾnāfiyya). (إذ) an adverbial noun, in the position of accusative as the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of an omitted verb, its implied form being اذكر (remember). (لأبيه) attached to (mutaʿalliq) (قال). (ممّا) attached to (براء). (ما) relative noun, and the resumptive pronoun (ʿāʾid) is omitted.
The clause «قال إبراهيم ...» is in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).
The clause «إنّني براء ...» is in the position of accusative as maqūl al-qawl (the object of speech).
The clause «تعبدون» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (ما).
27- (إلّا) for exception. (الذي) relative noun, in the position of accusative on exception [Note: It is disconnected (munqaṭiʿ) if they worshipped the idols alone.. and connected (muttaṣil) if they associated the idols with Allah.]. (الفاء) causal (taʿlīliyya). (السين) a particle of the future.
The clause «فطرني ...» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the relative noun (الذي).
The clause «إنّه سيهدين» has no grammatical position, being causal.
The clause «سيهدين» is in the position of nominative as khabar (predicate) of إنّ [Note: The nūn in (سيهدين) is the nūn of protection (al-wiqāya), protecting the verb from the kasra before the first-person yāʾ, which is implied (muqaddar) to suit the verse-endings.].
28- (الواو) resumptive, and the third-person pronoun in (جعلها) refers to the word of tawḥīd understood from the preceding saying of Ibrāhīm. (كلمة) second mafʿūl bihi, accusative (manṣūb). (في عقبه) attached to (باقية). The third-person pronoun in (يرجعون) may refer to the people of Mecca, not to the posterity of Ibrāhīm.
The clause «جعلها ...» has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
The clause «لعلّهم يرجعون» has no grammatical position, being an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī).
The clause «يرجعون» is in the position of nominative as khabar of لعلّ.

* Morphology:
(26) براء: maṣdar of the triliteral (برىء), of the class of فرح; its pattern is فعال, with fatḥa on the fāʾ — and it has been used in the place of an adjective. The verb has other maṣdars: برؤ, with ḍamma on the bāʾ, and براءة, with a tāʾ marbūṭa at its end.

safi-cedvel:29-31.t:
* I'rab:
(بل) for transitional digression (al-iḍrāb al-intiqālī). (الواو) conjunction. (آباءهم) conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the demonstrative هؤلاء, accusative (manṣūb). (حتّى) for the end-point (ghāya). (الواو) conjunction..
The interpreted maṣdar (أن جاءهم..) is in the position of genitive by (حتّى), attached to (mutaʿalliq) (متّعت).
The clause «متّعت ...» has no grammatical position, being resumptive (istiʾnāfiyya).
The clause «جاءهم الحقّ ...» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the implied particle relative (al-mawṣūl al-ḥarfī) (أن).
30- (الواو) conjunction. (لمّا) an adverb meaning حين (when), including the sense of condition. (الواو) conjunction. (به) attached to (كافرون).
The clause «جاءهم الحقّ» is in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).. and the clause of the condition, its protasis and its apodosis has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
The clause «قالوا ...» has no grammatical position, being the apodosis of a non-jussive condition.
The clause «هذا سحر ...» is in the position of accusative as maqūl al-qawl (the object of speech).
The clause «إنّا به كافرون» is in the position of accusative, conjoined to the clause هذا سحر.
31- (الواو) conjunction. (لولا) a particle of urging (taḥḍīḍ). (القرآن) badal (substitute) of the demonstrative هذا, in the position of nominative — or ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition) to it. (على رجل) attached to (نزّل). (من القريتين) attached to a naʿt (adjective) of (رجل), and in it a muḍāf is omitted, i.e. "from one of the two towns" [Note: Qatāda said: they are al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīra in Mecca, or ʿUrwa ibn Masʿūd al-Thaqafī in al-Ṭāʾif.].
The clause «قالوا ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the first clause قالوا.
The clause «نزّل هذا القرآن ...» is in the position of accusative as maqūl al-qawl.

safi-cedvel:32-32.t:
* I'rab:
(الهمزة) for the interrogative of wonder (istifhām taʿajjubī). (بينهم) an accusative adverb (ẓarf) attached to (mutaʿalliq) (قسمنا). (في الحياة) attached to (قسمنا). (فوق) an accusative adverb attached to (رفعنا). (درجات) mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) standing in for the maṣdar — a description of the maṣdar — i.e. "a varying raising" [Note: It may be a ḥāl (circumstantial) with a muḍāf omitted, i.e. ذوي درجات (possessing degrees).]. (اللام) of causation (taʿlīl). (يتّخذ) imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an implied أن after the lām. (سخريّا) second mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative.. (الواو) resumptive (istiʾnāfiyya). (ممّا) attached to (خير), and (ما) is a relative noun with the resumptive pronoun omitted [Note: (ما) may be a maṣdar-forming particle, so that nothing is omitted..].
The clause «هم يقسمون ...» has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
The clause «يقسمون ...» is in the position of nominative as khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject) (هم).
The clause «نحن قسمنا ...» has no grammatical position, being an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī).
The clause «قسمنا ...» is in the position of nominative as khabar of the mubtadaʾ (نحن).
The clause «رفعنا ...» is in the position of nominative, conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause قسمنا.
The clause «يتّخذ بعضهم ...» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the implied particle relative (al-mawṣūl al-ḥarfī) (أن), and the interpreted maṣdar (أن يتّخذ) is in the position of genitive by the lām, attached to (رفعنا).
The clause «رحمة ربّك خير ...» has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
The clause «يجمعون» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (ما).

* Benefits:
- People are in degrees so that some of them may take others into service..
This verse has made clear a social law in people's lives and livelihoods: His wisdom required that this one be rich and that one poor, this one strong and that one weak, this one a leader and that one led, so that they serve one another, and so that life becomes complete in all its aspects and the conditions of human beings in it are balanced, lest imbalance and disorder occur and some aspects of life come to a standstill. This is a constant law in people's lives and conditions, in every time and place, and no one can change or alter anything of it. Proceeding from this law, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, singles out some of His servants for the message and revelation, so that one of the most important aspects of life may be completed. None objects to that except a short-sighted fool who understands nothing of life; for Allah singles out for His mercy whom He wills; His is the judgement, and to Him is the return.

safi-cedvel:33-35.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive (istiʾnāfiyya). (لولا) a non-jussive conditional particle. (أن) a maṣdar-forming particle governing the accusative..
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يكون) is in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject), with a muḍāf omitted, i.e.: "were it not for the dislike of people being one community upon disbelief ...", i.e. that they should unite upon disbelief.
The khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ is omitted.
(اللام) linking the apodosis of لولا to the condition. (لمن) attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted second mafʿūl bihi (direct object). (بالرحمن) attached to (يكفر). (لبيوتهم) badal (substitute) of the relative noun with the preposition repeated, and it is a badal of inclusion (badal ishtimāl). (من فضّة) naʿt (adjective) of the first object (سقفا). (معارج) conjoined (maʿṭūf) to (سقفا) by the wāw, accusative (manṣūb), prevented from nunation because it is a plural on the pattern of the furthest plurals (ṣīghat muntahā al-jumūʿ). (عليها) attached to (يظهرون).
The clause «لولا أن يكون ... (the nominal one)» has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
The clause «يكون الناس أمّة ...» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the implied particle relative (al-mawṣūl al-ḥarfī) (أن). [Translator's note: the source says "implied" (المضمر), although أن is overt in this verse.]
The clause «جعلنا ...» has no grammatical position, being the apodosis of a non-jussive condition.
The clause «يكفر ...» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (من).
The clause «يظهرون» is in the position of accusative as a naʿt of معارج.
34- (الواو) conjunction. (لبيوتهم أبوابا ... يتّكئون) is like لبيوتهم سقفا ... يظهرون, and conjoined to it.
The clause «يتّكئون» is in the position of accusative as a naʿt of (سررا) [Note: (سررا) may be the mafʿūl bihi of an omitted verb, its implied form being جعلنا.. in which case the clause is conjoined to the first (جعلنا).].
(الواو) conjunction. (زخرفا) mafʿūl bihi of an omitted verb, its implied form being جعلنا [Note: It may be accusative by removal of the preposition, conjoined to (من فضّة), i.e. of silver and of زخرف — i.e. of gold ...]. (الواو) resumptive. (إن) a particle of negation. (لمّا) for restriction (ḥaṣr), meaning إلّا. (متاع) khabar of the mubtadaʾ (كلّ), nominative. (الواو) conjunction. (عند) an accusative adverb (ẓarf) attached to (المتّقين) [Translator's note: so in the source; the adverb would be attached to the following للمتّقين or to the khabar.]. (للمتّقين) attached to the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (الآخرة)..
The clause «(جعلنا) زخرفا ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the apodosis clause.
The clause «إن كلّ ذلك لمّا متاع ...» has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
The clause «الآخرة ... للمتّقين» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause إن كلّ ذلك ...

* Morphology:
(33) فضّة: a non-derived (jāmid) noun for the well-known metal; its pattern is فعلة, with kasra then sukūn.
(معارج) plural of معرج, a noun of instrument (ism āla) from the triliteral عرج, irregularly (ʿalā ghayr al-qiyās), on the pattern مفعل with fatḥa on the mīm; it may be regular, with kasra on it.

* Benefits:
1- (إن) lightened from the heavy (inna)..
In this verse occurs the saying of Allah the Exalted وَإِنْ كُلُّ ذلِكَ لَمَّا مَتاعُ الْحَياةِ الدُّنْيا; (إن) here is lightened from the heavy, and it has been left non-governing (muhmala), not governing like (إنّ). We will explain its ruling in detail below:
1- إن lightened from the heavy enters both kinds of sentence, the nominal and the verbal. If it enters the nominal, it may govern — contrary to the Kufans — and its governing has occurred in the Noble Quran, as in the reading of the two Ḥaram cities (al-Ḥaramiyyān) and Abū Bakr (وَإِنَّ كُلًّا لَمَّا لَيُوَفِّيَنَّهُمْ) [Translator's note: the source prints the nūn of إن with shadda here, although the reading cited is the lightened one.], and what Sībawayh reported: (إن عمرا لمنطلق). Its being left non-governing is frequent, and this is the position of many grammarians, as in the saying of Allah the Exalted وَإِنْ كُلُّ ذلِكَ لَمَّا مَتاعُ الْحَياةِ الدُّنْيا and وَإِنْ كُلٌّ لَمَّا جَمِيعٌ لَدَيْنا مُحْضَرُونَ, and the reading of Ḥafṣ: (إن هذان لساحران), and the saying of Allah the Exalted وَإِنْ كادُوا لَيَفْتِنُونَكَ.
2- If it enters a verb, it must be left non-governing, and most often the verb is an abrogating (nāsikh) past verb, e.g. (وَإِنْ كانَتْ لَكَبِيرَةً) and (إِنْ وَجَدْنا أَكْثَرَهُمْ لَفاسِقِينَ). It may come as an abrogating imperfect verb, as in the saying of Allah the Exalted (وَإِنْ يَكادُ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا لَيُزْلِقُونَكَ). Whenever إن occurs followed by the lām with fatḥa, judge that its origin is with shadda.
2- The enjoyment of this world is little..
This verse has made clear the swiftness of this world's passing away and the ending of its pleasures, and that the Hereafter is better and more lasting.
From Sahl ibn Saʿd, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "If this world weighed with Allah as much as the wing of a gnat, He would not give a disbeliever a single drink of water from it." Narrated by al-Tirmidhī,
who said: a ḥasan gharīb hadith.
From al-Mustawrid ibn Shaddād, the ancestor of Banū Fihr, who said: I was among the riders who stopped with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ at the dead السخلة (the kid of a goat), and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Do you see how this became worthless to its owners when they threw it away?" They said: "It was because of its worthlessness that they threw it away, O Messenger of Allah." He said: "This world is more worthless to Allah than this sheep is to its owners." Narrated by al-Tirmidhī,
who said:
a ḥasan hadith.

semin-durr:2-2.t:
In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.
