His saying: {والكتاب}: if you make «حم» an oath, the wāw is a conjunction; if not, the wāw is for the oath. The treatment of this has already been given.

semin-durr:3-3.t:
His saying: {إِنَّا جَعَلْنَاهُ}: the answer to the oath. In their view this is part of eloquence, namely that the oath and what is sworn upon come from one valley. Like the saying of Abū Tammām:

3980 - And your front teeth, truly they are a fresh white pearl ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .

This is so if by «الكتاب» the Qur'an is meant. If the genus of the revealed books other than the Qur'an is meant by it, it is not of that kind. The pronoun in «جَعَلْناه» refers, on the first view, to «الكتاب», and on the second to the Qur'an, even though it is not explicitly mentioned. Here «الجَعْل» means "making into". No attention is paid to al-Zamakhsharī's error in allowing that it might mean "We created it".

semin-durr:4-4.t: His saying: {في أُمِّ الكتاب لَدَيْنَا}: the two are attached to what follows them. The lām does not prevent that. It is also possible that they are two ḥāls from what follows them, because they were originally two attributes of it, so they are attached to an omitted element. It is also possible that «لدينا» is attached to what the preceding prepositional phrase is attached to, if we make it a ḥāl from «لَعَلِيٌّ», or that it is a ḥāl from the latent pronoun in it. Likewise it is possible for the prepositional phrase to be attached to what the adverbial is attached to /, or to be a ḥāl from its pronoun, according to those who permit it to precede a semantic governing agent. It is also possible that the adverbial is a badal from the preceding prepositional phrase, or that the two are ḥāls from «الكتاب» or from «أُمِّ». Abū l-Baqāʾ mentioned these three analyses. He said: "It is not permitted for either of the two adverbials to be the khabar, because the khabar must be «عَليٌّ» on account of the lām." I say: this would prevent you from saying «إن زيداً كاتبٌ لَشاعرٌ», because he prevented what is not joined to it from being a khabar.

semin-durr:5-5.t:
His saying: {صَفْحاً}: it has five analyses. The first: it is a maṣdar in the sense of «يَضْرِب», because it is said ضَرَبَ عن كذا and أَضْرَبَ عنه meaning he turned away from it and turned his face from it. He said:

3981 - Strike away from you the cares that visit by night ... as your striking the horse's forelock with the sword

The implied form is: "Shall We turn the Reminder away from you?", i.e. shall We remove the Qur'an from you with a removal, denouncing them for that. The second: it is accusative as a ḥāl from the agent, i.e. "turning away". The third: it is accusative as the maṣdar confirming the content of the sentence, so its governing agent is omitted, like {صُنْعَ الله} [al-Naml: 88]. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said this. The fourth: it is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose). The fifth: it is accusative as an adverbial. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "«صَفْحاً» is of two kinds: either a maṣdar of صَفَح عنه when he turned away from him, accusative as a mafʿūl lahu, meaning: 'Shall We withhold from you the sending down of the Qur'an and the imposition of the proof by it, out of turning away from you?' Or in the sense of 'side', from their saying: نَظَرَ إليه بصَفْحِ وَجْهِه, and صَفْحُ وَجْهِه, meaning 'Shall We put it aside from you, to one side?', and so it is accusative as an adverbial, like ضَعْه جانباً and امْشِ جانباً. The reading «صُفْحاً» with ḍamma supports it." I say: he points to the reading of Ḥassān ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Ḍubaʿī, Sumayṭ ibn ʿUmayr and Shubayl ibn ʿUzra, who read «صُفْحاً» with ḍamma on the ṣād. It has two possibilities. One: what he mentioned, that it is a dialect form of the fatḥa form and is an adverbial. The apparent sense of Abū l-Baqāʾ's wording is that everything permitted for the fatḥa form is permitted for it, because he made it a dialect form of it, like «السُّد» and «السَّد» (al-sudd and al-sadd). The second: it is the plural of ṣafūḥ, like ṣabūr and ṣubur. It is then accusative as a ḥāl from the agent of «نَضْرِب». Al-Zamakhsharī, as is his habit, implied a verb between the hamza and the fāʾ, i.e. "Shall We neglect you so that We turn away?" You have known what is in that more than once.

His saying: «أنْ كُنتم»: Nāfiʿ and the two brothers read it with kasra, as conditional, though their transgression was established, and «إنْ» only enters on what is not established, or what is established but of unspecified time. Al-Zamakhsharī answered: "It is of the kind of condition that issues from one who is confident of the soundness of the matter and its verification because of its being established, like the hired worker's saying: 'If I have done work for you, then give me my due in full', while he knows that. But in his speech he conveys the impression that your negligence in delivering my right is the act of someone in doubt about his entitlement to it, to make him out ignorant." It was also said: the sense is of requital, and the meaning is: "Shall We turn the Reminder away from you whenever you transgress?", i.e. you will not be left without warning whenever you are a transgressing people. This is what Abū l-Baqāʾ meant by his saying: "«إنْ» was read with kasra as conditional, and what came before indicates the apodosis." The others read it with fatḥa as a cause, i.e. "because you were", like the poet's saying:

3982 - Do you grieve that the departing companion has gone away? ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .

and like it:

3983 - Do you grieve that the two ears of Qutayba were cut off? ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .

It is reported with both kasra and fatḥa. Something like this has already been discussed at the beginning of al-Māʾida. Zayd ibn ʿAlī read «إذ» with a dhāl in place of the nūn, and it carries the sense of cause.

semin-durr:6-6.t: His saying: {وَكَمْ أَرْسَلْنَا}: «كم» is declarative (khabariyya) and a fronted object. «من نبيّ» is a tamyīz (specification). «في الأوَّلين» is attached to the sending, or to an omitted element as an adjective of «نبي».

semin-durr:8-8.t: His saying: {بَطْشاً}: it has two analyses. The first: it is a tamyīz of «أشدَّ». The second: it is a ḥāl from the agent, i.e. "We destroyed them while We were seizing".

semin-durr:9-9.t: His saying: {خَلَقَهُنَّ العزيز}: He repeated the verb for emphasis, since had «العزيزُ» come without «خَلَقَهُنَّ» it would have sufficed, as when you say "Who stood?" and it is said "Zayd". In it is evidence that the venerable name in His saying {وَلَئِن سَأَلْتَهُم مَّنْ خَلَقَهُمْ لَيَقُولُنَّ الله} [al-Zukhruf: 87] is nominative as the agent, not as a mubtadaʾ, because the verb is stated explicitly in its parallel. This answer corresponds to the question in meaning; had it followed the wording, / a nominal sentence would have been used in it, like the question.

semin-durr:11-11.t: His saying: {بَلْدَةً مَّيْتاً}: the majority read it lightened. ʿĪsā and Abū Jaʿfar read it doubled. The discussion of it has already been given in Āl ʿImrān. The difference over تُخْرَجُون and تَخْرُجُون was given in al-Aʿrāf.

semin-durr:12-12.t: His saying: {مَا تَرْكَبُونَ}: «ما» is a relative noun. Its returning pronoun is omitted, i.e. "what you ride it". Rakiba, with respect to the ship, is made transitive by a preposition: {فَإِذَا رَكِبُواْ فِي الفلك} [al-ʿAnkabūt: 65], and with other than it is transitive by itself. He said: {لِتَرْكَبُوهَا} [al-Naḥl: 8]. Here the one transitive by itself prevailed over the one transitive by an intermediary, which is why the returning pronoun was omitted.

semin-durr:13-13.t:
His saying: {لِتَسْتَوُواْ}: this may be the lām of cause, which is the apparent view, or the lām of becoming, and in both it is attached to «جَعَل». Ibn ʿAṭiyya allowed it to be the lām of command, but that is remote because of how seldom it enters on the command to the addressee. «فَلْتَفْرحوا» was read as an irregular reading. In the ḥadīth: «لِتَأْخُذوا مصافَّكم». And he said:

3984 - Let you stand, O son of the best of Quraysh ... so that the needs of the Muslims be fulfilled

The grammarians stated explicitly that it is rare, except Abū l-Qāsim al-Zajjājī, who made it a good dialect form.

His saying: «على ظُهورِه»: the pronoun refers to the wording of «ما تَرْكَبون», so he made «الظهور» plural in view of its meaning and made the pronoun singular in view of its wording.

His saying: «له مُقْرِنين»: «له» is attached to «مُقْرِنين», fronted for the sake of the verse-endings. Al-muqrin is the one able to bear a thing and in control of it, from aqrānahu, i.e. he was able for it. And al-qaran is the rope. Ibn Harma said:

3985 - I was able to bear what you loaded me with, yet rarely ... can the bearing of rejection and desertion be endured, O Duʿd

And ʿAmr ibn Maʿdī Karib said:

3986 - The tribes know what ʿUqayl is ... to us in calamities, no match for us

The reality of aqranahu: he found him his match, because the difficult is not the match of the weak. He said:

3987 - And the young camel, when it is tied in a rope ... cannot withstand the onslaught of the large strong camels

«مُقْتَرنين» with a tāʾ before the rā' was also read.

semin-durr:15-15.t:
His saying: {جُزْءًا}: the first object of «الجَعْل», and «الجَعْل» is a verbal "making into". It may also mean "they named and believed". The strangest thing said here is that al-juzʾ means the female. They recited:

3988 - If a free woman one day bears only females, it is no wonder ... the free woman who bears males sometimes does so too

And another said:

3989 - I married her to the daughters of al-Aws, one who bears females ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .

Al-Zamakhsharī said: "The trace of artifice in both is evident."

semin-durr:16-16.t: His saying: {وَأَصْفَاكُم}: it may fall within the scope of the denunciation, conjoined to «اتَّخذ». It may also be a ḥāl, i.e. "or did He take, in this state", with «قد» implied according to the majority. Its like has already been discussed in

semin-durr:17-17.t: His saying: {وَإِذَا بُشِّرَ أَحَدُهُم}. Here «وجهُه مُسْوَدٌّ» was read with «مُسْوَدٌّ» nominative, as a sentence in the position of the khabar of «ظَلَّ». The ism of «ظَلَّ» is the pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn).

semin-durr:18-18.t:
His saying: {أَوَمَن يُنَشَّأُ}: «مَنْ» has two analyses. The first: that it is in the position of accusative as an object of an implied verb, i.e. "or do they make one who is raised in ornaments". The second: that it is a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is omitted, its implied form being: "or one who is raised in ornaments is a part or a child", since they made it a part for Allah. The majority read «يَنْشَأ» with fatḥa on the yāʾ and sukūn on the nūn, from نَشَأَ في كذا يَنْشأ فيه. The two brothers and Ḥafṣ read it with ḍamma on the yāʾ, fatḥa on the nūn and doubling of the shīn, in the passive, i.e. "is brought up". Al-Jaḥdarī read likewise, except that he lightened the shīn, taking it from anshaʾahu. Al-Ḥasan read «يُناشَأُ» like يُقاتَل, in the passive. The form mufāʿala comes in the sense of if'āl, like al-muʿālāt in the sense of iʿlāʾ.

His saying: {وَهُوَ فِي الخصام غَيْرُ مُبِينٍ}: the sentence is a ḥāl. «في الخصام» may be attached to an omitted element indicated by what follows, its implied form being: "and he is not clear in dispute". It may also be attached to «مُبين», and it is permitted for the muḍāf ilayhi to govern what precedes the muḍāf, because «غيرَ» has the sense of «لا». The verification of this has already been given at the end of al-Fātiḥa, together with what I recited on it and the disagreement in the question.

semin-durr:19-19.t:
His saying: {عِبَادُ الرحمن}: Nāfiʿ, Ibn Kathīr and Ibn ʿĀmir read «عند الرحمن» as an adverbial. The others read «عبادَ», plural of ʿabd, and the script admits both. Al-Aʿmash read likewise, except that he made «عبادَ» accusative on an implied verb: "those who were created as servants" or the like. ʿAbd Allāh read, and so it is in his codex, «الملائكةَ عبادَ الرحمن». Ubayy and ʿAbd al-Raḥmān / read it in the singular. «إناثاً» is the second object of «الجَعْل» in the sense of belief, or a verbal "making into". Zayd ibn ʿAlī read «أُنُثا», a plural of a plural.

His saying: «أشَهِدُوا»: Nāfiʿ read it with an opened hamza, then another with ḍamma, eased between it and the wāw, and with sukūn on the shīn. Qālūn read it with the lengthening, meaning by inserting an alif between the two hamzas, and with the shortening, meaning without the alif. The others read it with fatḥa on the shīn after one hamza. Nāfiʿ entered the hamza of reproach on «أُشْهِدُوا», a quadriliteral passive verb, and eased its second hamza, and inserted an alif between them in dislike of their coming together, and at times did not insert it, content with easing the second, which is the more apt. The others entered the hamza of denunciation on «شهدوا», triliteral, and "witness" here means presence. Al-Shaykh did not report from Nāfiʿ the easing of the second but reported it from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib.

Al-Zuhrī read «أُشْهِدُوا» as a quadriliteral passive. It has two analyses. One: that he omitted the hamza because the other reading indicates it, as given before in the reading «أعجميٌّ». The second: that the sentence is declarative, occurring as an adjective of «إناثاً», i.e. "Did they make them females whose creation was witnessed as such?"

His saying: «سَتُكْتَبُ شهادتُهم»: the majority read «سَتُكْتَبُ» with the upper tāʾ in the passive, «شهادتُهم» nominative because it stands in the place of the agent. Al-Ḥasan read «شهاداتُهم» in the plural, and al-Zuhrī «سَيَكتب» with the lower yāʾ, and in the rest like the majority. Ibn ʿAbbās, Zayd ibn ʿAlī, Abū Jaʿfar and Abū Ḥaywa read «سنكتبُ» with nūn, for majesty, and «شهادتَهم» accusative as direct object.

semin-durr:22-22.t:
His saying: {على أُمَّةٍ}: the majority read it with ḍamma on the hamza, in the sense of way and religion. Qays ibn al-Khaṭīm said:

3990 - We were upon the way of our fathers ... and the last follows the first

i.e. upon their way. And another said:

3991 - Can the possessor of a religion and an ungrateful one be equal? ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .

i.e. the possessor of a religion. Mujāhid, Qatāda and ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz read it with kasra. Al-Jawharī said: "It is the good way, a dialect form of «أُمَّة» with ḍamma." Ibn ʿAbbās read it with fatḥa, which is the single act of amm, and what is meant by it is the intention and the state.

semin-durr:24-24.t: His saying: {قال}: Ibn ʿĀmir and Ḥafṣ read «قال» as a past verb in place of «قل» as an imperative, i.e. the warner said, or the Messenger, who is the Prophet ﷺ. The command in «قل» may be addressed to the warner or to the Messenger, which is the apparent view. Abū Jaʿfar and Shayba read «جِئْناكم» with the nūn of the speakers.

semin-durr:26-26.t: His saying: {بَرَآءٌ}: the majority read it with fatḥa on the bāʾ, then an alif and a hamza after the rā'. It is originally a maṣdar that has taken the place of the adjective, which is «بَريْء», and al-Aʿmash read it so. «براء» is not made dual, plural or feminine, like maṣdars in general. Al-Zaʿfarānī and Ibn al-Munādī, from Nāfiʿ, read it with ḍamma on the bāʾ, on the pattern of ṭuwāl and kirām. It is said: ṭawīl and ṭuwāl, barīʾ and burāʾ. Al-Aʿmash read «إنِّي» with a single nūn.

semin-durr:27-27.t:
His saying: {إِلاَّ الذي فَطَرَنِي}: it has four analyses. The first: it is a disconnected exception (munqaṭiʿ), because they were only idol-worshippers. The second: it is connected, because it is reported that they associated others with the Creator.

The third: that it is genitive as a badal from the relative «ما» in His saying «ممَّا تعبدُون». Al-Zamakhsharī said this. Al-Shaykh rejected it, because that is only permitted in a negation or its like. He said: "He was misled by «براء» being in the sense of negation, and that does not help him, because it is affirmative." I say: the grammarians have interpreted that in several places in the Qur'an, such as the saying of the Exalted: {ويأبى الله إِلاَّ أَن يُتِمَّ} [al-Tawba: 32] and {وَإِنَّهَا لَكَبِيرَةٌ إِلاَّ عَلَى الخاشعين} [al-Baqara: 45]. A vacated exception does not occur in an affirmative, but since «يأبى» means "does not do", and «وإنها لكبيرة» means "is not easy and not light", that was permitted. So this is like it.

The fourth: that «إلاَّ» is an adjective in the sense of «غير», with «ما» an indefinite described noun. Al-Zamakhsharī said this. Al-Shaykh said: "He only took it out of being a relative in this analysis because he holds that «إلاَّ» in the sense of «غير» is used to describe only an indefinite", and there is disagreement on it. On this, «ما» may be a relative and «إلاَّ» in the sense of «غير» an adjective of it.

semin-durr:28-28.t:
His saying: {وَجَعَلَهَا}: the nominative pronoun refers to Ibrāhīm, peace be upon him, which is the apparent view, or to Allah. The accusative refers to the word of tawḥīd (monotheism) understood from His saying «إنني بَراءٌ» to the end, or to the fact that it is in the position of a word, so the pronoun returned to that wording on account of what is meant by it.

«في عَقْبِه» was read with sukūn on the qāf. «في عاقِبه» was also read, i.e. his heir. Ḥumayd ibn Qays read «كلمة» with kasra on the kāf and sukūn on the lām.

semin-durr:29-29.t: The majority read «مَتَّعْتُ» with the tāʾ of the speaker. Qatāda / and al-Aʿmash read it with fatḥa for the addressee: Ibrāhīm, or Muḥammad ﷺ, addressed his Lord the Exalted with that. Nāfiʿ read it so in the transmission of Yaʿqūb. Al-Aʿmash also read «بل مَتَّعْنا» with the nūn of majesty.

semin-durr:31-31.t:
His saying: {مِّنَ القريتين}: there is an omitted muḍāf in it. Some implied it: "from two men of the two towns". It was also said: "from one of the two towns". The two men are al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīra, who was in Mecca, and ʿUrwa ibn Masʿūd al-Thaqafī, who was in al-Ṭāʾif. It was also said: he used to go back and forth between the two towns, so he was ascribed to both. «رَجْل» was read with sukūn on the ʿayn, and it is a Tamīmī form.

The discussion of «سُخْرِيَّا» has already been given in al-Muʾminūn. Here ʿAmr ibn Maymūn, Ibn Muḥayṣin, Abū Rajāʾ, Ibn Abī Laylā, al-Walīd ibn Muslim and many others read it with kasra, in the well-known sense, which is making use of (istikhdām). The saying of some that it is the mockery of the rich at the poor is remote.

semin-durr:33-33.t:
His saying: {لِبُيُوتِهِمْ}: a badal ishtimāl (substitute of inclusion) with repetition of the governing agent. The two lāms are for specification. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: the first is for ownership and the second for specification. Al-Shaykh rejected this on the ground that the second is a badal, so the particle is required to be the same in meaning, not different. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "They may be like the two lāms in your saying: 'I gave him a garment for his shirt'." Al-Shaykh said: "I do not know what he meant by this." I say: he meant that the two lāms are for cause, i.e. the gift was for your sake, for the sake of your shirt, so «لقميصك» is a badal ishtimāl with repetition of the very same governing agent. It has been reported that His saying {وَوَهَبْنَا لَهُ إِسْحَاقَ} [al-Anʿām: 84] has it for cause.

His saying: «سُقُفا»: Ibn Kathīr and Abū ʿAmr read it with fatḥa on the sīn and sukūn on the qāf in the singular, intending the genus. The others read it with two ḍammas in the plural, like ruhun as a plural of rahn. In «رُهُن» there is an interpretation that is not possible here: namely that it is the plural of «رِهان», plural of rahn, because «سِقاف» as a plural of saqf has not been heard. From al-Farrāʾ: it is the plural of saqīfa, so it is like ṣaḥīfa and ṣuḥuf. «سَقَفاً» with two fatḥas was also read, as a dialect form of saqf, and «سُقوفاً» on the pattern of fals and fulūs. Abū Rajāʾ read it with ḍamma and sukūn.

«مِنْ فِضَّة» may be attached to «الجعل», or attached to an omitted element as an adjective of «سُقُف». The majority read «معارِجَ», plural of maʿraj, which is the ladder. Ṭalḥa read «معاريج», plural of miʿrāj, like mafātiḥ for mafṭaḥ and mafātīḥ for miftāḥ.

semin-durr:34-34.t: His saying: {وَسُرُراً}: plural of sarīr. The majority read it with ḍamma on the rā'. It was also read with fatḥa, which is the dialect of some of Tamīm and Kalb. It has already been mentioned that the geminated faʿīl takes fatḥa on its ʿayn when it is a noun or an adjective, like thawb jadīd and thiyāb judad, and there is discussion of it among the grammarians. Does His saying «مِنْ فضة» include the ladders, the doors and the couches? Al-Zamakhsharī said: yes, as if he holds that the conjoined shares its qualifications with that to which it is conjoined. «عليها يَتَّكئون» and «عليها يَظْهَرون» are two adjectives of what precedes them.

semin-durr:35-35.t:
His saying: {وَزُخْرُفاً}: it may be accusative by «جَعَلَ», i.e. "and We made for them ornament". Al-Zamakhsharī allowed it to be accusative by conjunction to the position of «مِنْ فضة», as if it were said: "roofs of silver and gold", i.e. some of them thus and some of them thus.

The disagreement over «لَمَّا», lightened and doubled, has already been given in Sūrat Hūd. Abū Rajāʾ and Abū Ḥaywa read «لِما» with kasra on the lām, as the lām of cause entering the relative «ما» with its returning pronoun omitted, though the ṣila is not long. The original is: "that which is enjoyment", like {تَمَاماً عَلَى الذي أَحْسَنَ} [al-Anʿām: 154] with nominative on the nūn. «إنْ» is the lightened form of the heavy, «كل» is a mubtadaʾ, and the prepositional phrase after it is its khabar, i.e. "all that was mentioned before is for that which is the enjoyment of life". The right way would have been for the distinguishing lām to enter, because it is not made to govern, except that when the evidence indicated the affirmation, omitting it was permitted, as the poet omitted it in his saying:

3992 - I am the son of those who refuse humiliation, of the house of Mālik ... and if Mālik were of noble mines

semin-durr:36-36.t:
His saying: {وَمَن يَعْشُ}: the majority read it with ḍamma on the shīn, from ʿashā yaʿshū, i.e. he feigns blindness and ignorance. Qatāda and Yaḥyā ibn Sallām read «يَعْشَ» with fatḥa, meaning "goes blind". Zayd ibn ʿAlī read «يَعْشو» with the wāw retained. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "on the basis that «مَنْ» is a relative, and the right way for this is to read «نقيضُ» nominative." Al-Shaykh said: "Its being a relative is not necessary; it is rather analysed in two ways: either by implying the omission of the vowel of the weak letter, and al-Akhfash reported it as a dialect, and evidence for it came from him in Sūrat Yūsuf; or on the basis that it is jussive by the relative «مَنْ», likening it to the conditional «مَنْ»." He said: "And if they made jussive with «الذي», which is never conditional, then all the more so what is used both as conditional and non-conditional." And he recited:

3993 - Do not dig a well wishing a brother to fall in it ... for you, not he, will fall into it
Likewise whoever wrongs people unjustly ... the consequences of what he did will strike him despite himself

/ He said: "This is the school of the Kufans, and it has a ground in analogy: namely that «الذي» resembles the conditional noun in the entry of the fāʾ into its khabar, so it resembles the conditional noun in the jussive as well. Except that the entry of the fāʾ is regular under its condition, while this is not regular."

It is said: ʿashā yaʿshū and ʿashiya yaʿshā. Some made them the same in meaning, and some distinguished: ʿashiya yaʿshā is when the affliction occurs in his sight, and its origin is the wāw, but it was turned into yāʾ because of the kasra before it, like raḍiya yarḍā; whereas ʿashā yaʿshū means he feigned that. He looked the look of the night-blind though there is no affliction in his sight, as they said ʿaraja for one who has the affliction of lameness, and ʿaruja for one who feigns lameness and walks the gait of the lame. The poet said:

3994 - I look dimly when my neighbour woman comes out ... until the curtain hides my neighbour woman

i.e. I look the look of the night-blind. And another said:

3995 - When you come to him you will approach the light of his fire ... and find the best fire, beside which is the best of kindlers

i.e. you look the look of the night-blind because of the weakness of sight from the abundance of fuel. Some distinguished: ʿashawtu ilā l-nār is when you were guided to it by a weak look. It was also said; and al-Farrāʾ said: "ʿashā yaʿshā means turns away, and ʿashiya yaʿshā means went blind." However Ibn Qutayba said: "We have not seen anyone report ʿashawtu ʿan al-shayʾ as 'I turned away from it'; it is only said taʿāshaytu ʿan kadhā when you feign heedlessness and blindness to it."

The majority read «نُقَيِّضْ» with the nūn of majesty. ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, al-Aʿmash, Yaʿqūb, al-Sulamī, and Abū ʿAmr and ʿĀṣim in a transmission from them, read «يُقَيِّضْ» with the lower yāʾ, i.e. the Most Merciful appoints. «شيطاناً» is accusative in both readings. Ibn ʿAbbās read «يُقَيَّضْ» in the passive, «شيطانٌ» nominative, standing in the place of the agent.

semin-durr:37-37.t: His saying: {وَإِنَّهُمْ لَيَصُدُّونَهُمْ}: apparently the two accusative pronouns refer to «مَنْ» in respect of its meaning. He considered its wording first, so he used the singular in «له» and «له», then considered its meaning, so he used the plural in His saying «وإنَّهم ليَصُدُّوْنَهم». The nominative pronoun refers to the devil, because the genus is meant by it, and because every disbeliever has a companion with him. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "The first pronoun is for the devils and the second for the disbelievers. The implied form is: 'and the devils turn the sporting disbelievers away'."

semin-durr:38-38.t:
His saying: {إِذَا جَآءَنَا}: Abū ʿAmr, the two brothers and Ḥafṣ read «جاءنا» with the verb attributed to a singular pronoun that refers to the wording of «مَنْ», which is the one who feigns blindness. This is then one of those in which the wording is followed, then the meaning, then the wording again. It was first carried on its wording in His saying «نُقَيِّضْ له» and «فهو له», then made plural on its meaning in His saying «وإنَّهم ليَصُدُّونهم» and «يَحْسَبون أنهم», then returned to its wording in His saying «جاءنا». The others read «جاءانا», attributed to a dual pronoun, which are the one who feigns blindness and his companion.

His saying: «بُعْدَ المَشْرِقَيْنِ»: it was said that he meant the east and the west, and the predominant one was used, like al-ʿUmarayn and al-qamarayn. It was also said that he meant by the two easts of the sun its rising place on the shortest day and its rising place on the longest day. It was also said: the distance of the two easts from the two wests.

His saying: «فبِئْسَ القَرينُ»: its specified subject of the verb of censure is omitted, i.e. "you".

semin-durr:39-39.t:
His saying: {وَلَن يَنفَعَكُمُ}: there are two views about its agent. The first: that it is pronounced, namely «أنَّكم» and what is within its scope. The implied form is: "and your sharing in the punishment will not benefit you by way of consolation", as sharing in the misfortunes of this world benefits, the afflicted consoling himself with one like him. From it is the saying of al-Khansāʾ:

3996 - Were it not for the multitude of those weeping around me ... over their brothers, I would have killed myself
They do not weep like my brother, but ... I console myself for him by consolation

The second: that it is a latent pronoun. Some implied it as the pronoun of wishing, indicated by His saying {ياليت بَيْنِي}, i.e. "your wishing for distance will not benefit you". Some: "your gathering will not benefit you". Some: "your wrongdoing and your denial". The wording of those who said the agent is omitted aims at the stated latent pronoun, not at omission, since the agent is omitted only in places of which this is not one. On this analysis «أنَّكم» is a cause, i.e. "because you", the preposition being omitted, and the disagreement runs in its position: is it accusative or genitive? What supports the latent agent, rather than «أنَّكم» being the agent, is the reading «إنكم» with kasra, for it is / a resumptive clause giving the cause.

His saying: «إذْ ظَلَمْتُمْ»: the grammarians found this verse problematic. The reason is that His saying «اليومَ» is an adverbial of the present, «إذ» is an adverbial of the past, and «يَنْفَعَكم» is future because it is joined with «لن», which negates the future. Apparently it governs both adverbials, but how can a future event that has not yet occurred govern a present or past adverbial? This is not permitted. As to its governing the present adverbial, it was answered that this is by way of closeness, because the present is close to the future, so that is permitted. The Exalted said: {فَمَن يَسْتَمِعِ الآن} [al-Jinn: 9], and the poet said:

3997 - . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... I shall strive now that it has reached its time

This is only persuasive, otherwise the future is rationally impossible to occur in the present. As for His saying «إذ», people have many analyses of it. Ibn Jinnī said: "I consulted Abū ʿAlī about it repeatedly, and the last thing I obtained from him is that this world and the next are connected, and they are the same in the judgement of Allah the Exalted and His knowledge, so «إذ» is a badal from «اليوم», as if it were future or as if «اليوم» were past." Al-Zamakhsharī went this way. He said: "«إذْ» is a badal from «اليوم»", and al-Zamakhsharī took it in the sense of: since your wrongdoing has become clear and proven, and no one, nor you, is left with any doubt that you were wrongdoers. Its like:

3998 - When we trace our descent, no base woman bore me ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .

i.e. it has become clear that I am the son of a noble woman. Al-Shaykh said: "The badal is not permitted as long as «إذ» is on its basic placement as past; if it is made for absolute time, it is permitted." I say: it is not known of «إذ» that it is for absolute time; rather it is placed for a specific time in the past, like yesterday. The second: that there is an omitted muḍāf in the sentence, its implied form being: "after you wronged".

The third: that it is for cause. It is then a particle of cause like the lām. The fourth: that the governing agent of «إذ» is that implied agent, not its pronoun. The implied form is: "your wrongdoing, or your denial, will not benefit you since you wronged." The fifth: that the governing agent of «إذ» is what the meaning indicates. It is as if He said: "but your gathering will not benefit you since you wronged." Al-Ḥawfī said this, then said: "The agent of «يَنْفَعَكم» is the sharing." End of quotation. Apparently this is contradictory, because he first made the agent your gathering and then finally made it the sharing. He also prevented «إذ» from being a badal from «اليوم» because they differ in signification. In the book of Abū l-Baqāʾ: "It was also said: «إذْ» has the sense of «أَنْ», i.e. «أَنْ ظَلَمْتُم»." He did not restrict it to being «أَنْ» with fatḥa or kasra, but al-Shaykh said: "It was also said: «إذ» is a particle of cause in the sense of «أَنْ»", meaning with fatḥa; and he apparently meant what Abū l-Baqāʾ mentioned, except that calling «أنْ» a cause is figurative, for it is on the omission of the particle of cause, i.e. «لأَنْ», so because of its accompanying it and its dispensing with it, he named it by its name. One should not believe that in the book of Abū l-Baqāʾ it is with kasra as conditional, because that meaning is remote.

«إنكم» was read with kasra as a resumptive clause giving the cause. The agent is then a latent pronoun according to one of the mentioned analyses.

semin-durr:41-41.t: His saying: {فَإِمَّا نَذْهَبَنَّ}: the discussion of it has already been given recently.

semin-durr:42-42.t: «نُرِيَنْكَ» was also read with the light nūn. The majority read {أُوحِيَ} [al-Zukhruf: 43] in the passive with fatḥa on the yāʾ, and some of the reciters of Syria put sukūn on it for lightness. Al-Ḍaḥḥāk read «أَوْحَى» in the active, the agent being Allah the Exalted.

semin-durr:45-45.t: His saying: {مَنْ أَرْسَلْنَا}: it has three analyses, the clearest of which is that «مَنْ» is a relative and is the object of the asking. It is as if it were said: "ask the one whom We sent before you about what they were sent with, for they were sent only with tawḥīd." The second: that it is on the omission of the preposition, as the one asked about. The one asked, which is the first object, is omitted, its implied form being: "and ask [us] about whom We sent". The third: that «مَنْ» is interrogative, nominative as a mubtadaʾ, and «أَرْسَلَ» is its khabar. The sentence suspends the asking, so it is in the position of accusative by removal of the preposition. This is not apparent; rather what apparently suspends the asking is the interrogative sentence in His saying «أَجَعَلْنا».

semin-durr:47-47.t: His saying: {إِذَا هُم مِّنْهَا يَضْحَكُونَ}: al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you ask: how is it permitted for «لَمَّا» to be answered by the sudden «إذا»? I say: because the verb of suddenness is implied with it, and it is the accusative-assigning agent in its position, as if it were said: 'When he came to them with Our signs, they were suddenly surprised at the time of their laughter.'" Al-Shaykh said: "We do not know anything like what he went to, that the sudden «إذا» is accusative by an implied verb, its implied form being 'surprised'. Rather the schools are three: either it is a particle and needs no governing agent, or an adverbial of place, or an adverbial of time. If a khabar is mentioned after the noun that follows it, it is accusative as an adverbial, and the governing agent in it is that khabar, like «خرجتُ فإذا زيدٌ قائمٌ», its implied form being: 'I went out, and in the place where I went out Zayd is standing', or 'in the time when I went out Zayd is standing'. If no khabar is mentioned after the noun, or / a noun accusative as ḥāl is mentioned: if the noun is a body and we say it is an adverbial of place, the matter is clear, like «خرجْتُ فإذا الأسدُ», i.e. 'in the presence is the lion', or «فإذا الأسدُ رابضاً». If we say it is an adverbial of time, it is on the omission of a muḍāf, so that time is not predicated of a body, like «خَرَجْتُ فإذا الأسدُ», i.e. 'in the time is the presence of the lion'. If the noun is an event, it may be a place or time, and there is no need to imply a muḍāf, like «خرجْتُ فإذا القتالُ»; if you wish you may imply 'in the presence is the fighting', or 'in the time is the fighting'." [Translator's note: the editor of the source adds:] In this there is condensation and a great addition of examples; I saw that leaving them out would be damaging.

semin-durr:48-48.t:
His saying: {إِلاَّ هِيَ أَكْبَرُ}: a sentence occurring as an adjective of His saying «مِنْ آية», so its position is judged genitive in view of the wording, and accusative in view of the position. In the meaning of His saying {أَكْبَرُ مِنْ أُخْتِهَا} there are several views. The first, said by Ibn ʿAṭiyya: that they regard the sign that comes as great because of the newness of its matter and its occurrence, since they had grown used to the preceding sign, so the matter of the second becomes great and grows. This is as he said:

3999 - Though wounds heal, we are only charged ... with the nearer, even if what has passed was grave

The second, mentioned by some: that the meaning is "except that it is greater than its preceding sister", the adjective being omitted because it is known. The third, al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you ask: this is contradictory speech, because its meaning is: there is no sign among the nine except that it is greater than every one of them, so each one would be both superior and inferior in one state. I say: the aim of this speech is to describe them as great such that they hardly differ in it. Such is the habit with things that are close in merit to a slight degree: people's opinions differ in ranking them, so some prefer this one and some prefer that, and perhaps the opinions of one person differ about them, as in the saying of the Ḥamāsī poet:

4000 - Whomever of them you meet you say, 'I met their chief' ... like the stars by which the night traveller is guided

And the Anmārī woman said about all her sons: 'May I be bereaved of them if I know which of them is best; they are like a hollow ring, one cannot tell where its two ends are.'" End of his words. [Translator's note: the editor of the source comments:] The beginning of it is very harsh, as if the expressions were too narrow for him until he said what he said; though his answer is good, his question is harsh. The disagreement over {ياأيها الساحر} has already been given in al-Nūr.

semin-durr:50-50.t: Abū Ḥaywa read «يَنْكِثُوْن» with kasra on the kāf. It is a dialect form.

semin-durr:51-51.t:
His saying: {وهذه الأنهار}: «وهذه» has two analyses. The first: that it is a mubtadaʾ, with the wāw for ḥāl. «الأنهارُ» is an adjective of the demonstrative, or an ʿaṭf bayān. «تجري» is the khabar. The sentence is a ḥāl from the yāʾ of «لي». The second: that «هذه» is conjoined to «مُلْك مِصْرَ», and on this «تَجْري» is a ḥāl, i.e. "Is not the dominion of Egypt and these rivers flowing", i.e. the two things.

His saying: «تُبْصِرونَ»: the majority read it in the second person, for the one he addressed. ʿĪsā read it with kasra on the nūn, i.e. «تُبْصِروني». In the majority reading the object is omitted, i.e. "you see my dominion and my greatness". Fahd ibn al-Ṣaqr read «يُبْصِرون» with the yāʾ of the third person: either as a shift (iltifāt) from the second person to the third, or as a reply to the people of Mūsā.

semin-durr:52-52.t:
His saying: {أَمْ أَنَآ خَيْرٌ}: there are several views on «أم». The first: that it is disconnected (munqaṭiʿa), and so is implied as «بل» for the shift of transition, and the hamza of denunciation. The second: that it only has the sense of «بل», as in:

4001 - She appeared like the horn of the sun in the brilliance of the forenoon ... and her form, or are you more beautiful in the eye

i.e. "rather you". The third: that it is disconnected in wording, connected in meaning. Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "«أمْ» here is disconnected in wording because a sentence follows it in the wording, but in meaning it is connected and equivalent, since the meaning is: am I better than him or not, and which of us is better." This is a strange expression, that it be disconnected in wording and connected in meaning, because they are two different meanings; for disconnection requires a turning away, either by invalidation or by transition. The fourth: that it is connected, and the equivalent is omitted, its implied form being: "or do you see". This is not permitted except when «لا» comes after «أم», as in: أتقومُ أم لا؟, i.e. "or do you not stand?", and أزيدٌ عندك أم لا؟, i.e. "or is he not with you?". Omitting it without «لا» is not permitted, though the omission of «أم» with the equivalent has occurred, and it is very rare. The poet said:

4002 - My heart called me to her; I am to her affair ... listening, and I do not know whether pursuing her is right guidance

i.e. "or error". Al-Shaykh had reported from Sībawayh that this is the equivalent «أم», i.e. "or do you see the matter which deserves to be seen with him, namely that he is better than Mūsā". He said: "Al-Zamakhsharī began with this view, and said: «أم /» is connected, because the meaning is: 'Do you not see, or do you see?', except that he put His saying «أنا خيرٌ» in the place of «تُبْصِرون», because if they say 'You are better', they are seeing people in his view; and this is putting the cause in the position of the effect." Al-Shaykh said: "This is very strained, since the equivalent is only a counterpart of what precedes. If the equivalent is a verbal sentence, what precedes is a verbal sentence or a nominal sentence from which a verbal one can be implied, like {أَدَعَوْتُمُوهُمْ أَمْ أَنْتُمْ صَامِتُونَ} [al-Aʿrāf: 193], because its meaning is 'or have you been silent'. Here no verbal sentence can be implied from it, because His saying {أَمْ أَنَآ خَيْرٌ} is not the counterpart of His saying «أفلا تُبْصِرون». And if what precedes is a noun, the equivalent is a noun, or a verbal sentence from which a noun can be implied, like the saying:

4003 - Is he one with deformed hands, or has he been made complete

where «أتمَّت» is the equivalent of the noun, so the implied form is: 'or a completer'." I say: what he rejected in al-Zamakhsharī is a rejection of Sībawayh, because he is the first to have said it, and likewise his saying that the equivalent after «أم» is only omitted when «لا» follows it is open to consideration, since Sībawayh permitted omitting the equivalent without «لا», so it is a rejection of Sībawayh too.

[His saying: {وَلاَ يَكَادُ يُبِينُ}: this sentence may be conjoined to the ṣila, or resumptive, or a ḥāl.] The majority read «يُبين» from abāna, and al-Bāqir read «يَبين» with fatḥa from bāna, i.e. appeared.

semin-durr:53-53.t: His saying: {أَسْوِرَةٌ}: Ḥafṣ read «أَسْوِرَة» like aḥmira. The others read «أساوِرَة». So aswira is the plural of siwār, like ḥimār and aḥmira, and it is a plural of paucity (jamʿ qilla), and asāwira is the plural of iswār in the sense of siwār. It is said: a woman's siwār and her iswār. The origin is asāwīr with yāʾ, so the tāʾ of the feminine was substituted for the long vowel, like zanādiqa. It was also said: rather it is the plural of aswira, so it is a plural of a plural. Ubayy and al-Aʿmash, and it is reported from Abū ʿAmr, read «أساوِر» without tāʾ. It is also reported from Ubayy and ʿAbd Allāh «أساْوِير». Al-Ḍaḥḥāk read «أَلْقَى» in the active, i.e. Allah, and «وأساوِرة» accusative as object. «مِنْ ذَهَبٍ» is an adjective of «أَساورة». It is also possible that this «مِنْ» is the one entering the tamyīz.

semin-durr:55-55.t: His saying: {آسَفُونَا}: transitivised by the hamza of transitivity from asifa, meaning to be angry. The meaning: "they angered Us by their opposition to Our command". In the exegesis: "they grieved Our friends", meaning the magicians.

semin-durr:56-56.t:
His saying: {سَلَفاً}: the two brothers read it with two ḍammas, and the others with two fatḥas. The first admits three analyses. The first: that it is the plural of salīf, like raghīf and rughuf. Al-Qāsim ibn Maʿn heard from the Arabs: "a salīf of the people passed". Al-salīf of the people is like a party of them. The second: that it is the plural of sālif, like ṣābir and ṣubur. The third: that it is the plural of salaf, like asad and usud. The second admits two analyses. The first: that it is a plural of sālif, like ḥāris and ḥaras, and khādim and khadam. This is in reality a collective noun, not a broken plural, since the pattern faʿal is not among the broken-plural forms. The second: that it is a maṣdar applied to a group. You say salafa l-rajulu yaslufu salafan, i.e. went before. A man's salaf are his forefathers who went before, and the plural is aslāf and sulāf. Ṭufayl said:

4004 - They passed on as predecessors; the middle path is theirs ... the vicissitudes of death turn men over

ʿAlī, may Allah honour his face, and Mujāhid read «سُلَفاً» with ḍamma on the sīn and fatḥa on the lām. It has two analyses, the better known of which is that it is the plural of sulfa, like ghurfa and ghuraf, and al-sulfa is the nation. It was also said: the original is «سُلُفاً» with two ḍammas, and a fatḥa was substituted for the ḍamma.

semin-durr:57-57.t:
His saying: {مَثَلاً}: either a second object, if it has the sense of "made", otherwise a ḥāl.

His saying: «يَصِدُّون»: Nāfiʿ, Ibn ʿĀmir and al-Kisāʾī read «يَصُدُّون» with ḍamma on the ṣād. The others read it with kasra. It was said that they have one meaning, and that is the correct view, and the wording is said: ṣadda yaṣiddu and yaṣuddu, like ʿakafa yaʿkifu and yaʿkufu, and yaʿrushu and yaʿrishu. It was also said that the ḍamma is from al-ṣudūd, which is turning away. Ibn ʿAbbās denied the ḍamma, though it is reported from ʿAlī, may Allah be pleased with them both, and Allah knows best, before it reached the level of tawātur.

semin-durr:58-58.t:
His saying: {وقالوا أَآلِهَتُنَا خَيْرٌ}: the people of Kufa read the second hamza with full realisation, and the others ease it between the two (bayna bayna). None of the reciters, whose rule it is to separate two hamzas with an alif, inserted an alif, in dislike of four similar letters in succession, and all of them changed the third hamza into an alif. / Some further clarification is needed: «آلِهة» is the plural of ilāh, like ʿimād and aʿmida, so the origin is «أَأْلِهَة» with two hamzas: the first is augmentative, the second is the fāʾ of the word. The second fell quiescent after a hamza with fatḥa, so it had to be turned into an alif, like amina and its class. Then the hamza of interrogation entered the word, so two hamzas met in the pronunciation: the first for interrogation and the second the hamza of the pattern afʿila. The Kufans did not take their meeting into account, so they left them as they were. Others found it heavy, so they lightened the second by easing it between the two, and the third by a pure alif that was not changed at all. Most of the people of this age recite this word with one hamza followed by an alif, in the form of a statement. None of the seven read it so, in what I have read with, except that it is reported that Warsh read it so in the transmission of Abū l-Azhar. It admits the interrogative like the majority, the particle of interrogation having been omitted because «أم» indicates it, which is frequent; and it admits that he read it as a pure statement, in which case «أم» is disconnected and is implied as «بل» and the hamza.

As for the group, in their view it is connected. His saying «أم هو», in the reading of the majority, is conjoined to «آلهتنا», and is a conjunction of single words. The implied form is: "Are our gods better, or he", i.e. which of them is better. In the reading of Warsh, «هو» is a mubtadaʾ, and its khabar is omitted, its implied form being: "rather, is he better", and «أم» is then not a conjunction.

His saying: «جَدَلاً»: a mafʿūl li-ajlihi, i.e. for the sake of disputation and wrangling, not to show the truth. It was also said: it is a maṣdar in the position of ḥāl, i.e. "only as disputers".

Ibn Miqsam read «جِدالاً», and both analyses apply to it. The apparent view is that «هو» refers to ʿĪsā, like the other pronouns. It was also said that it refers to the Prophet ﷺ.

semin-durr:60-60.t:
His saying: {لَجَعَلْنَا مِنكُمْ مَّلاَئِكَةً}: there are several views on this «مِنْ». The first: that it has the sense of "in place of", i.e. "We would have made in your place". Among it also is {أَرَضِيتُمْ بالحياة الدنيا مِنَ الآخرة} [al-Tawba: 38], i.e. in place of it. He recited:

4005 - They took the pregnant camels from the weaned foal by force ... unjustly, and young camels were written down for the commander

And another said:

4006 - A girl who has not eaten the thin bread ... and has not tasted pistachios from among the herbs

The second, which is the famous one: that it is partitive. The interpretation of the verse in their view: "We would have begotten from you, O men, angels on earth who succeed you as your children succeed you, as We begot ʿĪsā from a female without a male." Al-Zamakhsharī mentioned it. The third: that it is partitive. Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "It was said: the meaning is 'We would have turned some of you into angels'." [Translator's note: the source gives the second and third views both as «تبعيضية»; this is as written.] Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "We would have made a replacement from you."

semin-durr:61-61.t:
His saying: {وَإِنَّهُ لَعِلْمٌ}: the famous view is that the pronoun refers to ʿĪsā, meaning his descent at the end of time. It was also said that the pronoun refers to the Qur'an, i.e. in it is knowledge of the Hour and its terrors, or it is a sign of its nearness. In it: {اقترب لِلنَّاسِ حِسَابُهُمْ} [al-Anbiyāʾ: 1] and {اقتربت الساعة} [al-Qamar: 1]. It was also said: it refers to the Prophet ﷺ. From it: "I was sent, I and the Hour, like these two (fingers)."

The majority read «عِلْم» as a maṣdar. It was made "knowledge" by way of exaggeration, since knowledge is attained by it, or since it is a condition by which that is known, it was called knowledge. Ibn ʿAbbās, Abū Hurayra, Abū Mālik al-Ghifārī and Zayd ibn ʿAlī read «لَعَلَمٌ» with fatḥa on the first and second letters, i.e. a condition and a sign. Abū Naḍra and ʿIkrima read likewise, except that they made it definite with the lām, so they read «للعَلَمُ», i.e. the well-known sign.

semin-durr:67-67.t: His saying: {الأخلاء يَوْمَئِذٍ}: a mubtadaʾ, and its khabar is «عَدُوٌّ». The tanwīn in «يومئذٍ» is a substitute for a sentence, its implied form being: "on the day when the Hour comes upon them". The governing agent in «يَوْمئذ» is the word «عَدُوٌّ», i.e. their enmity on that day.

semin-durr:68-68.t: His saying: {ياعبادي}: Abū Bakr, from ʿĀṣim, read «يا عبادِيَ، لا خَوْفٌ» with fatḥa on the yāʾ. The two brothers, Ibn Kathīr and Ḥafṣ omitted it in both continuation and pause. The others retained it with sukūn. The majority read «لا خوفٌ» with nominative and tanwīn, either as a mubtadaʾ or as the ism of «لا», which is rare. Ibn Muḥayṣin read it without tanwīn, on the omission of a muḍāf and waiting for it: "no fear of anything". Al-Ḥasan and Ibn Abī Isḥāq read it with fatḥa, as the lā of generic negation (lā al-tabriʾa), which in their view is more emphatic.

semin-durr:69-69.t: His saying: {الذين آمَنُواْ}: it may be an adjective of «عبادي», or a badal from it, or an ʿaṭf bayān of it, or cut off (maqṭūʿ), accusative or nominative.

semin-durr:71-71.t:
His saying: {يُطَافُ}: before it something is omitted, i.e. "they enter; there is circulated". Al-ṣiḥāf is the plural of ṣaḥfa, like jafna and jifān. Al-Jawharī said: "The ṣaḥfa is like the qaṣʿa (bowl). Al-Kisāʾī said: the largest of bowls is the jafna, then the qaṣʿa, which satisfies ten, then the ṣaḥfa, which satisfies five, then the miʾkala, which satisfies / two or three men." The ṣaḥīfa is the book, and the plural is ṣuḥuf and ṣaḥāʾif. Al-Kisāʾī, in one transmission, pronounced «بِصحاف» with imāla. Al-akwāb is a plural. It was said: it is like the ewer except that it has no handle. It was also said: except that it has no spout. It was also said: except that it has neither handle nor spout together. Al-Jawālīqī said: "so that the drinker can drink from wherever he wishes, for the handle prevents that."

ʿAdī said:

4007 - Reclining, his doors rattling ... the slave runs around him with the cup

The implied form is: "and cups of gold", or he did not intend to restrict them.

His saying: {مَا تَشْتَهِيهِ الأنفس}: Nāfiʿ, Ibn ʿĀmir and Ḥafṣ read «تَشْتهيه» with the returning pronoun to the relative retained, like His saying {الذي يَتَخَبَّطُهُ الشيطان} [al-Baqara: 275]. The others omitted it, like His saying {أهذا الذي بَعَثَ الله رَسُولاً} [al-Furqān: 41]. This reading is similar to His saying {وَمَا عَمِلَتْهُ أَيْدِيهِمْ} [Yā Sīn: 35], and that was discussed in Yā Sīn. This hāʾ in this sūra is written in the codices of Medina and Syria and omitted from the others. Abū ʿAbd Allāh al-Fāsī, the commentator on the qaṣīda, made a slip, and his pen went ahead and wrote: "and the hāʾ in it is omitted in the codices of Medina and Syria and present in the others." He meant to write "present in the codices of Medina and Syria and omitted from the others", but he reversed it. In the codex of ʿAbd Allāh it is {تَشْتَهِيهِ الأنفس وَتَلَذُّ الأعين} with the hāʾ in both.

semin-durr:73-73.t: His saying: {مِّنْهَا تَأْكُلُونَ}: «مِنْ» is partitive or for the beginning of the range, and the prepositional phrase was fronted for the sake of the verse-ending.

semin-durr:75-75.t: His saying: {لاَ يُفَتَّرُ عَنْهُمْ}: a circumstantial sentence (ḥāl), and likewise {وَهُمْ فِيهِ مُبْلِسُونَ}. ʿAbd Allāh read «وهُمْ فيها», i.e. in the Fire, since «العذاب» indicates it.

semin-durr:76-76.t:
His saying: {ولكن كَانُواْ هُمُ الظالمين}: the majority read it with yāʾ (accusative «الظالمين») as the khabar of «كان», and «هم» is either a separator (faṣl) or emphasis. ʿAbd Allāh and Abū Zayd, the two grammarians, read «الظالمون» on the basis that «هو» is a mubtadaʾ and «الظالمون» its khabar, the sentence being the khabar of «كان», and it is the dialect of Tamīm. Abū Zayd said: "I heard them reciting «تَجِدُوْه عند الله هو خيرٌ وأعظمُ أجراً» with nominative." Qays ibn Dharīḥ said:

4008 - You long for Laylā though you are the one who left her ... and you had power over her in the open field, you were the more able

with «أقدرُ» nominative, and «أنت» a separator or emphasis. Sībawayh said: "It has reached us that Ruʾba used to say «أظنُّ زيداً هو خيرٌ منك»", meaning with nominative.

semin-durr:77-77.t: His saying: {يامالك}: the majority read it without truncation (tarkhīm). ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, ʿAbd Allāh, Ibn Waththāb and al-Aʿmash read «يا مالِ», truncated, in the dialect of those who wait. Abū l-Siwār al-Ghanawī read «يا مالُ», indeclinable on ḍamma, in the dialect of those who do not intend (the omitted letter).

semin-durr:79-79.t:
His saying: {أَمْ أبرموا}: «أم» is disconnected. Ibrām is making firm, and its origin is in twisting. It is said: abrama l-ḥabl, i.e. he made its twisting firm, which is the second twisting, and the first is called saḥīl. Zuhayr said:

4009 - By my life, how excellent are the two chiefs you two were found ... in every condition, whether loosely twisted or firmly twisted

semin-durr:81-81.t:
His saying: {إِن كَانَ للرحمن}: it was said: it is conditional in its usual sense. Its interpretation is disputed. It was said: if that were sound, I would be the first to worship him, but it is not at all sound, by decisive proof, for he made worship depend on the existence of a child, which is impossible in itself, so what depends on it is impossible like it. So in form it is an affirmation of the existence and the worship, and in meaning a negation of both in the most emphatic and strongest way. Al-Zamakhsharī mentioned it. It was also said: "if he has a child by your claim". It was also said: «العابدين» means "the disdainful", from ʿabida yaʿbadu when one is intensely disdainful, so he is ʿabid and ʿābid. The reading of al-Sulamī and al-Yamānī «العَبِدين» without an alif supports it. Al-Khalīl reported a strange reading, «العَبْدِيْن» with sukūn on the bāʾ, which is a lightening of the reading of al-Sulamī, whose origin is the kasra. Ibn ʿArafa said: "It is said ʿabida with kasra, yaʿbadu with fatḥa, so he is ʿabid, and rarely ʿābid, and the Qur'an does not come with the rare or the irregular." I say: he means that the analysis of those who said that «العابدين» means "the disdainful" is not sound; then he said, like Mujāhid's saying. Al-Farazdaq said:

4010 - Those are my fathers, so bring me their like ... and I disdain to satirise Kulayb through Dārim

i.e. I disdain. And another said:

4011 - Whenever the friend wishes he cuts off his close companion ... and is, without doubt, held in contempt unjustly

Abū ʿUbayda said: "Its meaning is 'the deniers'." It is said: ʿabadanī ḥaqqī, i.e. he denied me it. Abū Ḥātim said: "al-ʿabid with kasra on the bāʾ means the very angry", and it is a good sense, i.e. if he has a child by your claim, I am the first to be angry at that.

It was also said: «إنْ» is negative, i.e. "he did not have"; then He reported with His saying {فَأَنَاْ أَوَّلُ العابدين}, and the fāʾ is causal. Makkī prevented it from being negative. He said: "because it gives the impression that you negated a child from Allah only in the past and not in what is to come, and this is impossible."

People have answered Makkī and said: «كان» indicates continuity, as in His saying {وَكَانَ الله غَفُوراً رَّحِيماً} [al-Nisāʾ: 96] and countless others. The correct view of the grammarians' schools is that it does not indicate discontinuation, and the one who says that says it where there is no indication, like the mentioned verses. The disagreement over the two readings walad and wuld was given in Maryam.

semin-durr:83-83.t: His saying: {يُلاَقُواْ}: the majority read it from mulāqāt. Ibn Muḥayṣin, and it is reported from Abū ʿAmr, read «يَلْقَوا» from laqiya.

semin-durr:84-84.t:
His saying: {وَهُوَ الذي فِي السمآء إله}: «في السماء» is attached to «إله» because it has the sense of "worshipped", i.e. worshipped in the heaven and worshipped on the earth. It is then said: the ṣila can only be a sentence or what is in the interpretation of one, namely the adverbial and its equivalent, and nothing of that is here. The answer: the mubtadaʾ is omitted because the meaning indicates it, and that omitted element is the returning pronoun, its implied form being: "and He is the One who in the heaven is a god and on the earth is a god", and it was only / omitted because of the length of the ṣila through the governed element, since the prepositional phrase is attached to «إله». Like it: «ما أنا بالذي قائلٌ لك سوءاً».

Al-Shaykh said: "Its length through conjunction to it made it good, as its length through the governed element made it good in their saying «قائل [لك] شيئاً»." I say: its occurrence in the verse and in what he reported is the same, for the ṣila became long through the governed element in both, and the conjunction is a further matter beyond that, so it is an addition to the goodness of the omission. It is not permitted for the prepositional phrase to be a fronted khabar and «إله» a postponed mubtadaʾ, so that the sentence is not left without a link, since it would then be like «جاء الذي في الدار زيد». If you make the prepositional phrase the ṣila, with a pronoun in it referring to the relative, and make «إله» a badal from it, Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "it is permitted but weak, because the overall aim is to establish divinity, not His being in the heaven and the earth, and it would also be corrupt in another respect, namely His saying {وَفِي الأرض إله}, because it is conjoined to what precedes it, and if you do not imply what we mentioned it becomes cut off from it and the meaning would be: that there is a god on the earth." End of quotation. Al-Shaykh said: "The ṣila may be the preposition and its genitive noun, and the meaning is: that He is in both by His divinity and lordship, since taking it as settling in place is impossible."

ʿUmar, ʿAlī and ʿAbd Allāh, in a group, read {وَهُوَ الذي فِي السمآء الله}. The proper name was also given the sense of a derived noun, so the prepositional phrase is attached to it. Like it: «هو حاتمٌ في طَيِّئ», i.e. the generous one among them. And like it: "Pharaoh of the punishment".

semin-durr:85-85.t:
His saying: {وَإِلَيْهِ تُرْجَعُونَ}: the two brothers and Ibn Kathīr read it with the lower yāʾ, and the others with the upper tāʾ, and in both it is passive. It was also read in the second person in the active.

The majority also read «يَدْعُوْنَ» with the yāʾ of the third person, the pronoun referring to the relative. Al-Sulamī and Ibn Waththāb read it with the tāʾ of the second person, and al-Aswad ibn Yazīd with doubling of the dāl, and the reading with tāʾ and yāʾ together with that is reported from him.

semin-durr:86-86.t: His saying: {إِلاَّ مَن شَهِدَ بالحق}: there are two views on it. The first: that it is connected, and the meaning is: "except those who bear witness to the truth", like ʿUzayr and the angels, for they have the power of intercession by Allah's giving them ownership of it. It was also said: it is disconnected, in the sense that these do not intercede except for the one who bears witness to the truth, i.e. but those who bear witness to the truth, these intercede for them. So they implied it. In this implied form the exception may be connected, with the object omitted, its implied form being: "and those whom they call upon besides Him do not have the power of intercession for anyone except for the one who bore witness".

semin-durr:87-87.t: The majority read «فأنَّى يُؤْفَكون» in the third person. It is reported from Abū ʿAmr in the second person.

semin-durr:88-88.t:
His saying: {وَقِيلِهِ}: Ḥamza and ʿĀṣim read it genitive. The others read it accusative. The genitive has two analyses. The first: it is conjoined to «الساعة», i.e. "with Him is knowledge of his saying", i.e. the saying of Muḥammad or ʿĪsā, peace be upon them. Al-qawl, al-qāl and al-qīl have one meaning; the maṣdars came on these patterns. The second: that the wāw is for an oath. The answer is either omitted, its implied form being "you will surely be given victory" or "I will surely do to them what I wish", or mentioned, namely His saying {إِنَّ هؤلاء قَوْمٌ لاَّ يُؤْمِنُونَ}. Al-Zamakhsharī mentioned it.

As for the accusative reading, it has eight analyses. The first: it is accusative on the position of «الساعة», as if it were said: "He knows the Hour and knows his saying thus". The second: it is conjoined to «سِرَّهم ونجواهم», i.e. "We do not know their secret and their private talk, and We do not know his saying". The third: conjoined to the omitted object of «يكتُبون», i.e. "they write that and they write his saying thus too". The fourth: conjoined to the omitted object of «يعلمون», i.e. "they know that and know his saying". The fifth: it is a maṣdar, i.e. "he said his saying". The sixth: that it is accusative by an implied verb, i.e. "Allah knows the saying of His Messenger", who is Muḥammad ﷺ. The seventh: that it is accusative on the position of «بالحق», i.e. "he bore witness to the truth and to his saying". The eighth: that it is accusative on the omission of the particle of oath, as in:

4012 - . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... By Allah's trust, that is the tharīd

Al-Aʿraj, Abū Qilāba, Mujāhid and al-Ḥasan read it nominative, and it has several analyses. [The first:] nominative by conjunction to «علمُ الساعةِ» with an implied muḍāf, i.e. "and with Him is knowledge of his saying", then it was omitted and this was put in its place. The second: it is nominative as a mubtadaʾ, and the sentence from «يا رب» to the end is the khabar. The third: it is a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is omitted, its implied form being: "and his saying such-and-such is heard" or "accepted". The fourth: that it is a mubtadaʾ whose origin is the oath, like their saying «ايمُنُ الله» and «لَعَمْرُ الله», so its khabar is omitted. The answer is as above. Al-Zamakhsharī mentioned this too.

A group preferred the accusative reading. Al-Naḥḥās said: "The clear reading is the accusative, in two respects. One: separation between the accusative and what is conjoined to it is forgiven, unlike separation between the genitive and what is conjoined to it. The second: the exegetes' interpretation is in the sense of the accusative." I say: he seems to mean what Abū ʿUbayda said. He said: "It is in the exegesis: 'Or do they think that We do not hear their secret and their private talk, and do not hear his saying, "O my Lord"'." Al-Zamakhsharī was satisfied with none of the earlier analyses, and only preferred that it be an oath in the three readings, and their verification has been given.

Abū Qilāba read «يا رَبَّ» with fatḥa on the bāʾ, on turning the yāʾ into an alif then omitting it, content with the fatḥa in place of it, as in:

4013 - . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... with "alas" and without "if only" . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .

and al-Akhfash makes it regular.

semin-durr:89-89.t: His saying: {فَسَوْفَ يَعْلَمُونَ}: Nāfiʿ and Ibn ʿĀmir read «تَعْلمون» in the second person as a shift (iltifāt), and the others in the third person, looking to what preceded.

ukberi-tibyan:1-2.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (حم (١) وَالْكِتَابِ الْمُبِينِ (٢)).
His saying (وَالْكِتَابِ): whoever makes «حم» an oath takes the wāw as a conjunction; and whoever says otherwise makes it the wāw of the oath.

ukberi-tibyan:17-17.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَإِذَا بُشِّرَ أَحَدُهُمْ بِمَا ضَرَبَ لِلرَّحْمَنِ مَثَلًا ظَلَّ وَجْهُهُ مُسْوَدًّا وَهُوَ كَظِيمٌ (١٧)).
His saying (وَجْهُهُ مُسْوَدًّا): the noun of ظَلَّ and its khabar (predicate). It is also possible that the noun of «ظَلَّ» is a latent pronoun (mustatir) referring to أَحَدُهُمْ, with وَجْهُهُ a badal (substitute) of it. Both are also read in the nominative (وَجْهُهُ مُسْوَدٌّ), as a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar in the position of the khabar of ظَلَّ. (وَهُوَ كَظِيمٌ) is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the noun of «ظَلَّ», or of the pronoun in «مُسْوَدًّا».
Allah the Exalted said: (أَوَمَنْ يُنَشَّأُ فِي الْحِلْيَةِ وَهُوَ فِي الْخِصَامِ غَيْرُ مُبِينٍ (١٨)).
His saying (أَوَمَنْ): «مَنْ» is in the position of the accusative, its implied wording being "do you then make one who is brought up…"; or in the position of the nominative, i.e. "is one who is brought up… a part [of Him] or a child?". And (فِي الْخِصَامِ) is attached (mutaʿalliq) to «مُبِينٍ». If you say: the muḍāf ilayhi (second term of a genitive construct) does not govern what precedes it?
It is answered: except with «غَيْرُ», because it contains the meaning of negation; so it is as though He said "and he does not make clear in disputation". Like it is the case in al-Kitāb [of Sībawayh]: أَنَا زَيْدًا غَيْرُ ضَارِبٍ ("I am not one to strike Zayd"). It is also said: [زَيْدًا] is accusative by a verb that ضَارِبٍ explains, and likewise in the verse.

ukberi-tibyan:24-24.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (قَالَ أَوَلَوْ جِئْتُكُمْ بِأَهْدَى مِمَّا وَجَدْتُمْ عَلَيْهِ آبَاءَكُمْ قَالُوا إِنَّا بِمَا أُرْسِلْتُمْ بِهِ كَافِرُونَ (٢٤)).
His saying (قُلْ أَوَلَوْ): in the form of the imperative, and it is resumptive. It is also read (قَالَ), meaning the warner mentioned [before].

ukberi-tibyan:26-26.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَإِذْ قَالَ إِبْرَاهِيمُ لِأَبِيهِ وَقَوْمِهِ إِنَّنِي بَرَاءٌ مِمَّا تَعْبُدُونَ (٢٦)).
His saying (بَرَاءٌ): with fatḥa on the bāʾ and a single hamza; it is a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the place of the active participle, in the sense of بَرِيءٌ ("free of"), and that has also been read.

ukberi-tibyan:3-5.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (إِنَّا جَعَلْنَاهُ قُرْآنًا عَرَبِيًّا لَعَلَّكُمْ تَعْقِلُونَ (٣) وَإِنَّهُ فِي أُمِّ الْكِتَابِ لَدَيْنَا لَعَلِيٌّ حَكِيمٌ (٤) أَفَنَضْرِبُ عَنْكُمُ الذِّكْرَ صَفْحًا أَنْ كُنْتُمْ قَوْمًا مُسْرِفِينَ (٥))
His saying (فِي أُمِّ الْكِتَابِ): it is attached (mutaʿalliq) to عَلِيٌّ, and the lām does not prevent that.
And (لَدَيْنَا) is a badal (substitute) of the preposition and its genitive noun. It may also be a ḥāl (circumstantial) of الْكِتَابِ, or of «أُمِّ». Neither of the two adverbial phrases can be the khabar (predicate), because the khabar must be «عَلِيٌّ» on account of the lām; but each of them may be a naʿt (adjective) of the khabar, which became a ḥāl by being placed before it.
And (صَفْحًا) is a maṣdar (verbal noun) from the meaning of نَضْرِبُ, because it has the sense of نَصْفَحُ ("We turn aside"); it may also be a ḥāl.
It was also read with ḍamma on the ṣād (صُفْحًا), and the more likely view is that it is a dialectal variant. And (أَنْ), with fatḥa on the hamza, means "because you were" (لِأَنْ كُنْتُمْ); and with kasra on it (إِنْ) it is conditional, and what precedes indicates the apodosis.

ukberi-tibyan:31-31.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَقَالُوا لَوْلَا نُزِّلَ هَذَا الْقُرْآنُ عَلَى رَجُلٍ مِنَ الْقَرْيَتَيْنِ عَظِيمٍ (٣١)).
His saying (عَلَى رَجُلٍ مِنَ الْقَرْيَتَيْنِ): i.e. from one of the two towns, Mecca and al-Ṭāʾif. It is also said: the implied wording is "upon one man of two men from the two towns".
It is also said: the man was one who lived in Mecca and al-Ṭāʾif and went back and forth between them, so he became as though he were one of the people of both.

ukberi-tibyan:33-33.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَلَوْلَا أَنْ يَكُونَ النَّاسُ أُمَّةً وَاحِدَةً لَجَعَلْنَا لِمَنْ يَكْفُرُ بِالرَّحْمَنِ لِبُيُوتِهِمْ سُقُفًا مِنْ فَضَّةٍ وَمَعَارِجَ عَلَيْهَا يَظْهَرُونَ (٣٣)).
His saying (لِبُيُوتِهِمْ): it is a badal (substitute) with the preposition repeated, i.e. "for the houses of whoever disbelieved".
السَّقْفُ (roof) is a singular with a plural meaning; and سُقُفًا, with ḍamma, is a plural, like رَهْنٌ and رُهُنٌ.

ukberi-tibyan:38-38.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (حَتَّى إِذَا جَاءَنَا قَالَ يَا لَيْتَ بَيْنِي وَبَيْنَكَ بُعْدَ الْمَشْرِقَيْنِ فَبِئْسَ الْقَرِينُ (٣٨)).
His saying (جَاءَنَا): in the singular, referring back to the wording of مَنْ; and in the dual (جَاءَانَا), referring back to the two towns [Translator's note: the text has «الْقَرْيَتَيْنِ» ("the two towns"), evidently for «الْقَرِينَيْنِ» ("the two companions"), as the following words show]: the disbeliever and his devil. And (الْمَشْرِقَيْنِ): it is said that He meant the east and the west, giving one the dominant role (taghlīb), as in الْقَمَرَيْنِ ("the two moons", i.e. the sun and the moon).

ukberi-tibyan:39-39.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَلَنْ يَنْفَعَكُمُ الْيَوْمَ إِذْ ظَلَمْتُمْ أَنَّكُمْ فِي الْعَذَابِ مُشْتَرِكُونَ (٣٩)).
His saying (وَلَنْ يَنْفَعَكُمُ): there are two views on the fāʿil (agent). The first: «أَنَّكُمْ» and what it governs, i.e. "your consoling one another in the punishment will not benefit you".
The second: that it is the pronoun of the wishing (al-tamannī) indicated by His saying (يَالَيْتَ بَيْنِي وَبَيْنَكَ), i.e. "wishing for distance will not benefit you"; on this view «أَنَّكُمْ» means "because you…" (لِأَنَّكُمْ).
As for (إِذْ), its matter is problematic, because it is an adverb of past time, whereas لَنْ يَنْفَعَكُمْ, its agent, and the day mentioned are not past.
Ibn Jinnī said, in his questioning of Abū ʿAlī: "I went back to him about it many times, and the last thing I obtained from him was that this world and the next are connected, and they are the same in the judgement and knowledge of Allah the Exalted; so «إِذْ» is a badal (substitute) of الْيَوْمَ, so that it is as though it were future, or as though the day were past." Another said: the speech is construed according to the meaning, and the meaning is that the establishment of their wrongdoing in their own eyes will take place on the Day of Resurrection; so it is as though He said "it will not benefit you today, when your wrongdoing has been confirmed to you"; so it is also a badal.
Others said: the implied wording is "after you did wrong" (بَعْدَ إِذْ ظَلَمْتُمْ), and the muḍāf was omitted because it is understood.
It is also said: إِذْ has the sense of أَنْ, i.e. "because you did wrong". It is also read «إِنَّكُمْ فِي الْعَذَابِ», with kasra on the hamza, as resumptive; and this is on the view that the agent is the wishing.
On this view it is also possible that the agent is "your wrongdoing" or "your denial", indicated by ظَلَمْتُمْ; and the agent omitted from the wording is then what governs إِذْ, not the pronoun of the agent.

ukberi-tibyan:52-53.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (أَمْ أَنَا خَيْرٌ مِنْ هَذَا الَّذِي هُوَ مَهِينٌ وَلَا يَكَادُ يُبِينُ (٥٢) فَلَوْلَا أُلْقِيَ عَلَيْهِ أَسْوِرَةٌ مِنْ ذَهَبٍ أَوْ جَاءَ مَعَهُ الْمَلَائِكَةُ مُقْتَرِنِينَ (٥٣)).
His saying (أَمْ أَنَا خَيْرٌ): «أَمْ» here is disconnected (munqaṭiʿa) in wording, because a clause occurs after it; but in meaning it is connected and correlative (muttaṣila muʿādila), since the meaning is "Am I better than him or not?", or "Which of us is better?".
And (أَسْوِرَةٌ) is the plural of سِوَارٌ (bracelet). As for أَسَاوِرَةٌ, it is the plural of إِسْوَارٌ, or the plural of أَسْوِرَةٌ, a plural of a plural; its original form is أَسَاوِيرُ, and the yāʾ was made a compensation for the tāʾ [Translator's note: so in the text; the usual statement is that the tāʾ of أَسَاوِرَةٌ compensates for the yāʾ of أَسَاوِيرُ].

ukberi-tibyan:56-56.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (فَجَعَلْنَاهُمْ سَلَفًا وَمَثَلًا لِلْآخِرِينَ (٥٦)).
As for «سَلَفًا», it is a singular with a plural meaning, like النَّاسُ and الرَّهْطُ.
As for سُلُفًا, with two ḍammas, it is a plural like أَسَدٌ and أُسُدٌ; or the plural of سَالِفٌ, like صَابِرٌ and صُبُرٌ; or the plural of سَلِيفٌ, like رَغِيفٌ and رُغُفٌ. As for سُلَفًا, with ḍamma on the sīn and fatḥa on the lām, it is said: the ḍamma was replaced with a fatḥa for lightness.
It is also said: it is the plural of سُلْفَةٌ, like غُرْفَةٌ and غُرَفٌ.

ukberi-tibyan:57-57.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَلَمَّا ضُرِبَ ابْنُ مَرْيَمَ مَثَلًا إِذَا قَوْمُكَ مِنْهُ يَصِدُّونَ (٥٧)).
His saying (مَثَلًا): it is the second object of ضُرِبَ, i.e. "he was made an example". It is also said: it is a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. he was mentioned as one used for comparison. And (يَصِدُّونَ), with ḍamma on the ṣād (يَصُدُّونَ), means "they turn away"; and with kasra on it, it is a dialectal variant of it.
It is also said: [the form with] kasra means "they clamour".

ukberi-tibyan:6-8.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَكَمْ أَرْسَلْنَا مِنْ نَبِيٍّ فِي الْأَوَّلِينَ (٦) وَمَا يَأْتِيهِمْ مِنْ نَبِيٍّ إِلَّا كَانُوا بِهِ يَسْتَهْزِئُونَ (٧) فَأَهْلَكْنَا أَشَدَّ مِنْهُمْ بَطْشًا وَمَضَى مَثَلُ الْأَوَّلِينَ (٨)).
(وَكَمْ) is accusative by «أَرْسَلْنَا», and (بَطْشًا) is a tamyīz (specification). It is also said: it is a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the agent, i.e. "We destroyed them, [We] being violent in assault" (أَهْلَكْنَاهُمْ بَاطِشِينَ).

ukberi-tibyan:60-60.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَلَوْ نَشَاءُ لَجَعَلْنَا مِنْكُمْ مَلَائِكَةً فِي الْأَرْضِ يَخْلُفُونَ (٦٠)).
His saying (لَجَعَلْنَا مِنْكُمْ): i.e. "in place of you".
It is also said: the meaning is "We would have turned some of you into angels".

ukberi-tibyan:66-66.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (هَلْ يَنْظُرُونَ إِلَّا السَّاعَةَ أَنْ تَأْتِيَهُمْ بَغْتَةً وَهُمْ لَا يَشْعُرُونَ (٦٦)).
His saying {أَن تأتيهم}: it is a badal (substitute) of السَّاعَةَ — a substitute of inclusion (badal al-ishtimāl).

ukberi-tibyan:71-71.t:
Allah the Exalted said: {يُطَاف عَلَيْهِم بصحاف من ذهب وأكواب}
His saying (يُطَافُ): the implied wording of the speech is "they enter, and then [the vessels] are passed around"; it was omitted because the meaning is understood.

ukberi-tibyan:75-75.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (لَا يُفَتَّرُ عَنْهُمْ وَهُمْ فِيهِ مُبْلِسُونَ (٧٥)).
His saying (لَا يُفَتَّرُ عَنْهُمْ): it is a ḥāl (circumstantial), or a second khabar (predicate); and both are tawkīd (emphasis).

ukberi-tibyan:77-77.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَنَادَوْا يَا مَالِكُ لْيَقْضِ عَلَيْنَا رَبُّكَ قَالَ إِنَّكُمْ مَاكِثُونَ (٧٧)).
His saying (يَامَالِكُ): it is read «يَا مَالِ», with kasra and with ḍamma, by way of vocative truncation (tarkhīm).

ukberi-tibyan:81-81.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (قُلْ إِنْ كَانَ لِلرَّحْمَنِ وَلَدٌ فَأَنَا أَوَّلُ الْعَابِدِينَ (٨١)).
His saying (إِنْ كَانَ لِلرَّحْمَنِ وَلَدٌ): «إِنْ» has the sense of «مَا» (negation).
It is also said: it is conditional, i.e. "if you say that, then I am the first to affirm His oneness".
It is also said: "if that were true, I would be the first of those who disdain to worship him" — and that will never be true.

ukberi-tibyan:84-84.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَهُوَ الَّذِي فِي السَّمَاءِ إِلَهٌ وَفِي الْأَرْضِ إِلَهٌ وَهُوَ الْحَكِيمُ الْعَلِيمُ (٨٤)).
His saying (وَهُوَ الَّذِي فِي السَّمَاءِ إِلَهٌ): the ṣila (relative clause) of «الَّذِي» can only be a clause, and the implied wording here is "and He is the One who is God in the heaven". «فِي» is attached (mutaʿalliq) to إِلَهٌ, i.e. "worshipped in the heaven and worshipped in the earth". It is not sound to make «إِلَهٌ» a mubtadaʾ (subject) and فِي السَّمَاءِ its khabar (predicate), because then no referring pronoun would remain for الَّذِي; it would be like your saying هُوَ الَّذِي فِي الدَّارِ زَيْدٌ ("He is the one who — in the house is Zayd"). The same holds if you make إِلَهٌ nominative by the adverbial phrase. If you place in the adverbial phrase a pronoun referring to الَّذِي and make إِلَهٌ a badal (substitute) of it, that is permissible, though weak, because the overall purpose is to affirm His divinity, not His being in the heavens and the earth. It would also be unsound from another angle, namely His saying «وَفِي الْأَرْضِ إِلَهٌ»: for it is conjoined to what precedes it, and if you do not assume what we have mentioned, it becomes cut off from it, and the meaning would be "in the earth there is a god".

ukberi-tibyan:88-88.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَقِيلِهِ يَا رَبِّ إِنَّ هَؤُلَاءِ قَوْمٌ لَا يُؤْمِنُونَ (٨٨)).
His saying (وَقِيلِهِ): in the accusative (وَقِيلَهُ), and there are several views on it. The first: that it is conjoined to «سِرَّهُمْ», i.e. "He knows their secret and his saying".
The second: that it is conjoined to the position of السَّاعَةِ, i.e. "and with Him is [the knowledge] that He knows the Hour, and his saying". The third: that it is accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. "and he said his saying".
It is also read in the nominative (وَقِيلُهُ) as a mubtadaʾ (subject), with «يَا رَبِّ» as its khabar (predicate). It is also said: the implied wording is "and his saying is the saying 'O Lord'". It is also said: the khabar is omitted, i.e. "his saying 'O Lord' is heard", or "is answered".
It was also read in the genitive (وَقِيلِهِ), conjoined to the wording of السَّاعَةِ. It is also said: it is an oath. And Allah knows best.

zajjaj:38-38.t:
And His saying: ﴿يا لَيْتَ بَيْنِي وبَيْنَكَ بُعْدَ المَشْرِقَيْنِ فَبِئْسَ القَرِينُ﴾. It is also read "جاءانا" (the two of them came to Us). Whoever reads "جاءانا", the meaning is: "until, when the disbeliever and his devil came…"; and whoever reads "حَتّى إذا جاءَنا" (until, when he came to Us), it refers to the disbeliever alone. ﴿قالَ يا لَيْتَ بَيْنِي وبَيْنَكَ بُعْدَ المَشْرِقَيْنِ فَبِئْسَ القَرِينُ﴾: the meaning of "اَلْمَشْرِقَيْنِ" (the two easts) here is the distance between the east and the west; when they were made a pair, the word "east" prevailed (taghlīb), as the poet said:
لَنا قَمَراها والنُّجُومُ الطَّوالِعُ
(Ours are its two moons and the rising stars.)
He means the sun and the moon; and as they said: "سُنَّةُ العُمَرَيْنِ" (the practice of the two ʿUmars), meaning the practice of Abū Bakr and ʿUmar, may Allah have mercy on them both.

zajjaj:39-39.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلَنْ يَنْفَعَكُمُ اليَوْمَ إذْ ظَلَمْتُمْ أنَّكم في العَذابِ مُشْتَرِكُونَ﴾: the meaning is: "Sharing in the punishment will not benefit you." Muḥammad ibn Yazīd [al-Mubarrad] said, in answer concerning this verse: They were denied the relief of consolation (al-taʾassī), because consolation makes calamity easier to bear; so they were informed that sharing in the punishment would not benefit them, and that Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, would place no consolation in it. He said: And he recited to me on this meaning, by al-Khansāʾ:
وَلَوْلا كَثْرَةُ الباكِينَ حَوْلِي ∗∗∗ عَلى إخْوانِهِمْ لَقَتَلْتُ نَفْسِي
(Were it not for the many around me weeping over their brothers, I would have killed myself.)

وَما يَبْكُونَ مِثْلَ أخِي ولَكِنْ ∗∗∗ أُعَزِّي النَّفْسَ عَنْهُ بِالتَّأسِّي
(They do not weep for one like my brother, but I console my soul over him by taking comfort in others' grief.)

zajjaj:41-41.t: And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَإمّا نَذْهَبَنَّ بِكَ فَإنّا مِنهم مُنْتَقِمُونَ﴾ ﴿أوْ نُرِيَنَّكَ﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 42]: "ما" entered as an emphasis (tawkīd) of the condition, and the heavy nūn in His saying ﴿نَذْهَبَنَّ﴾ also entered as emphasis. When "ما" enters, the nūn enters with it, just as it enters together with the lām of the oath. The meaning is: "We shall take vengeance on them if you are taken in death, or We shall show you what We promised them, and what We promised you concerning them, of victory." And Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, did indeed show him what He promised him concerning them, and what He promised them, of their destruction if they denied.
